title: How Gambian women are restoring the mangroves protecting Banjul
excerpt:
Banjul, The Gambia – At dawn, before the heat settles over the coast, Fatou Jarjue waits for the tide to retreat.

She pulls on her gloves and socks, steps into the muddy edge of the Tanbi Wetland and...
body_text:
Banjul, The Gambia – At dawn, before the heat settles over the coast, Fatou Jarjue waits for the tide to retreat.

She pulls on her gloves and socks, steps into the muddy edge of the Tanbi Wetland and pushes her wooden canoe through narrow channels surrounded by tangled mangrove roots. Inside the canoe sit empty pans waiting to be filled, not with oysters today, but with crabs hiding beneath the surface.

The life of this mother of one is inseparable from the wetland she navigates each day. The mangroves – salt-tolerant coastal trees that protect shorelines from erosion and flooding – provide the oysters, crabs and fish that sustain her family’s livelihood while serving as a natural barrier against erosion and flooding for her coastal community.

Her brother, Musa, trails behind in a smaller canoe whenever he can, keeping watch as she moves deeper into the mangrove channels. On days when he is busy elsewhere, Jarjue ventures into the wetland alone.

For generations, women around the Tanbi Wetland have depended on these waters for survival. Jarjue still does. But unlike previous generations, she also spends part of her time restoring the ecosystem that has sustained her family for decades.

Only months earlier, these waterways were filled with women collecting oysters attached to mangrove roots. With the arrival of The Gambia’s rainy season, oyster harvesting pauses, forcing many women to turn to crabs and fishing until the shellfish season reopens.

For the 34-year-old, the change in her daily catch is temporary. Her commitment to restoring the mangroves is not.

“I have restored more than 5,000 mangroves since last year,” she told Al Jazeera.

Jarjue grew up in Ndangan, a small settlement of about 300 people located roughly 2km (1.2 miles)  from Banjul, the capital of The Gambia. Like many children in the community, she grew up with the rhythms of the wetland.

At just 12 years old, she began following her mother into the mangroves, learning how to harvest oysters and catch crabs and fish.

The forest was both a classroom and a source of income.

Over the years, Jarjue watched the environment around her change. Rising seas, coastal erosion and changing weather patterns began threatening the coastline her community depends on.

Instead of only taking from the wetland, she decided to help rebuild it.

Today, she returns regularly not only to harvest but also to inspect young seedlings, replace damaged plants and monitor areas where restoration is needed.

“The mangroves are part of our lives,” she said.

For Jarjue, conservation is not separate from survival. The healthier the mangroves become, the stronger the future of her community.

As Jarjue paddles deeper into the wetland, oysters cling to the roots of the mangroves. They are large, growing and ready for harvest in another season. She leaves them untouched.

She points towards them proudly, knowing that protecting them now will mean a better harvest later.

Although crab harvesting provides income during the rainy season, oysters remain the more profitable catch. A milk-can measure of oysters sells for about 100 dalasis ($1.34), and demand at local markets is higher.

“Oysters are difficult to harvest,” Jarjue explained. “But that is where the money is.”

The annual closure of oyster harvesting during the rainy season is sometimes misunderstood as a warning that oysters become poisonous at that time of year.

But marine scientist Dawda Saine says the reason is more complex and is rooted in conservation, ecology and food safety.

The closure forms part of The Gambia’s Oyster and Cockle Co-management Plan, which allows oyster stocks time to regenerate, reproduce and grow while reducing pressure on the resource.

“We don’t close the season because oysters are poisonous,” Saine told Al Jazeera. “We close it to protect the resource and because, during the rains, oysters filter everything in the water, including increased run-off, which can affect their quality, taste and safety.”

During the rainy season, increased run-off can carry waste and other materials into waterways where oysters feed by filtering water. Allowing them to remain undisturbed helps protect both the ecosystem and consumers.

For women like Jarjue, respecting the closure is an investment in the future.

Jarjue is among several women in Ndangan who have become guardians of the ecosystem they depend on.

For 48-year-old Sussan Colley, the difference is visible every time she enters the wetland.

Colley has harvested oysters, fished and collected crabs since she was a teenager. She remembers when declining mangrove cover began affecting the community’s catches.

There were fewer oysters. Harvests became smaller. Families who depended on the wetland faced increasing uncertainty.

As restoration efforts expanded, Colley began noticing changes beneath the roots.

The oysters returned. They grew faster and larger. The wetland became productive again.

“The mangroves are changing our lives for the better,” she told Al Jazeera.

For Colley, restoration is also about preparing the next generation. She is teaching her children the skills she inherited from her parents while passing on another lesson: People must protect the natural systems that sustain them.

“I want them to make a livelihood from this,” she said, “but also understand the importance of the mangroves and the role they play in our lives.”

Jarjue and other women received training in mangrove restoration through a local conservation initiative supporting coastal communities in The Gambia. The programme equipped them with the skills to restore degraded mangroves, protect the ecosystems that support fisheries and strengthen their communities’ resilience to climate change.

For the women of Ndangan, the training changed how they viewed the forest, not only as a place to harvest, but also as something they have a responsibility to protect.

The work happening in Ndangan carries significance far beyond the settlement.

Banjul, The Gambia’s capital, is a low-lying island city facing growing threats from rising seas, coastal erosion and flooding. Experts have warned that a 1-metre (3ft-4-inch) rise in global sea levels could inundate parts of the city, increasing the urgency of protecting its remaining natural barriers.

The threat is not only a future concern. In 2022, severe flooding affected thousands of people across The Gambia, exposing the vulnerability of communities living along the coast.

For settlements surrounding the Tanbi Wetland, mangroves are more than an environmental resource. They are a natural defence system.

Rohey Malick Lowe, the mayor of Banjul, says the future of the capital is closely tied to the survival of its mangroves.

“Banjul is an island,” she told Al Jazeera. “If the mangroves disappear, it goes with the city.”

The mayor said the Banjul City Council is working to protect the capital from climate threats but acknowledged that challenges remain, including the degradation of parts of the wetland through human activities.

Supporting women like Jarjue, she said, is not just about protecting their incomes but also strengthening the city’s resilience.

“They are not only protecting their livelihoods,” Lowe said. “They are helping to protect Banjul.”

Despite their contribution, women in Ndangan still face challenges. Without reliable electricity, preserving oysters and crabs remains difficult, especially when market demand is low and harvests cannot be sold immediately.

But each day, Jarjue returns to the mangroves.

Sometimes she goes to harvest. Other times, she goes simply to check whether the trees she planted are surviving.

The work is slow. A mangrove seedling does not transform a coastline overnight. But for Jarjue, every new root represents a future she is helping build.

As the tide slowly rises, she guides her canoe back towards shore, leaving behind thousands of young mangroves she helped plant.

Months from now, she will return to harvest oysters from the same roots she is protecting today. Until then, she is content watching the forest grow.

Every new seedling is a quiet act of hope, not only for her family, but also for a city increasingly vulnerable to the rising sea.

Jarjue pauses before stepping onto dry land and looks back at the green canopy stretching across the wetland.

“Every morning I wake up and see the mangroves growing,” she said. “That gives me peace. If the mangroves disappear one day, our lives will disappear with them.”

title: Meta says AI model accessed the internet and hacked another firm
excerpt: Facebook owner Meta says an issue during an evaluation by an independent testing company allowed one of its artificial intelligence (AI) models to connect to the internet and hack another organisation...
body_text:
Facebook owner Meta says an issue during an evaluation by an independent testing company allowed one of its artificial intelligence (AI) models to connect to the internet and hack another organisation's system.

The announcement follows recent incidents across the AI industry, including breaches by OpenAI and Anthropic models, that have raised cyber-security concerns.

A Meta spokesperson told the BBC that it was investigating the hack that was caused by a "misconfiguration", which it described as similar to previously reported incidents at other firms.

The incidents have prompted researchers and governments to call for tougher safeguards and more rigorous testing.

Meta said the security trials were conducted by Irregular, the same AI security vendor that carried out tests for Anthropic's AI model that had gained access to three other companies' systems.

An Irregular spokesperson said the Meta incident "is the exact same evaluation-environment issue that was already disclosed by Anthropic last week."

Irregular is working on a report on how to securely run cyber-security tests involving AI agents, the firm's spokesperson told the BBC.

Meta also said it will publish more information on the incident "once we have all the facts."

In the past two weeks, AI leaders OpenAI and Anthropic have also reported incidents in which their models hacked into other organisation's systems during testing.

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said in a series of announcements that its agents attacked several publicly available services, including AI tools hub Hugging Face.

OpenAI's disclosure prompted rival Anthropic to conduct its own checks, leading to the discovery that its Claude AI model had carried out similar attacks on several firms after a "misconfiguration" gave it access to the internet.

Meta shares fall as frustration grows over AI spending plans

AI or real? BBC analyses viral China disaster videos

Some commentators have questioned the timing of disclosures about the incidents as tech firms wrestle for dominance in AI development.

OpenAI and Anthropic are preparing blockbuster stock market listings that are expected to value each firm at around $1tn (£740bn).

This week, the UK's AI Security Institute (AISI) said that its testing had found that some models tried to carry out cyber-attacks by creating fake human profiles to try and trick people.

In the most serious case, the AISI said Anthropic's Mythos AI tried to gain access to a service by sending private messages using fake accounts mimicking real people.

Anthropic said AISI's tests were not "representative of any of our production models". OpenAI, whose models were also tested, said AISI's evaluations did not reflect ordinary use.

title: Colombia minister warns of ‘terrorism’ threat at presidential inauguration
excerpt:
Colombia’s outgoing defence minister has warned of a heightened risk of “terrorism” ahead of Friday’s inauguration of President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella.

Minister of Defence Pedro Sanchez told ...
body_text:
Colombia’s outgoing defence minister has warned of a heightened risk of “terrorism” ahead of Friday’s inauguration of President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella.

Minister of Defence Pedro Sanchez told radio station La FM on Wednesday that authorities were tracking a “threat” against Friday’s proceedings. “Most likely, these criminals would attempt to disrupt this democratic event with acts of terrorism,” he said.

The handover of the presidency will take place in the region of Cali in Colombia’s southwest, which has recently seen a series of militia attacks.

De la Espriella, 48, who narrowly won the June presidential run-off, had asked Congress to move the event from the capital, Bogota, to the country’s third-largest city despite its proximity to areas under the control of rebel groups.

Several foreign leaders, including the presidents of Argentina, Paraguay, Chile and Ecuador, along with Spain’s King Felipe VI, are expected to attend the inauguration ceremony.

To secure the event, Colombia’s military is deploying roughly 11,000 troops and has imposed a no-fly zone on drones over Cali and its surroundings. Rebel fighters have previously used drones to drop explosives.

In the department of Cauca, near Cali, a dissident faction of the FARC armed group operates under the command of Ivan Mordisco, the alias of Colombia’s most wanted rebel leader.

The hard-right de la Espriella campaigned on dismantling outgoing President Gustavo Petro’s “Total Peace” negotiation strategy with armed groups.

Petro has disputed the election result and said he will not attend Friday’s ceremony.

title: Trump blasts Democratic socialist candidate as 'full of s---' and Dems are skipping socialism 'for communism'
excerpt:
President Donald Trump blasted democratic socialist Abdul El-Sayed while warning that Democrats are skipping socialism and embracing communism during remarks Wednesday in Las Vegas, Nevada.

President...
body_text:
President Donald Trump blasted democratic socialist Abdul El-Sayed while warning that Democrats are skipping socialism and embracing communism during remarks Wednesday in Las Vegas, Nevada.

President Donald Trump escalated his attacks on Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed Wednesday, singling out the progressive candidate as "full of s---" while arguing Democrats are embracing communism.

The remarks came hours after El-Sayed narrowly defeated Rep. Haley Stevens in Michigan's Democrat Senate primary, winning by less than one percentage point after The Associated Press called the race early Wednesday.

He will face Republican Mike Rogers in November for the Senate seat being vacated by retiring Sen. Gary Peters.

Trump devoted several minutes of his Las Vegas speech to attacking democratic socialist candidates, arguing they are advancing communist ideas and calling communism "the greatest threat" facing the United States.

SOCIALIST SURGE: FAR-LEFT DEMOCRATS TEST NATIONAL PLAYBOOK AFTER BLUE-CITY PRIMARY SHOCKS

President Donald Trump speaks during an event in Las Vegas on Wednesday. (Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"These people are dangerous and frankly, they are lunatics. They're crazy, and we can't let them get into office," Trump said. "Communism is the greatest threat to our country in its history, including even World War One, World War Two, Pearl Harbor, 9/11. I think it's the greatest threat."

The White House later amplified that portion of Trump's remarks on social media, posting simply: "Communism is the greatest threat to our country."

Trump mocked what he said communist policies would mean for Americans.

"Would you like a free house? We'll take one from your neighbor. Would you like free rent? We'll take it from whoever. We'll take your building away from the landlord," Trump said. "What they don't say, and what Republicans should say, is that at the end of the year, you'll have nothing but death, squalor, poverty. You'll have a life of hell."

LIZ PEEK: MICHIGAN CAN STOP THE SOCIALIST FEVER RAGE — OR WATCH IT SWALLOW THE SENATE

FILE - U.S. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate primary candidate Abdul El-Sayed and U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt, greet the crowd after El-Sayed spoke at The People V. The Powerful rally at the Detroit Opera House on July 18, 2026 in Detroit, Mich. He was recently endorsed by Michigan Democratic Sen. Tina Smith. (Sarah Rice/Getty Images, File)

The president pointed to Venezuela as an example of what he said happens when communist policies take hold.

"Look at Venezuela, where it was such a rich country 20 years ago," Trump said. "Every time this has happened, you go through squalor ... filth, crime, death, destruction, embarrassment. You lose your home. You lose your apartment."

Trump then singled out El-Sayed by name, drawing one of the loudest reactions of the night.

"When I watch Abdul, he's full of s---," Trump said.

2026 MIDTERMS STATE OF PLAY: KEY RACES UNFOLD AS STEVENS, EL-SAYED BATTLE IN MICHIGAN

Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive candidate in the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate in Michigan, films a social media video at a pool party for content creators supporting his campaign, Monday, in Detroit. (AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson)

El-Sayed's victory gives Democrats a progressive nominee in one of the country's most closely watched Senate races. Backed by Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., El-Sayed campaigned on Medicare for All, getting money out of politics and ending U.S. military aid to Israel.

He has described himself as a capitalist and has distanced himself from the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), though Republicans have frequently tied him to the broader democratic socialist movement.

Trump later returned to a familiar theme from the second term of his presidency.

"If you remember, during my State of the Union speech, I made a very strong statement. I said that America will never be a socialist country," Trump said. "I was right."

The president argued Democrats now want to move beyond socialism.

TRUMP HAILS AMERICA AS 'MOST EXCEPTIONAL NATION EVER TO EXIST' IN MOUNT RUSHMORE SPEECH

President Donald Trump introduces a family who has benefited from the "no tax on tips" policy during an event at Red Rock Casino Resort and Spa in Las Vegas on Wednesday. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

"What I didn't say is what they're trying to do. They want to skip socialism. They want to go right down to the bottom of the barrel. That's communism," Trump said. "They want it to be a communist country. We're not letting them have it as a communist country, not even for a minute."

Trump closed by vowing to defeat what he called the Democrat Party's leftward movement.

"Together we will defeat communism, socialism and Marxism in America once and for all," Trump said. "It's defeated. It's going to go down. It always goes down."The White House and El-Sayed's campaign did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.Fox News Digital's Andrew Mark Miller, Kiera McDonald, and Robert Schmad contributed to this reporting.

Jasmine Baehr is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital, where she covers politics, the military, legal debates surrounding life and family policy, as well as faith and culture.

title: Nato to ‘urgently’ get air defences for Ukraine, as Zelenskyy warns of surge in Russian missile production
excerpt:
After Ukraine failed to shoot down a single ballistic missile fired by Russia on Wednesday, the president urged allies to increase supplies of Patriot interceptors

Nato is working to get Ukraine the ...
body_text:
After Ukraine failed to shoot down a single ballistic missile fired by Russia on Wednesday, the president urged allies to increase supplies of Patriot interceptors

Nato is working to get Ukraine the air defences it “urgently needs”, its secretary general has said, after Kyiv failed to shoot down a single Russian missile in an attack on Wednesday, and as Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Moscow was seeking to significantly boost missile ⁠production ahead of winter.

Speaking at a National Security and Defense Council meeting on winter resilience, the Ukrainian president did not rule out the idea that stalling missile supplies from western allies were “aimed at making Ukraine, so to speak, more willing to compromise” in peace talks with Russia.

After meeting Nato’s Mark Rutte, Zelenskyy said: “It is important to cut through all red tape and make the necessary political decisions. Literally every day, people’s lives here in Ukraine depend on the resolve of our partners in Europe and the United States.”

Russia launched 24 ballistic missiles in an overnight attack on Wednesday, killing at least 17 people. Preliminary data from the Ukrainian air force showed its defences shot down 98 of the 115 drones fired by Russia overnight, but none of the ballistic missiles.

On Wednesday, Zelenskyy said that in the first half of 2026, supplies of air defence missiles from Ukraine’s allies had fallen to a third of their 2025 level.

The president also warned that Moscow was looking to significantly increase ballistic missile ⁠production as winter neared, when it is expected to renew its campaign against Ukraine’s energy sector.

Serhii Beskrestnov, an adviser to Ukraine’s president on the development of defence technology, estimated that Russia was capable of launching 100 ballistic missiles every month to attack logistic ​hubs, industrial facilities, food stores and warehouses. “The war of attrition has entered its next phase,” he said on the Telegram app.

Ukraine has been short on US-made Patriot interceptors capable of downing Russian ballistic missiles since the ⁠start of the war. But in recent weeks, an acute shortage has come into focus, with Moscow pummelling Kyiv, on ​average, every three days in July alone. Zelenskyy said the shortage of interceptor missiles was mainly caused by the war in the Middle East.

Patriot missile systems are the only system in Ukrainian service able to intercept the Russian Iskander-M, S-400 and Zircon missiles, according to the Ukrainian air force.

Russia often combines ballistic missiles with cruise missiles, drones and decoys, forcing defenders to track many threats and ration scarce interceptors, but Ukraine says it has too few batteries and interceptors to properly protect itself.

The interceptor shortage has become more acute as a result of the US-Israel war on Iran, which has consumed large numbers of Patriot and other interceptors. An analysis by the Associated Press estimated that the US Patriot inventory had fallen by at least 65% since before the war. The Pentagon claims it retains a deep arsenal of supplies.

Production cannot immediately close the gap. Lockheed Martin delivered more than 600 of the newest model of interceptors in 2025 and is working toward annual capacity of 2,000 by the end of 2030. But according to some estimates, Gulf states collectively fired more than 1,100 interceptors in the first three months of the Iran war.

Nato says Europe’s first Patriot missile production facility is expected to open in September in Germany.

Political signals from Washington have also shifted. At a Nato summit last month, Donald Trump said the US would give Ukraine a licence to produce Patriots. About three weeks later, he said he had not made a final decision. Even with a licence, officials and experts estimate that starting production in Ukraine would take years.

Despite Trump casting doubt on the deal last month, the US is pressing ahead with talks on allowing Ukraine to make Patriot interceptors, according to reports from Reuters.

The discussions ⁠include an option for Ukraine to ⁠build some components for final assembly elsewhere in ​Europe, according to the report.

title: Crowded Russian beach descends into chaos after alleged Ukrainian drone incident kills 7, including 4 children
excerpt: Video captured the moment a projectile struck a crowded beach in Russia's Black Sea resort town of Arkhipo-Osipovka, killing seven people, including four children, and injuring dozens. (Social Media v...
body_text:
Video captured the moment a projectile struck a crowded beach in Russia's Black Sea resort town of Arkhipo-Osipovka, killing seven people, including four children, and injuring dozens. (Social Media via Reuters)

Vacationers were sent scrambling for safety Monday after a projectile struck a crowded beach in a Russian Black Sea resort town, killing seven people, including four children, and injuring dozens more, officials said.

Video footage captured the incident in the village of Arkhipo-Osipovka near Gelendzhik, where the beach was packed with visitors at the time of the strike.

The Russian Mission in Geneva said in a post on X that the "bloody attack" was carried out by a drone launched by Ukraine, accusing Kyiv of targeting civilians.

UKRAINE LAUNCHES WHAT APPEARS TO BE ONE OF ITS LARGEST DRONE ATTACKS AGAINST RUSSIA: REPORT

A projectile flies overhead near Arkhipo-Osipovka, Russia, on Monday. (Social media via Reuters)

"The attack targeted civilian infrastructure. Emergency and special services are working at the crash site," regional Gov. Veniamin Kondratyev said in a post on Telegram.

"What happened today is a targeted attack by the Kyiv regime against civilians who have no connection to the military infrastructure. This cynical and inhumane terrorist attack against children cannot be justified."

UKRAINE UNLEASHES MORE THAN 400 DRONES NEAR MOSCOW IN ONE OF WAR'S BIGGEST ATTACKS

A fiery explosion rocks a Black Sea beach resort in Russia on Monday. (Social media via Reuters)

Andriy Kovalenko, an officer with Ukraine’s Defense Forces, disputed Russia’s account, saying the deaths were directly caused by Russian air defenses that intercepted a drone, sending debris onto the beach.

"Russian air defense shot down a drone over people lying on the beach," Kovalenko said on Telegram.

In the video, sounds resembling gunfire were heard just seconds before a drone struck the beach, causing a fireball explosion that sent bystanders screaming. As the gunfire was heard, the drone appeared to veer sharply before diving toward the beach.

Preliminary Russian reports also found that several of the deaths were caused by "falling drone debris," Kondratyev said.

ZELENSKYY SAYS PUTIN 'LOST THE INITIATIVE' AS UKRAINE'S TECH INDUSTRY RESHAPES THE WAR

In another Telegram post, Kovalenko indicated that Ukraine uses its weapons against Russian military-industrial infrastructure to affect Moscow’s ability to finance the war.

He further accused Russian President Vladimir Putin of creating an "illusion" that Russia would remain safe from the war by downplaying daily explosions as falling debris, limiting air raid warnings, and positioning air defenses near populated areas such as the Black Sea resort.

Smoke rises after a deadly blast along a Russian resort beach on Monday. (Social media via Reuters)

"Putin deliberately killed these people. Because if he had not started the war and struck Ukraine, they would be alive," Kovalenko said.

"It was Putin, his air defense, who killed these Russians. His decisions in response to their decisions launched a chain of death for Russians."

Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Florida man accused of cutting off diver's air supply in fight over coveted lobster diving spot
excerpt: A man wanted on a felony warrant spent about 90 minutes in the Pacific Ocean off Will Rogers State Beach before Los Angeles County lifeguards surrounded him and helped take him into custody. (Credit: ...
body_text:
A man wanted on a felony warrant spent about 90 minutes in the Pacific Ocean off Will Rogers State Beach before Los Angeles County lifeguards surrounded him and helped take him into custody. (Credit: FOX 11 Los Angeles)

A battle over a lobster diving spot off the Florida coast allegedly escalated into an underwater nightmare after a man was accused of shutting off another diver's air supply, a confrontation that landed him behind bars on an attempted murder charge.

Michael Joseph Simpson, 51, surrendered Tuesday to the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center in Miami-Dade County, where he was booked Tuesday evening on an attempted murder charge, according to Miami-Dade jail records. His bond was set at $10,000.

According to Local 10 News, the incident occurred shortly after 7 a.m. on July 29 about a half-mile east of Fisher Island during Florida's annual lobster mini season.

Citing the arrest affidavit, Law&Crime reported that Simpson allegedly approached another boat at a high rate of speed and circled the vessel several times before anchoring about 10 feet away.

FLORIDA MAN ARRESTED FOR DUI AFTER TROOPERS ALLEGEDLY FIND 34 OPEN ALCOHOL CONTAINERS IN VEHICLE

Michael Joseph Simpson's booking photo after his arrest on an attempted murder charge in Miami-Dade County, Fla. (Miami-Dade County Corrections and Rehabilitation)

Investigators say the confrontation began after Simpson claimed the group was diving in "his spot" and warned that a larger boat was on its way before it arrived and anchored nearby.

Authorities allege Simpson then threatened to turn off the surface-supplied air system providing oxygen to an 18-year-old diver searching for lobsters. Investigators say Simpson jumped into the water and intentionally shut off the unit.

As the confrontation unfolded, witnesses yelled, "We have a diver down there you a--hole!" according to the arrest affidavit cited by Law&Crime.

The diver's boat owner jumped into the water and pulled him to the surface. The diver was gasping for air and appeared disoriented but was not injured, Local 10 reported.

FLORIDA MAN GIVES AN INCREDIBLE INTERVIEW ABOUT HOW HE FOUGHT OFF AN ALLIGATOR WITH A FISHING POLE

Rodriguez was awaiting trial at the Miami-Dade Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center in Miami, Fla. on charges of cocaine possession with intent to sell, being a felon in possession of a firearm and ammunition and trespassing. (Google Maps)

Investigators allege Simpson left before deputies arrived. After authorities identified him as the suspect, Simpson voluntarily surrendered Tuesday, according to Local 10.

Simpson's attorney, Howard Srebnick, strongly denied the allegations in a statement to Fox News Digital, arguing investigators ignored evidence and witnesses he says support his client's account.

Srebnick said Simpson was diving from his own boat with friends and his two young children and "never disabled anyone's diving equipment."

Srebnick said video shows one of the accusers becoming entangled in the Brownie's Third Lung air system while Simpson "was nowhere near it."

AMERICAN TOURIST ATTACKED BY SHARK IN VACATION HOT SPOT

A tourist snorkels near the Christ of the Abyss statue surrounded by dead coral on the ocean bed in the Straits of Florida near Key Largo, Fla., Sept. 23, 2021. (Chandan Khanna/AFP via Getty Images)

He also disputed investigators' allegation that Simpson fled, saying his client instead idled his boat away from the immediate area to avoid escalating the confrontation before cooperating with responding Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission officers and providing a statement.

Srebnick said numerous eyewitnesses aboard two separate boats corroborated Simpson's version of events and criticized the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office for arresting his client before interviewing what he described as exculpatory witnesses.

"We are optimistic that the State Attorney's Office, after reviewing the video and interviewing all the eyewitnesses, will dismiss the charges, clear his name, and restore the reputation he has spent a lifetime building," Srebnick said.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office for additional comment.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Bodycam video shows Canadian woman allegedly giving false name before deputies discovered 12 fake IDs
excerpt: Body camera footage captured a traffic stop that led Florida deputies to discover 12 fraudulent driver’s licenses with the same woman’s photo but different names and birthdates. (Credit: X@ChadChronis...
body_text:
Body camera footage captured a traffic stop that led Florida deputies to discover 12 fraudulent driver’s licenses with the same woman’s photo but different names and birthdates. (Credit: X@ChadChronister)

Police body camera video shows the moments Florida deputies arrested a Canadian woman after she allegedly gave a false name during a traffic stop and investigators discovered 12 fraudulent identification cards in her vehicle.

Hillsborough County Sheriff Chad Chronister released the July 29 bodycam footage showing deputies stopping a vehicle in Tampa because its taillights and tag lights were not working.

The driver, Bryce Swanson, 28, initially identified herself as "Brianna Valenzuela" and initially told deputies she had a driver's license but did not have it with her, according to authorities.

SEMITRUCK DRIVER IN DEADLY INTERSTATE CRASH FRAUDULENTLY OBTAINED LICENSE, CITIZENSHIP: OFFICIALS

Body camera footage captured the traffic stop that led deputies to discover multiple allegedly fraudulent identification cards inside a vehicle in Tampa, Fla. (Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office)

"Swanson told deputies she did not have an ID and had never possessed a valid driver's license, after initially claiming she did," Chronister wrote on X. "A search of her vehicle revealed 12 driver's licenses with her picture, but different names and dates of birth."

According to authorities, Swanson is a Canadian national who overstayed her visa.

The body camera footage shows a deputy questioning Swanson about her identity after she said she was visiting Florida from New York in a rental vehicle.

"I live in New York," Swanson said. "I'm here in Florida literally just visiting friends and stuff right now."

VIRAL BODYCAM CAPTURES FLORIDA DEPUTY'S TRAFFIC STOP UNRAVEL AS HE ACCUSES ONE-HANDED DRIVER OF HOLDING PHONE

A Hillsborough County deputy speaks with Bryce Swanson during a traffic stop in Tampa, Fla. Investigators later said they discovered 12 fraudulent driver's licenses in her vehicle. (Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office)

The deputy pointed out she did not have any New York identification.

"Your story's not making a lot of sense to me, right?" the deputy said. "You say you live in New York, but you don't have any ID in New York."

When the deputy again asked how she could live in New York without any identification, Swanson replied, "I've never had a driver's license or anything like that."

Deputies then searched the vehicle and found what investigators described as numerous fraudulent identification cards.

MAN FLEEING ICE OFFICERS IN FLORIDA IS STRUCK AND KILLED BY TRACTOR-TRAILER, POLICE SAY

Body camera footage shows a Hillsborough County deputy questioning Bryce Swanson after she allegedly provided a false name during a traffic stop. (Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office)

"All these are fake," one deputy said in the video before placing Swanson under arrest.

Swanson was booked into the Orient Road Jail and charged with driving without a valid driver's license and providing a false name to a law enforcement officer.

She is being held without bond because of an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detainer, according to jail records.

Fox News Digital has reached out to ICE for comment.

Michael Sinkewicz is a writer for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to michael.sinkewicz@fox.com

title: Meta says its AI model hacked into another company during testing
excerpt:
Company is the third to report such an incident after Anthropic and OpenAI reported breaches during training

Meta said on Wednesday that one of its AI models hacked ⁠another company during cybersecur...
body_text:
Company is the third to report such an incident after Anthropic and OpenAI reported breaches during training

Meta said on Wednesday that one of its AI models hacked ⁠another company during cybersecurity testing, after an error by its testing partner gave the model unintended internet access.

The incident adds to a ⁠growing list of ⁠cases in ​which AI agents from major developers breached systems at other companies during testing, after Anthropic said last week that some of its models ⁠hacked three companies, and OpenAI disclosed that an AI agent breached the startup Hugging Face.

Meta said a misconfiguration by the independent testing company Irregular inadvertently allowed one ⁠of its models internet access during an evaluation, adding that it was investigating the incident.

The model “exploited ​a security vulnerability in a third-party service, ‌in a manner similar ‌to previously reported instances with other companies”, Meta said in a statement.

Earlier in the day, ‌The Information, citing sources, reported that Meta’s Muse Spark 1.1 model, which it has touted as its most capable model for real-world coding and agentic tasks, breached an unidentified company and altered its internal systems.

A spokesperson for Irregular told Reuters the incident was the “exact same evaluation-environment issue that was already disclosed by Anthropic last week” and that it did ‌not involve a “sandbox escape or a sophisticated cyber action”.

“There are no current open issues. Irregular is developing a white paper to share best ​practices for containment and securely running cyber evaluations,” Irregular said.

The incidents revealed by Meta and Anthropic were due to mistakes that inadvertently gave their models access to the open internet. That contrasts with OpenAI, whose AI agent independently exploited a novel vulnerability to reach the internet during cyber testing.

Even ⁠so, the breaches highlight how AI has increased threats to cybersecurity and ​how developers can struggle ​to keep the capabilities of their ​models contained.

The disclosures are likely to intensify a US government push to ​better manage AI security ‌risks at a ​time when Anthropic and ​OpenAI are racing to release more capable systems ahead of their planned public listings. Prominent leaders at these labs have called for a slowdown to address risks first.

title: Halle Berry sizzles in racy lingerie look for sunset beach stroll during Fiji getaway
excerpt:
Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Halle Berry is enjoying a tropical reset ahead of her 60th birthday.

The 59-year-old actress shared a series of Instagram photos fr...
body_text:
Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Halle Berry is enjoying a tropical reset ahead of her 60th birthday.

The 59-year-old actress shared a series of Instagram photos from a tropical getaway in Fiji, offering glimpses of quiet mornings, poolside relaxation and sunset walks along the beach.

Berry posed near the shoreline in an animal-print cover-up layered over a black lace lingerie bodysuit as the sun dipped toward the ocean. The flowing black-and-white wrap featured wide sleeves and tassel detailing, while her short, tousled hair blew across her face as she smiled for the camera.

KRISTIN CAVALLARI FLAUNTS HER TONED FIGURE IN BIKINIS DURING EUROPEAN SUMMER VACATION

Halle Berry shared sizzling photos from her Fiji vacation. (Stephanie Cardinale/Getty Images)

"The only bad thing about this trip is that each day must come to an end," she captioned the post.

A separate Instagram post captured the Academy Award winner in silhouette beneath sheer fabric draped around an outdoor daybed. Berry arched backward as the setting sun streamed through the material, with palm trees, an infinity pool and the ocean visible beyond the shaded retreat.

Halle Berry shared a peaceful sunset moment from her tropical getaway in Fiji. (Halle Berry/Instagram)

In a separate poolside image, the "Catwoman" star reclined along the edge of the water in a gold bikini. A wide-brimmed straw hat rested across her torso as she stretched one arm across the wooden deck and displayed several rings and stacked bracelets.

Halle Berry embraced the relaxed pace of island life during her Fiji vacation. (Halle Berry/Instagram)

Berry also shared an artful reflection photographed through a glass window. The layered image showed the actress appearing to relax inside a rounded bathtub while the surrounding ocean, palm trees and outdoor pool reflected across the glass.

GISELE BÜNDCHEN CELEBRATES BIRTHDAY IN LEOPARD-PRINT BIKINI AS SHE REFLECTS ON GRATITUDE

Berry is set to turn 60 on August 14. (Getty Images)

Halle Berry relaxed with an oceanfront soak during her Fiji getaway. (Halle Berry/Instagram)

The actress appeared to be enjoying the laid-back pace of the trip, joking in another caption, "We got drunk last night, and still drunk today 🤪."

Berry’s vacation comes as she prepares to celebrate her 60th birthday and continues challenging expectations about how women should approach aging.

During a July appearance on Hoda Kotb’s "Making Space" podcast, Berry said the milestone feels far different than she once imagined.

"I’m so happy to still be here, you know, when I was growing up and I thought of 60, it felt so old, you know, and now that I am 60, um, it doesn’t feel old at all," she said. "You know, I’m like, this is 60, well, that’s not so bad."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Halle Berry recently reflected on aging and embracing her next chapter ahead of her 60th birthday. (Mike Marsland/WireImage/Getty Images)

Berry said she currently feels more comfortable and confident in herself than she has in years.

"I feel really great actually, if I’m honest, I feel, I think, better than I have in a very, very long time," she said. "Um, I feel more of myself. I feel all of myself."

The Oscar winner explained that growing older has allowed her to stop worrying about satisfying everyone else’s expectations.

"You do stop managing everybody’s expectations," Berry told Kotb. "You do start to realize you’re usually the oldest person in the room. And so with that, you know, that carries some weight. You get to do what you wanna do."

'KNOTS LANDING' ICON DONNA MILLS JOINS ONLYFANS AT 85 TO CONNECT WITH FANS 'ON HER OWN TERMS’

She added, "You get to be who you wanna be, say what you want to say, you know, you’re no longer walking on eggshells, and that’s a really wonderful place to arrive."

Berry also pushed back against the idea that reaching a certain age should mean stepping away from her career permanently.

The actress said people have asked whether she intends to continue making movies before suggesting that she has already accomplished enough.

"Are you still going to keep working in movies?" Berry recalled being asked. "And I say, yeah, why should I not?"

She said others have questioned whether it is time for her to "quit all that and sit down somewhere and just be on a permanent vacation."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Berry rejected the assumption that women should withdraw from professional life as they grow older, arguing that meaningful work continues to provide purpose and connection.

"Why do I wanna, after I’ve worked my whole life so hard and it’s made me feel all of myself, it’s validated who I was, it’s, it’s given me a sense of purpose," she said. "Why should I now sit down and give that all away and then what?"

The actress said she encourages her 18-year-old daughter, Nahla, to pursue work she genuinely loves so that retirement never feels like the ultimate goal.

"Choose what you love so that you never feel like you want to retire, because working and being active and contributing is what keeps us young as we go down the path of life," Berry said.

She added, "It keeps us connected to life, to ourselves, to the others. You, you never want to stop doing that thing that you love so much."

Danielle Minnetian is an Entertainment Production Assistant for Fox News Digital covering celebrity news, entertainment trends and pop culture.

title: Meta’s AI model follows rivals in revealing hacks of outside systems
excerpt:
Meta has said that its AI model hacked another company during cybersecurity testing, following on from recent similar announcements by rival companies Anthropic and OpenAI.

Meta said on Wednesday tha...
body_text:
Meta has said that its AI model hacked another company during cybersecurity testing, following on from recent similar announcements by rival companies Anthropic and OpenAI.

Meta said on Wednesday that one of its AI models – reported to have been Muse Spark 1.1 – made changes to the unnamed hacked company’s internal systems after accessing the public internet because of an error in the setup of the “sandbox” testing environment by independent testing company Irregular.

A “sandbox” is an isolated internal virtual testing environment, which has no access to the internet.

Last week, Anthropic said that its Claude AI model hacked into the systems of three organisations during testing that was supposed to keep it isolated from the internet.

Anthropic said a misconfiguration had allowed Claude models to reach the internet. The company said it discovered the incidents after reviewing 141,006 test sessions.

The announcement came days after rival OpenAI first revealed that its models improperly accessed the internet and went rogue during security testing.

OpenAI and Anthropic have both released their most powerful models this year, known as Sol and Mythos, respectively.

The AI Security Institute (AISI), the UK’s AI watchdog, warned in a report released on Tuesday that OpenAI’s GPT-5.6-Sol and Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5 employed previously unseen levels of deception to carry out “sustained, potentially harmful activity” during a routine safety evaluation.

The New York Police Department (NYPD) are investigating the destruction of a Virgin Mary statue outside St. Rita Roman Catholic Church in Long Island City as a possible hate crime after a man climbed over a fence and repeatedly smashed it down using a hammer.

In surveillance video released by The Diocese of Brooklyn, the masked man is seen violently hitting the statue outside the church in what Catholic officials say is the latest in a string of attacks targeting the parish.

ANCIENT ESTATE TIED TO GROUP IN THE BIBLE UNEARTHED WITH 'FASCINATING' TREASURES IN ISRAEL

The Virgin Mary statue was vadalised outside St. Rita Roman Catholic Church in Long Island City (St. Rita’s Church)

According to the Diocese of Brooklyn, the incident happened at around 1:42 a.m. on Aug. 1.

WORLD-FAMOUS CATHOLIC SHRINE TORCHED, 'DEVIL IN A SKIRT' SCRAWLED ON VIRGIN MARY STATUE

The Diocese said in a statememt that the attack was the fourth vandalism incident at St. Rita Roman Catholic Church since 2024. (St. Rita Roman Catholic Church)

The video shows the man, who is wearing a dark T-shirt and shorts, climb over the fence into a courtyard where a statue of the Blessed Mother stood.

The suspect removes a hammer from his pocket and repeatedly strikes the statue before knocking it off its pedestal. He then climbs back over the fence and walks away.

The Diocese said in a statement that the attack was the fourth vandalism incident at St. Rita Roman Catholic Church since 2024.

WOMAN ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY BEHEADING JESUS STATUE OUTSIDE CATHOLIC CHURCH

Surveillance video released by the church shows a masked man, in a dark shirt and shorts, jumping over a fence into a courtyard where a statue of the Blessed Mother stood. (St. Rita’s Church.)

Past acts of vandalism in the parish include the destruction of a 60-year-old stained-glass window and graffiti that defaced a statue of St. Francis of Assisi and the sidewalk.

There was also damage done to a statue of St. Jude inside the church.

The Diocese of Brooklyn told Fox News Digital that no arrests have been made.

"This week, the NYPD also issued a crime stats update and hate crimes are up by 9.4% over the same 7-month period (Jan-July) of last year," John Quaglione, Deputy Press Secretary for the Roman Catholic Diocese of Brooklyn said.

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: FAA says Trump’s Marine One briefly flew too close to passenger jet
excerpt: US President Donald Trump’s military helicopter Marine One briefly flew too close to a passenger jet taking off from Washington’s Reagan National airport, prompting investigations by both the Federal ...
body_text:
US President Donald Trump’s military helicopter Marine One briefly flew too close to a passenger jet taking off from Washington’s Reagan National airport, prompting investigations by both the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the National Transportation Safety Board.

The FAA said in a statement that its preliminary safety review of the incident on Tuesday found “a momentary loss of separation, after which the aircraft continued to move away from one another”.

The statement added that Trump was not in danger and that an air traffic controller remained in contact with both pilots throughout.

According to the Reuters news agency, two people familiar with the matter said that air traffic controllers had not paused commercial departures at Reagan National as required under the policy adopted after a crash last year.

In January 2025, a collision between a military helicopter and an American Airlines regional jet killed 67 people.

Marine One lifted off from the Ellipse near the White House at about 2:33pm local time (18:33 GMT) on Tuesday, en route to Joint Base Andrews ahead of a presidential trip to Los Angeles, according to a White House pool report.

Both the aircraft landed safely, although neither flight’s involvement has been confirmed by the FAA.

A source told Reuters that Envoy Air flight 3742, a regional jet operated on behalf of American Airlines and bound for Pensacola, Florida, was the aircraft involved, and that a second flight, Republic 4700, was separately rerouted as a precaution after coming within three miles of the airport.

The National Transportation Safety Board said it would launch its own investigation into the incident.

The near-miss on Tuesday afternoon revives scrutiny of air traffic protocols at Reagan National following the collision last year.

The crash then led to permanent restrictions on mixed helicopter and commercial traffic at the airport, along with a subsequent ban, introduced in March, on using visual-only separation for helicopters near major US airports.

title: Amazon driver caught on video flinging customer’s package onto porch in infuriating delivery blunder
excerpt:

body_text:
A doorbell camera video captures an Amazon delivery driver throwing a package onto a customer's front porch before walking away. Credit: Nathan Pekas via Storyful

A delivery driver is under scrutiny after a doorbell camera captured a package sailing through the air instead of being carefully delivered.

Ring camera video shared by Florida resident Nathan Pekas shows the driver approaching the home, hurling a package onto the concrete porch, raising a handheld device to take a proof-of-delivery photo and then walking away as a dog howls from inside the house.

The box lands with a loud thud in the video before the driver snaps the photo and leaves without placing the package at the front door.

Pekas told Storyful the package was delivered by Yun Express, a third-party carrier used for some Amazon deliveries.

TEXAS DOORDASH DRIVER GETS HIT BY A CAR FLEEING FROM POLICE AND STILL DELIVERS THE ORDER

A Ring doorbell camera captured a delivery driver after a package was thrown onto the concrete porch of a Florida home. (Nathan Pekas via Storyful)

He also shared a photo showing what appeared to be damage to one corner of the box.

The Florida resident said he was surprised by the driver's handling of the delivery, joking that the state's sweltering summer heat "must have been too much to make those extra two steps to the door."

Amazon acknowledged the incident in a statement provided to Storyful.

DOORDASH DRIVER HAILS KEY TRUMP POLICY AFTER DELIVERING MCDONALD'S TO WHITE HOUSE: 'I'M GOING TO ENJOY IT'

The package recipient shared a photo showing damage to one corner of the box after the delivery. (Nathan Pekas via Storyful)

"This video does not reflect the standards we have for our delivery partners, and we're looking into this matter," an Amazon spokesperson said.

It was not immediately clear whether the contents of the package were damaged or whether the driver remains assigned to make Amazon deliveries.

Fox News Digital has reached out to Amazon for additional comment.

The incident is the latest package delivery to go viral after being captured on a homeowner's doorbell camera.

Last month, a FedEx driver in Georgia made headlines after tumbling backward into a front yard swimming pool while stepping away to take a proof-of-delivery photo.

The driver quickly laughed off the mishap, joking, "I needed that," before climbing out of the pool and returning to the delivery route.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

A beloved Kansas college basketball coach and former Jayhawks standout is in the hospital with serious injuries after a highway crash Tuesday night.

Washburn University head coach Brett Ballard, 46, was behind the wheel of his 2024 Ford F-150 when the crash occurred.

According to the Kansas Highway Patrol, Ballard was traveling westbound on Interstate 470 in Topeka just after 8:15 p.m. when his pickup truck veered off the left side of the roadway.

Brett Ballard of Kansas walks off the court as Maryland players celebrate in the background after the semifinal round of the NCAA Men's Final Four at the Georgia Dome in Atlanta, Ga., on March 30, 2002. Maryland defeated Kansas 97-88 and advanced to the championship game. (Getty Images)

The truck struck a delineator post, traveled into a steep embankment, and then collided with a concrete bridge pillar. The impact left the vehicle heavily damaged. Ballard was the only person inside the truck. First responders transported the injured coach to Stormont Vail Hospital in Topeka for treatment. Authorities confirmed he was wearing his seatbelt at the time of the crash.

Washburn University President JuliAnn Mazachek asked the close-knit community to keep Ballard and his family in their thoughts.

"We are deeply saddened to share that Coach Brett Ballard was seriously injured in a car accident last evening," Mazachek said in a statement. "Our hearts are with Coach Ballard, his family, the men's basketball program and all who are affected during this difficult time."

Ballard has long been one of the most recognizable figures in Kansas basketball. The Hutchinson native played guard for the Kansas Jayhawks from 2000 to 2002 under Hall of Fame coach Roy Williams before spending seven seasons as an assistant on Bill Self's coaching staff.

A Kansas cheerleader waves the school flag as the team enters the court before the start of the game during the NCAA men's basketball tournament at the Kohl Center in Madison, Wis., on March 24, 2002. Kansas beat Oregon 104-86 to advance to the Final Four in Atlanta, Ga. (Getty Images)

Head coach Roy Williams celebrates as Kansas players cut down the net after beating Oregon during the NCAA men's basketball tournament at the Kohl Center in Madison, Wis. The Jayhawks won 104-86 to advance to the Final Four in Atlanta, Ga. (Getty Images)

For the past nine seasons, Ballard has led the Washburn Ichabods, building one of Division II's most consistent programs.

Ballard has compiled a 198-81 overall record while guiding Washburn to multiple NCAA Tournament appearances and helping establish the Ichabods as a perennial contender in the MIAA.

Before taking over at Washburn, Ballard also gained head coaching experience at Baker University, where he led the Wildcats to a Heart of America Athletic Conference regular-season championship and an NAIA national tournament appearance.

Ballard's success at every stop has made him a respected figure throughout the state's basketball community. As word of the crash spread, supporters across Kansas and beyond shared messages of encouragement while hoping for positive news regarding his recovery.

title: Francesca Hong remarks Thanksgiving is her 'favorite holiday,' answers she does not 'want to cancel it'
excerpt: Rep. Tom Tiffany, a Wisconsin gubernatorial hopeful, reacted to Democratic candidate Francesca Hong's past comments suggesting she wanted to cancel Thanksgiving. Tiffany warns that far-left progressiv...
body_text:
Rep. Tom Tiffany, a Wisconsin gubernatorial hopeful, reacted to Democratic candidate Francesca Hong's past comments suggesting she wanted to cancel Thanksgiving. Tiffany warns that far-left progressives want to destroy American culture.

Democratic socialist Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong said Thanksgiving was her "favorite holiday" Wednesday, and she has no interest in canceling it despite her past controversial X posts.

"My favorite holiday is Thanksgiving," Hong told Politico Playbook, which in an X post wrote that Hong was "joking." "Yep, I don't want to cancel it. I actually love it."

Hong explained that the holiday was a "big event" for her family members and their in-laws.

SOCIALIST FRONTRUNNER IN THE HOT SEAT AFTER 'CANCEL THANKSGIVING' POST EMERGES ONLINE

Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong faced backlash for several deleted X posts, including one calling to "cancel Thanksgiving." (Joshua Lott/Getty Images)

"You know, I'm just ... I'm going to be real," Hong said. "I'm kind of a curmudgeon when it comes to holidays in general."

Hong was responding to the backlash she faced for a deleted post, which was initially made on X in November 2020, after she appeared to draw comparisons between the deadly pandemic and the Thanksgiving holiday.

"Cancel Thanksgiving. Should have done this in 1621," Hong wrote, according to Fox News Digital’s previous reporting.

"If it takes a worldwide pandemic for us to realize we should stop celebrating colonialism and the original superspreader event that killed indigenous folx [sic] and women, so be it," she added, referring to the spread of smallpox that killed many Indigenous Americans.

TOP WISCONSIN DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST CANDIDATE CONFRONTED ON PAST 'DEFUND POLICE' RHETORIC

In a statement to Fox News Digital, Hong's campaign previously said, "No, she does not want to 'cancel' Thanksgiving."

However, Hong hesitated to give the same answer when asked if she still believes Thanksgiving should be canceled on CNN Monday.

Francesca Hong initially hesitated to answer whether she still wants to cancel Thanksgiving during an interview on CNN. (Scott Bauer/AP Photo)

"I’m a chef, and one of the first meals that I made that was for the community when I was 16 [years old] was a Thanksgiving meal," Hong said. "I always think my hospitality background in owning a restaurant for seven, eight years, that bringing folks around the table to share conversation and build community is always a good thing.

"But Thanksgiving is also a time that’s incredibly painful for many people in our communities," Hong continued. "And, so, I think there, I wanted to make sure that people understood that there are multiple views, but views can evolve.

"And the position that I'm running for right now, and I think my background as a chef will actually help me become a better governor that's able to bring more people to the table."

LEFT’S LATEST SOCIALIST DARLING DRAGGED OVER ‘WHITENESS’ COMMENTS PULLING IN HER OWN FAMILY: ‘WEIRDO RACISM’

Fox News Digital reached out to Hong's campaign for comment.

Republican Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany criticized Hong's original posts on Fox News Tuesday, accusing her and other socialist candidates of wanting to "destroy" American culture.

Francesa Hong told Politico Wednesday she definitively did not want to cancel Thanksgiving. (Getty Images for WisDems)

"Well, considering she also posted, ‘Please DON'T gather for the colonizer holiday,’ and just days ago called Thanksgiving ‘incredibly painful,’ it's hard to believe she now claims it's her favorite holiday. But this goes far beyond Thanksgiving. It's part of the broader socialist message that seeks to tear down the traditions, institutions, and values that bring Americans together," Tiffany said.

"Whether it's Thanksgiving, Christmas, Culver's, the police or even Valentine's Day, Francesca Hong has spent her entire political career criticizing the very fabric of Wisconsin and the traditions that bring our communities together."

Fox News' Julia Bonavita contributed to this report.

Lindsay Kornick is an associate editor for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to lindsay.kornick@fox.com and on Twitter: @lmkornick.

title: El-Sayed's threat against GOP rival backfires as conservatives bring receipts: 'Is Dubai in Florida?'
excerpt:
