Abdul El-Sayed sparked online controversy moments after capturing the...
body_text:
His comments come as the newly-crowned Democratic Senate nominee challenged the Republican candidate to a series of five debates.

Abdul El-Sayed sparked online controversy moments after capturing the Democratic Party’s nomination in Michigan's Senate race for his word choice in challenging Republican nominee Mike Rogers to a series of five debates.

"I know you're going to say no because you're a coward. Five debates. All right?" El-Sayed said.

"You and I both know that you will wither in front of your own crimes, but I'm gonna make sure Michiganders know about them. By the time we're done, you are not going to have safe quarter from people holding you accountable for what you've done," El-Sayed continued.

The language of "safe quarter" is raising eyebrows among viewers online.

The online backlash demonstrates how closely the Michigan Senate race is being watched across the country and how viewers are analyzing every move of El-Sayed in particular.

2026 MIDTERMS STATE OF PLAY: KEY RACES UNFOLD AS STEVENS, EL-SAYED BATTLE IN MICHIGAN

Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed claps during a news conference in front of the Spirit of Detroit statue Aug. 5, 2026, in Detroit. (Finn Gomez/Getty Images)

The former local public health official succeeded in his race against Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., a more establishment candidate with the backing of Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., despite being heavily outspent.

His campaign has been a proxy for larger questions in the Democratic Party of whether the progressive label and promises of aggressively expanded public sector involvement will resonate with its base over the relative safety of establishment messaging.

Conservatives ripped El-Sayed on social media for attacking Rogers' out-of-state vacation home while he owned multiple rental properties overseas. Doug Powers, a longtime editor and contributor for Twitchy, believes it clashes with El-Sayed's financial disclosures revealing that he owns property not just out of the state but also overseas.

"If I’m the Rogers campaign, I’m putting this in an ad. ‘A socialist who owns property in Dubai and India is attacking me for having a vacation house in Florida while threatening me in my home state?’" Powers wrote in his own post to social media.

"’No safe quarter from people holding you accountable’ is commie messaging," he added.

"The easy rebuttal for Mike Rogers here is to point out that El-Sayed owns property in a luxury development in Dubai," Chuck Ross, an investigative reporter for The Washington Free Beacon, pointed out.

"Is Dubai in Florida?" yet another account wrote.

Fox News Digital previously reported that El-Sayed's most recent financial disclosure exposes how El-Sayed and his wife own at least two foreign properties in Bangalore, India and Dubai. The Dubai property is worth up to $250,000.

Other conservatives slammed El-Sayed for the tone of his message and suggested it was putting a target on the back of his Republican rival.

LIZ PEEK: MICHIGAN CAN STOP THE SOCIALIST FEVER RAGE — OR WATCH IT SWALLOW THE SENATE

Abdul El-Sayed, a Democratic Senate candidate in Michigan, at a campaign event in Detroit Aug. 2, 2026  (Paul Steinhauser/Fox News )

Scott Jennings, the conservative political personality and media commentator on CNN, bashed El-Sayed's phrasing at the victory press conference.

"Abdul el Sayed threatening the safety of his opponent while the Jewish Democrat AG of Michigan says she can't go to a Dem convention because she's not safe, either. Does everyone see what's happening here?" Jennings wrote in a post to X, referring to recent developments in the Wolverine state over anti-Semitic comments.

Brian Newberry, a Rhode Island state representative and former minority leader, echoed Jenning's concern.

"Democratic U.S. Senate nominee, who pals around with [a] guy who celebrates 9/11, tells his Republican opponent that he will ‘not have safe quarter’ in his home state. Who the hell does this guy think he is?" Newberry wrote, hinting at El-Sayed's association with Hasan Piker, a progressive streamer who has drawn backlash for past comments of his own.

"And will any — and I mean ANY — Democrat condemn this rhetoric?"

AG Hamilton, a popular conservative X account, called on El-Sayed to bring more clarity to the statement.

"Someone should ask el Sayed what exactly this means because it certainly comes off as a threat of political violence aimed at his opponent," the account wrote.

El-Sayed’s campaign did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the phrasing or on whether the online reactions were overblown.

DEMS SELECT THEIR CANDIDATE TO FACE LONGTIME GOP LAWMAKER WHO BALKED AT VIRGINIA REDISTRICTING

Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive candidate in the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate in Michigan, speaks during a primary election night event Wednesday, Aug. 5, 2026, at the Majestic Theatre in Detroit. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

In his remarks on Wednesday morning, El-Sayed continued to press his case against Rogers.

"Mike Rogers is a guy whose politics and vision and perspective are old. Mike Rogers is a guy who has never shied away from a corporation he could do a favor for," El-Sayed said.

"If you want a senator who’s going to lick some boots, fine. Go vote for Mike Rogers. But if you want a senator who’s going to stand up to Donald Trump, then you’ve got your option right here."

With the Democratic primary in the rearview mirror, El-Sayed will face off against Rogers in the state’s general election Nov. 3.

Leo Briceno is a politics reporter for the congressional team at Fox News Digital. He was previously a reporter with World Magazine.

title: Taxpayer-funded housing for illegal immigrants in GOP's crosshairs: 'It's got to stop'
excerpt: Sen. Bill Hagerty, R-Tenn., introduces new legislation, the End Housing Welfare for Illegal Aliens Act, that tightens eligibility for federal housing programs and denies grants to sanctuary cities. (C...
body_text:
Sen. Bill Hagerty, R-Tenn., introduces new legislation, the End Housing Welfare for Illegal Aliens Act, that tightens eligibility for federal housing programs and denies grants to sanctuary cities. (Credit: Nicholas Ballasy for Fox News Digital)

EXCLUSIVE: Sen. Bill Hagerty, R-Tenn., is introducing new legislation that works to restrict illegal aliens from reaping federal housing benefits, blocking loopholes and cutting off access for sanctuary cities to receive federal community development grants.

"[Illegal immigrants] have been allowed to participate in federally subsidized housing programs," Hagerty told Fox News Digital. "They're using American taxpayer dollars to jump to the front of the line while putting Americans at the back of the lines. It's got to stop."

The End Housing Welfare for Illegal Aliens Act is part of a larger effort by both the Trump administration and GOP members of Congress to halt illegal immigrants and sanctuary cities' ability to thrive, which they claim often comes at the expense of benefits for the American people.

HOUSE REPUBLICANS MOVE TO MAKE TRUMP'S BORDER POLICIES PERMANENT

President Donald Trump waves as he walks to board Marine One en route to Joint Base Andrews from the Ellipse near the White House Aug. 4, 2026, in Washington, D.C. Trump was traveling to Los Angeles to attend a RNC fundraising event and then onto Las Vegas for a rally Aug. 5. (Alex Wong/Getty Images)

"The Trump administration has taken a look at this," Hagerty said. "The preliminary estimates are 24,000 of these illegals are utilizing HUD programs. Again, crowding out Americans that would be deserving of these programs and, again, putting illegals into these positions."

The bill Hagerty is putting forward codifies the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development’s (HUD) efforts to close loopholes that allow illegal immigrants to receive federal benefits on taxpayer-funded housing if they are roommates with eligible individuals.

"HUD housing assistance is intended for U.S. citizens and certain eligible noncitizens, yet HUD resources serve only a quarter of eligible households in need," HUD said in a statement. "Meanwhile, a recent HUD and DHS audit of all assisted households identified nearly 200,000 tenants with incomplete or unknown eligibility verification. Furthermore, HUD estimates approximately 24,000 illegal aliens, ineligibles and fraudsters in 20,000 ‘mixed status households’ benefit from HUD assistance."

Hagerty’s bill, if passed, would enforce this proposed rule by HUD Secretary Scott Turner under all administrations.

"This current administration is going to do everything it can, I'm certain, to stop this type of fraudulent behavior," Hagerty said. "But what I want to do is preclude this from happening if there were ever to be another Democrat administration."

GOP SENATORS RALLY AROUND NEW DHS PROPOSAL TARGETING SANCTUARY CITIES: 'SHOULD PAY A PRICE'

Sen. Bill Hagerty, R-Tenn., inside the U.S. Capitol Feb. 4, 2026. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc.)

Hagerty also said the legislation would eliminate Biden-era incentives for sanctuary cities by denying these cities access to Community Development Block Grants (CBDG), federal funding that supports affordable housing, infrastructure and local services.

He also argued that, under the Biden administration, the adoption of sanctuary city policies was incentivized because those lacking citizenship documentation are still included in population counts when considering congressional representation.

"What the Biden administration did, they were creating incentives for people to come here illegally," Hagerty said. "You think about where they situated sanctuary cities — in blue states, where they're losing population, where they’re losing voters."

"Why?" Hagerty said. "Because you can count these illegal aliens for the purpose of allocating congressional districts. You can count them for the purpose of locating electoral votes. That is the motive behind the crime."

'AMERICA FIRST' IMMIGRATION OVERHAUL BILL WOULD CODIFY TRUMP'S CAMPAIGN PROMISES ONCE AND FOR ALL

The bill would require public housing authorities to verify citizenship before providing housing assistance. This would change the law so agencies "shall" verify citizenship, meaning they are legally required to do so, instead of saying they only "may" do so.

It would also specifically bar illegal immigrants from being eligible for both Section 202 and Section 811, which provide affordable housing for low-income elderly and people with disabilities.

"Illegal aliens are pushing out and crowding out people that are disabled, American taxpayers that are disabled, elderly that are disabled," Hagerty said.

Hagerty’s efforts to crack down on any negligence in restricting illegal immigrants from federal programs comes amid a broader fight by the Trump administration and Republicans in Congress to crack down on illegal immigration throughout the country.

"The goal is to pass the legislation," Hagerty said. "And I think if you polled Americans, you'd find this is extraordinarily popular."

Cameron Cawthorne is a politics editor for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to Cameron.Cawthorne@Fox.com and on Twitter: @cam_cawthorne

title: Mexican influencer shot dead during TikTok livestream
excerpt:
A Mexican social media influencer with 650,000 followers on TikTok has been killed while he was doing a livestream, authorities have said.

Cesar Gastelum was shot dead on Tuesday in Culiacan, the cap...
body_text:
A Mexican social media influencer with 650,000 followers on TikTok has been killed while he was doing a livestream, authorities have said.

Cesar Gastelum was shot dead on Tuesday in Culiacan, the capital of Mexico’s volatile Sinaloa state. The shooting took place near the local prosecutor’s office.

A video of the moment of Gastelum’s death, seen by The Associated Press news agency, shows him laughing with two other men in the car park of a Kentucky Fried Chicken when two men pull up on a motorcycle. One is seen pulling out a gun and shooting Gastelum. The attackers then flee the scene.

Sinaloa has been ravaged by warring between two factions, Los Mayos and Los Chapitos, of the Sinaloa Cartel in recent years, with dead bodies left across the city marked with either faction’s signature.

“We must find out why this deplorable homicide occurred,” Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum told journalists during a Wednesday morning news conference.

“Perpetrators must be arrested,” she added.

Gastelum posted content in which he would refer to himself as “belico”, a term often used in subcultures in Mexico to imply a connection to cartel culture.

Mexico’s security cabinet and local prosecutors said an investigation was ongoing and that it appeared Gastelum had released some videos in which he “alluded to a faction of a criminal group”.

In May 2025, 23-year-old beauty influencer Valeria Marquez was also shot dead while livestreaming on TikTok, in the central state of Jalisco.

Soon after, the US Department of the Treasury imposed sanctions against five leaders of a Mexican drug cartel, including the prime suspect in Marquez’s murder.

The sanctions targeted the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG), which the administration of US President Donald Trump says is responsible for a significant share of fentanyl and other illegal drugs entering the US.

The cartel is led by Nemesio Ruben “El Mencho” Oseguera Cervantes, who was among the five leaders named. US authorities have offered a $15m reward for information leading to his capture.

A cartel commander closely linked to him, Ricardo Ruiz Velasco, was also sanctioned. The US Treasury Department said that he was the prime suspect in the murder of Marquez, whom they identified as his alleged romantic partner.

On Wednesday, the Trump administration announced rewards of up to $102m for information leading to the arrest or conviction of eight CJNG leaders.

title: Winner of Florida python hunting contest nabs 96 snakes: ‘I was on a mission’
excerpt:
Burmese pythons are an invasive species in the Everglades, and the challenge is part of initiative to remove them

The winner of this year’s annual Florida Python Challenge hunted down and eliminated ...
body_text:
Burmese pythons are an invasive species in the Everglades, and the challenge is part of initiative to remove them

The winner of this year’s annual Florida Python Challenge hunted down and eliminated 96 invasive Burmese pythons from the Everglades national park, as part of an initiative to remove hundreds of the snakes from the area every year.

The challenge invites hunters to participate in 10 days of capturing and humanely euthanizing as many of the invasive snakes as possible across eight designated hunting locations, with the winner taking home a cash prize of $10,000. The event is hosted by Florida fish, wildlife and conservation (FWC), the south Florida water management district, the National Park Service and others.

This year’s competition drew 907 participants from 30 US states, as well as Canada and Vietnam. The winner, Tom Rahill, harvested 96 Burmese pythons, all from the Everglades. A python hunter by trade, Rahill founded an organization called SwampApes in Broward county that takes veterans suffering from PTSD on python hunts in Florida’s wetlands.

In comments reported by Naples Daily News, Rahill told an FWC meeting in Panama City on Wednesday: “I was on a mission to get one of our veterans a big snake. I did it. And we wrestled this thing … The veteran was just over the moon.”

Once that was achieved, he said he went deeper into the Everglades, where he found the 96 snakes. Over the course of 10 days in July, 280 snakes in total were removed. Before the competition began, 1,400 pythons had been taken out this year.

The challenge also awards several other cash prizes, including $1,000 for the longest python killed, which this year went to Rahm Levinson, who hunted a snake measuring 16ft 5in.

Burmese pythons are native to south-east Asia, and have wreaked havoc since they were first found in the Everglades ecosystem in the 1990s, consuming resources and wiping out a significant portion of the area’s native wildlife. The apex predators are incredibly hard to detect, contributing to the population ballooning to a number that conservative estimates put in the tens of thousands.

Females can lay dozens of eggs, sometimes up to 100 annually, and although many hatchlings do not survive to adulthood, there are fears the pythons are reproducing faster than they can be caught. The annual challenge is therefore now held during the summer hatching season in a bid to boost the number captured.

Aimed at raising public awareness of invasive species, and getting the public involved in conservation and efforts to protect the Everglades ecosystem by controlling the number of Burmese pythons, the event has seen more than 1,600 of the snakes removed from the area since 2017. Combined with FWC contractors, who hunt the reptiles year-round, that figure rises to more than 19,000 snakes removed since 2017.

Sarah Funck, program coordinator at the FWC, told Wednesday’s meeting that there is no “silver bullet” to solve Florida’s python invasion, but stressed that the elimination of just one python “is a win for Florida’s native wildlife”.

title: Nigeria announces rescue of 308 kidnapped citizens
excerpt:
More than 300 people who had been kidnapped across Nigeria have been freed in an intelligence and security operation, the government has announced.

“President Bola Ahmed Tinubu warmly welcomes the su...
body_text:
More than 300 people who had been kidnapped across Nigeria have been freed in an intelligence and security operation, the government has announced.

“President Bola Ahmed Tinubu warmly welcomes the successful rescue of 308 Nigerian citizens who were abducted in different attacks in Niger and Kwara states,” Bayo Onanuga, a special adviser to Nigeria’s president, said in a statement.

The statement said that 163 of those rescued were abducted from the Woro Community in Kaiama Local Government Area in Kwara State, and 145 were taken from Niger State.

“The victims were rescued from the Kainji Lake National Park Forest in New Bussa Local Government Area of Niger State”, according to the statement, as a result of a “coordinated, intelligence-driven operation”. The operation was carried out by the country’s National Counter Terrorism Centre, involving members of the armed forces, the police force and the Department of State Services.

“It was the largest rescue operation ever carried out on the same day by Nigeria’s joint security team,” the statement added.

The government in Kwara State, near the border with Benin, welcomed the rescue in a social media post, local channel Arise News reported.

“Kudos to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu GCFR, security forces, and everyone who played a role in this huge feat. We are grateful!”, said the Kwara government statement, announcing the release of those abducted during the February 3 attack on local communities in Kaiama.

At least 200 people were killed in the attack, when suspected Boko Haram-linked fighters launched a coordinated assault that lasted several hours, according to the Nigeria-based Punch website.

Kidnapping for ransom by criminal groups, Boko Haram-linked fighters and gangs known as bandits has become a major crisis in Nigeria, especially in areas with little state presence.

Soft targets, including schools, churches and mosques, particularly in vulnerable rural communities with limited state security, have been particularly at risk.

On January 18, 177 people were abducted from three churches in the village of Kurmin Wali in Kaduna State.

Last month, security services freed at least 40 students and teachers kidnapped in May from the southern state of Oyo.

In June, the president announced that the military had “neutralised” more than 13,000 “terrorists” in the past year. The army also said it had rescued 360 people abducted by Boko Haram, which has spread across parts of the country from Borno State, once considered the centre of its operations.

“The successful execution of this intelligence-led operation demonstrates the growing efficiency and collaboration among our security services. I commend our gallant men and women in uniform for their bravery and unwavering commitment to safeguarding Nigerian lives,” the president said in his latest statement.

title: Explosive drone forces shutdown at major German airport serving NATO, Ukraine flights
excerpt: Jennifer Griffin reports on Russia's shadow fleet launching a drone campaign across Europe to surveil military sites and test NATO's air defenses. The International Institute for Strategic Studies rep...
body_text:
Jennifer Griffin reports on Russia's shadow fleet launching a drone campaign across Europe to surveil military sites and test NATO's air defenses. The International Institute for Strategic Studies report reveals 144 suspected drones near sensitive sites in Germany, France and the UK.

A drone carrying explosives was found near a Ukrainian plane at Germany's Leipzig/Halle Airport late Tuesday, prompting officials to warn the incident represented "a new quality of danger," authorities said Wednesday.

The discovery temporarily shut down both runways at the major European freight hub and forced several flights to divert to other airports, according to The Associated Press.

Another flying object was spotted nearby shortly before midnight and several flights, including one passenger plane, were then diverted to other airports.

JETBLUE FLIGHT REPORTS DRONE STRIKE DURING APPROACH TO NEW YORK AIRPORT: FAA

Police said an airport worker had found the first drone near the airport's south runway with "an unknown explosive device." (Hendrik Schmidt/DPA via AP)

German police launched a large response and opened an investigation into the two incidents.

Police said an airport worker found the first explosive drone near the airport's south runway with "an unknown explosive device."

An explosives disposal robot was deployed to examine the device before authorities removed its detonator.

The plane, bearing the blue and yellow colors of the Ukrainian flag, displayed the English-language slogan, "Be Brave Like Kherson," a tribute to the southern Ukrainian region, Deutsche Welle reported.

In the second incident, an unidentified flying object collided with a cargo aircraft that had aborted its landing at Leipzig/Halle Airport because of the runway closure.

HELICOPTER REPORTS NEAR MISS WITH RC PLANE NEAR JFK AFTER JETBLUE DRONE STRIKE

The plane bore the colors of the Ukrainian flag. (Hendrik Schmidt/DPA via AP)

The aircraft diverted to Hannover Airport, about 125 miles north-west of Leipzig, where officials found minor damage, according to The Associated Press.

German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said the discovery of the first drone marked a significant escalation.

"Drone sightings, drone threats, including in a hybrid context, are something we know from the past," he said. "That a drone armed with explosives is at an airport is a new threat scenario."

Dobrindt also described the incident as "a hybrid attack scenario."

He said questions about the type of explosives used, the drone's origin and who was responsible remained under investigation.

"All the speculation that is currently going on about the explosives, the construction, the question of the drone, the origin and, of course, who is behind it, is now part of the investigation," Dobrindt said.

"What is happening now also shows that the assessment made months ago — that we are dealing with a high level of danger — was justified."

In June, Dobrindt opened Germany's Joint Centre for Countering Hybrid Threats, which brings together federal and state security agencies to address threats including espionage, sabotage and disinformation.

REPORT WARNS RUSSIA USING SHADOW FLEET TO PROBE NATO DRONE DEFENSES

A drone carrying explosives was found at Germany's Leipzig/Halle Airport Tuesday night next to a Ukrainian plane, and officials warned the incident represented "a new quality of danger." (Hendrik Schmidt/DPA via AP)

Leipzig/Halle Airport is a major European cargo hub, and Ukrainian Antonov transport aircraft are based there.

NATO said it was aware of the incidents but referred questions to German authorities.

RUSSIA LINKED TO ARSON ATTACKS ON PROPERTIES CONNECTED TO UK PM KEIR STARMER, POLICE SAY

Ukraine's ambassador to Germany, Oleksii Makeiev, suggested Moscow may have been behind the incident, telling Welt TV Wednesday, "Who else could it be but Russia?" according to reports.

In 2024, an incendiary device ignited at a logistics center at Leipzig/Halle Airport, setting fire to a freight container in an incident Western security officials suspect was part of a Russian intelligence sabotage operation.

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial: toxicologist testifies about medications found in defendant’s blood
excerpt:
Variety of prescriptions were found in blood of mother accused of strangling her three kids, according to testimony

Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

The trial of Lindsay Clancy, the...
body_text:
Variety of prescriptions were found in blood of mother accused of strangling her three kids, according to testimony

Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

The trial of Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mom accused of killing her three children in January 2023, continued on Wednesday with a forensic toxicologist testifying to the variety and concentration of medications found in the defendant’s blood.

Justin Brower, a forensic toxicologist with NMS Laboratories, testified that his lab examined the levels of four psychiatric medications detected in Clancy’s blood after she allegedly strangled her kids and attempted to take her own life.

Those drugs included the antidepressant mirtazapine, the mood stabilizer lamotrigine, the antidepressant trazodone and quetiapine, a drug used to treat schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and major depressive disorder. Brower noted that quetiapine could also be prescribed in low doses to treat insomnia.

Asked if the concentrations of each drug were different from what was prescribed, Brower said the only drug that appeared slightly elevated was quetiapine, but noted that it was not at a “toxic concentration” or “suicidal concentration”.

“Usually people take handfuls of pills when they’re trying to harm themselves and take their own life, and this is not consistent with that,” Brower testified.

He later testified, upon questioning from Clancy’s defense attorney, that the toxicology results “don’t tell the entire story”.

Prosecutors say Clancy acted intentionally when she killed her children Callan, eight months old; Dawson, three years old; and Cora, five years old. Her defense team says she was a loving mother who was overcome by postpartum psychosis, had undiagnosed bipolar disorder and was on problematic medications.

The court has heard from a range of experts for the prosecution, with testimony at times halted when witnesses, including Clancy’s ex-husband, Patrick Clancy, or the defendant have become overwhelmed.

If convicted, Clancy faces life in prison without parole. A not-guilty verdict by reason of a lack of criminal responsibility could lead to commitment to a state mental health facility.

On Monday, jurors heard excerpts from Clancy’s journals that revealed her mental struggles including thoughts of suicide and her feeling overwhelmed with motherhood, including her struggles to get her newborn to sleep, going back to work as a labor and delivery nurse, not being able to breastfeed, and feeling disconnected from her children and husband.

“I’m so desperate to get a mental break from taking care of everyone that my mind is trying to find something physically wrong with me,” she wrote in an entry on 18 November 2022.

The trial has shone a light on significant gaps in the diagnosis and treatment of postpartum psychosis and postpartum depression. Clancy’s attorneys say her condition seemed to worsen on an ever-shifting lineup of psychiatric prescriptions.

In the three months before the killings, various clinicians prescribed a range of antidepressants, sleep aids, an antipsychotic and other medications while she reported increasingly profound insomnia, anxiety, despair and confusion about what was real, according to a civil lawsuit filed against caregivers that claims they should have recognized that both she and her children were at risk.

In her diaries, Clancy wrote, “I want help. I want to be well,” and described feeling “incredibly sad and guilty” about not breastfeeding. She also wrote that she was “obsessed” with managing Callan’s sleep and nap schedule.

“I have crazy brain fog. I feel like I can’t make a plan,” she wrote in another, undated entry. “I live moment to moment waiting for the next nap time. I’m terrified of Cal getting overtired now because I feel can’t help him.

“Hearing him cry for 1 plus hours and not intervening just about killed me,” Clancy wrote, adding that she had told her husband, Patrick, “I want to die.” She also wrote: “I now have horrible insomnia and anxiety which is causing depression. I have no appetite. I don’t know what’s wrong with me. I want help. I want to be well.”

Clancy first sought help from a postpartum depression program in late December 2022. She went on to check herself into a psychiatric hospital and later told a psychiatrist that she heard a “man’s voice” in her head telling her to “kill the children so you can kill yourself”. Nineteen days later, after being discharged, she carried out the killings.

The defendant is now paralyzed from her attempt to take her own life. When she woke up in hospital and was asked by a forensic psychologist how she felt, she responded: “Horrified.” Dr Jhilam Biswas of Brigham and Women’s hospital testified that Clancy asked “can she have visitors, and where her family is”.

The court has also heard from Patrick Clancy, who recounted the medications his former wife was taking, her health and demeanor, and the destructive thoughts she was having. He has said he forgives Lindsay and believes that the killings were motivated purely by her mental health.

When the jury heard the anguished 911 call Patrick Clancy made on the night of the killings, several members could be seen holding back tears. He described returning home after collecting medications and a takeout meal to find their home “quiet”.

Patrick Clancy went upstairs to find found the door to their bedroom locked. After breaking in, the room was covered in blood and the window was open. His wife was lying on the ground below. She told him she had tried to take her own life. He asked where the children were, and she told him they were in the basement.

When emergency services arrived, he ventured downstairs to find their three children with exercise resistance bands around their necks. Duxbury police officer Brian Josephine testified that he heard Patrick scream, “She killed the fucking kids.”

title: News Corp subscriptions fall in Australia as company takes aim at ‘slimy’ AI slop
excerpt:
Chief executive Robert Thomson says ‘crass kleptomaniac’ AI companies are ‘in possession of stolen goods’

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app...
body_text:
Chief executive Robert Thomson says ‘crass kleptomaniac’ AI companies are ‘in possession of stolen goods’

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

News Corp has reported a slight slide in digital subscriptions at its Australian mastheads, erasing recent gains, among otherwise robust financials at the Rupert Murdoch-backed global conglomerate.

Digital subscribers at News Corp Australia – a division that includes the Australian, the Daily Telegraph and the Herald Sun, among others – fell from 1,166,000 to 1,162,000 during the financial year, according to the company’s internal data published in its full year results on Thursday morning.

The figures represent a reversal in momentum. The Australian division has grown digital subscriptions in recent years, as it transitions away from its traditional newspaper base.

News Corp’s broader news media unit, which includes the Sun and the Times in London and the New York Post, recorded mixed results, with advertising revenue still under pressure, falling 2% during the year to 30 June.

The news media division also recorded costs linked to the launch of News Corp’s latest newspaper, the California Post, which is the Los Angeles outpost of the New York Post and edited by Australian News Corp veteran Nick Papps.

The News Corp chief executive, Robert Thomson, used the release of the company’s financial results to hit out at AI models that “pilfer and profit from our work”, as media companies around the world seek compensation for the use of their content.

“Without our journalists, our authors, our data, our brands and our professional expertise, users would be drowning in a slimy sea of AI slop,” Thomson said.

“We will pursue those pilferers and companies that are clients of these crass kleptomaniacs should know they are patently in possession of stolen goods.”

News Corp has commercial agreements in place with OpenAI and Meta.

The comments come amid contested plans by the Albanese government to expand its news bargaining incentive, which would require tech giants to compensate media outlets for the news on their platforms, either through making commercial deals or paying a higher levy.

title: Trump has become America's most targeted leader, facing threats every few months
excerpt: Weijia Jiang recounts Friday watching President Donald Trump huddle with Cabinet officials moments after the shooting at the first White House Correspondents' Association Dinner in April as journalist...
body_text:
Weijia Jiang recounts Friday watching President Donald Trump huddle with Cabinet officials moments after the shooting at the first White House Correspondents' Association Dinner in April as journalists raced to report the unfolding crisis.

President Donald Trump has become the most targeted U.S. leader on record among both sitting and former presidents, facing threat-related incidents roughly every two to three months in recent years.

Trump has survived three major assassination attempts and nearly a dozen other threat-related incidents over the past two years alone. Overall, he has faced nearly 20 known threats since first taking office in 2017.

By comparison, every other U.S. president targeted in an assassination attempt faced just one, except President Gerald R. Ford, who survived two. Those presidents include Andrew Jackson, Abraham Lincoln, James A. Garfield, William McKinley, Theodore Roosevelt, Franklin D. Roosevelt, Harry Truman, John F. Kennedy, Gerald R. Ford, Ronald Reagan, Bill Clinton, George W. Bush and Barack Obama. Four of those presidents — Lincoln, Garfield, McKinley and Kennedy — were killed.

FROM TRAINED ASSASSINS TO RALLY STAGE RUSHERS, HERE'S EVERY KNOWN ATTEMPT ON TRUMP'S LIFE SINCE 2016

Photos of the assassination attempt against then-Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump are displayed during the Republican National Convention in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, on Thursday, July 18, 2024. (Jae C. Hong/AP Photo)

Seven known threat-related incidents occurred during Trump's first presidency, while four occurred during his 2024 campaign, including two assassination attempts. His second presidency has already seen eight additional incidents, including a third assassination attempt.

July 2024: Trump's first assassination attempt came during a campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, when a gunman opened fire from a nearby rooftop, killing one spectator and critically wounding two others. The shooter, 20-year-old Thomas Matthew Crooks, struck Trump in the upper right ear before being killed by a Secret Service sniper.

September 2024: Two months later, Secret Service agents spotted a gunman hiding in bushes with a rifle near Trump's Florida golf course while the then-presidential candidate was golfing. The suspect, Ryan Wesley Routh, was arrested and later sentenced to life in prison.

TWO MEN SHOT AT TRUMP'S BUTLER RALLY SUE FEDERAL GOVERNMENT OVER SECRET SERVICE 'PREVENTABLE FAILURES'

April 2026: A major security breach occurred during the White House Correspondents' Dinner while Trump was in attendance. The suspect, Cole Allen, allegedly charged a security checkpoint armed with multiple weapons, shot an officer and was later taken into custody.

Trump's first three security incidents unfolded during his 2016 campaign before he ever took office.

March 2016: An attendee at a Trump campaign rally in Dayton, Ohio, attempted to rush the stage before being arrested. The suspect, Thomas DiMassimo, 22, told police he intended to grab the microphone and shout that Trump was a racist but reportedly did not intend to harm him. He was later sentenced to one year of probation.

June 2016: Three months later, a British national attending a Trump campaign rally in Las Vegas attempted to grab a police officer's handgun from her holster, according to a federal criminal complaint. The suspect, Michael Steven Sandford, initially told an officer he wanted Trump's autograph before trying to seize the weapon and later admitting he intended to kill Trump. He was sentenced to 12 months and one day in prison.

November 2016: Secret Service agents rushed Trump off the stage during a campaign rally in Reno, Nevada, after an attendee shouted "gun." Authorities found no weapon but briefly detained Austyn Crites, 33, who said he had brought a sign reading "Republicans Against Trump." Trump returned to the stage minutes later to finish his remarks.

Thomas Matthew Crooks was a 20-year-old from Bethel Park, Pennsylvania, who attempted to assassinate Trump during a 2024 campaign rally before being shot and killed by Secret Service agents. (Associated Press; Fox News Digital)

September 2017: A man stole a forklift and drove it toward Trump's presidential motorcade in an apparent attempt to overturn the presidential limousine in North Dakota. The suspect, Gregory Lee Leingang, later pleaded guilty to federal charges and was sentenced in 2019 to time served and one year of supervised release.

October 2018: A Navy veteran in Utah was charged after ricin-laced letters addressed to Trump and other officials were intercepted before delivery. William Clyde Allen III was charged with five federal counts but was later found incompetent to assist in his defense.

August 2020: Trump was abruptly escorted out of a briefing room during a televised news conference after a Secret Service officer shot a man who threatened to kill people near the White House. The suspect, Myron Basil Berryman, 51, of Forestville, Maryland, was found unarmed and arrested on a charge of assaulting a law enforcement officer, according to the Metropolitan Police Department.

September 2020: A suspect mailed a ricin-laced letter to Trump that was intercepted before reaching the White House. The sender, Pascale Cecile Veronique Ferrier, a dual citizen of Canada and France, admitted to manufacturing ricin at her residence in Canada and was later sentenced to 262 months in prison, equivalent to more than 21 years, followed by lifetime supervised release.

Trump then faced two assassination attempts and two additional threat-related incidents during his 2024 presidential campaign.

July 2024: One day prior to the Butler assassination attempt, federal authorities arrested a Pakistani national accused of orchestrating a murder-for-hire plot targeting Trump and other U.S. officials on behalf of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The suspect, Asif Merchant, was later convicted in federal court in March 2026.

November 2024: Following his second assassination attempt in September 2024, the Justice Department disclosed another alleged Iranian murder-for-hire plot targeting Trump. The suspect, Farhad Shakeri, was accused of being an Iranian government asset who had been tasked with planning the assassination of Trump. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said in March 2026 that Shakeri had been killed in a U.S. military operation.

Suspected would-be assassin Ryan Routh was arrested by law enforcement in Florida in September 2024. He was convicted of all charges against him. (Martin County Sheriff's Office/Reuters)

Just one and a half years into his second presidency, Trump has faced seven additional threat-related incidents and one assassination attempt.

May 2025: A Florida man was arraigned in federal court after allegedly writing a letter to an official at the Charlotte Correctional Institution claiming he had "orchestrated the most daring Presidential assassination that this country has ever seen" and that "Donald J. Trump must perish." The suspect, Christopher Davies, later admitted he wanted to kill Trump and was sentenced to 27 months in federal prison.

July 2025: Authorities arrested a Texas man after he allegedly threatened Trump on social media ahead of the president's visit to the state following the July 4 flooding along the Guadalupe River. The suspect, Robert Herrera, was later sentenced to two years in prison.

August 2025: Authorities arrested a Georgia man after he allegedly posted a comment on a TikTok livestream threatening to shoot Trump. The suspect, 29-year-old Jauan Rashun Porter, wrote, "So there's only one way to make America great and that is putting a bullet in between Trump's eyes." He was later sentenced to more than three years in federal prison.

FBI DISRUPTS ALLEGED EXPLOSIVE-DRONE PLOT TARGETING WHITE HOUSE UFC EVENT, OFFICIALS SAY

Cole Allen lies face down on the floor as law enforcement officers detain him following an alleged shooting at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner in Washington, D.C., on April 25, 2026. (@realDonaldTrump via Truth Social; Heather Diehl/Getty Images)

February 2026: An armed man drove into the secure perimeter of Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach as another vehicle was exiting the property. The suspect, 21-year-old Austin Tucker Martin, was fatally shot by authorities.

April 2026: Officials unsealed a federal criminal complaint against a Kentucky man accused of posting a series of politically violent threats on Instagram between January and late March 2026. The suspect, 23-year-old Kadrioan Serainity Santiago, allegedly threatened to cut Trump with a razor blade and feed his skin to stray dogs. He also threatened to kill the next member of law enforcement who interacted with him, encouraged violence against ICE agents, and posted comments saying, "I’m filled with political violence."

June 2026: Law enforcement officials uncovered an alleged terrorism conspiracy targeting Trump's UFC event at the White House just four days before the mixed martial arts event was scheduled to take place. Eight men were indicted in connection with an alleged plot to fly explosive-laden drones into the event and open fire on attendees as they fled, according to authorities.

August 2026: Authorities arrested a suspect who was allegedly seen photographing and recording security preparations ahead of a scheduled fundraising dinner at the Trump National Golf Club in Rancho Palos Verdes, California. The suspect, Jeanine John Taele, 38, was found carrying a 16-round magazine loaded with ammunition, while investigators recovered an additional pistol and a fake "security protection agent" badge from his truck.

Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Diddy's federal prison release delayed weeks after reported solitary confinement stint
excerpt:
Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Sean "Diddy" Combs' federal prison release date was changed once again.

Diddy, 56, is now expected to leave prison on Feb. 20, 2028...
body_text:
Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Sean "Diddy" Combs' federal prison release date was changed once again.

Diddy, 56, is now expected to leave prison on Feb. 20, 2028, nearly one month after his previously scheduled release date, according to the Federal Bureau of Prisons. Diddy's release date has changed multiple times since he began serving his sentence.

According to multiple reports, the disgraced rap mogul was reportedly sent to solitary confinement last month following a prison fight with another inmate.

DIDDY SENT TO SOLITARY CONFINEMENT AFTER PRISON FIGHT WITH ANOTHER INMATE: MULTIPLE REPORTS

The Federal Bureau of Prisons moved Sean "Diddy" Combs' release date back following a reported incident at the FCI Fort Dix prison. It's unclear if his release date was impacted due to the reported fight. (Scott Dudelson)

The alleged incident began after a fellow inmate "made a remark to Combs, which instigated the event" at FCI Fort Dix, ABC News reported at the time.

Diddy was then reportedly sent to solitary confinement, the outlet noted. It's unclear if his release date was impacted due to the reported fight.

CASSIE VENTURA FLED THE UNITED STATES AFTER TESTIFYING AGAINST DIDDY IN SEX CRIMES TRIAL: DOCS

"For privacy, safety, and security reasons, we do not release information regarding the conditions of confinement for any inmate, including housing assignments, nor do we discuss whether a particular inmate is the subject of allegations, investigations, or sanctions," a representative for the Federal Bureau of Prisons told Fox News Digital.

Sean "Diddy" Combs did not testify in his federal trial for sex crimes. (Stephen Lovekin/Getty Images)

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Diddy's representatives declined Fox News Digital's request for comment.

In September 2024, the "Last Night" singer was arrested on federal sex trafficking charges after months of sexual misconduct allegations, lawsuits, investigations and the release of surveillance video that appeared to show the rapper severely beating his then-girlfriend Cassie in the hallway of a Los Angeles hotel.

He was sentenced to more than four years behind bars in October after being convicted in July on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Cassie and Diddy met in 2006 and officially ended their romantic relationship in 2018. (Getty Images)

Cassie, who was pregnant with her third child, testified over the course of four days in the Diddy trial last summer. (Jane Rosenberg)

Diddy initially faced a maximum of life in prison if convicted on charges, which included racketeering conspiracy, sex trafficking by force, coercion and transportation to engage in prostitution.

A jury convicted Diddy on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution on July 2. The "I'll Be Missing You" rapper was acquitted of his most serious charges of racketeering and sex trafficking.

In addition to the 50-month sentence, Diddy will have five years of supervised release and pay a $500,000 fine. The prosecution recommended 135 months (just over 11 years) for his sentencing.

title: Man arrested at Trump’s California golf course faces more charges
excerpt:
Jeanine John Taele detained for ‘suspicious’ behavior and charged with possession of unregistered short-barreled rifle

A California man who was arrested at Donald Trump’s Los Angeles-area golf course...
body_text:
Jeanine John Taele detained for ‘suspicious’ behavior and charged with possession of unregistered short-barreled rifle

A California man who was arrested at Donald Trump’s Los Angeles-area golf course ahead of a presidential visit is facing more charges, as authorities released new details about the investigation.

Authorities say federal agents first observed 38-year-old Jeanine John Taele near the golf grounds in Rancho Palos Verdes on 31 July, wearing an earpiece and capturing photographs and videos of security agents assessing the property.

Taele returned on 2 August, authorities say, two days before Trump was scheduled to visit the resort for a fundraising dinner with the Republican National Committee (RNC). Teale approached federal agents and said he was employed by the state department and was there for a security detail.

After detaining Taele for “suspicious” behavior, Los Angeles county sheriff’s deputies found a loaded magazine in his pocket. In his pickup truck, which was parked at the golf club, deputies found a loaded 9mm pistol, binoculars and a badge labeled “security protection agent”, authorities have said.

Law enforcement officers also recovered a trove of weapons from his residence in the nearby city of Downey, including a .45-caliber pistol, body armor, an illegally modified AR-type pistol, among others, officials said. Law enforcement officials also located notebooks containing “concerning statements” in the home. The Los Angeles county sheriff’s office declined to comment on the nature of the remarks.

Taele was due in court Wednesday on a federal weapons charge but the hearing was cancelled. He was charged federally with possession of an unregistered short-barreled rifle that was found at this home, authorities said. The complaint alleges the firearm is an illegally modified AR-style rifle with a barrel that was cut down to 10in (25cm) from 14in (35cm).

He is being held at a downtown LA jail on state charges, according to booking records. He was not yet in federal custody, said a spokesperson for the US attorney’s office. Taele is facing a misdemeanor charge for carrying a concealed weapon in a vehicle and two felony charges for possession of a short-barreled rifle or shotgun and the manufacture, importation or sale of a large-capacity magazine, court records show.

The Los Angeles county public defender’s office, which is representing Taele in the state criminal case, declined to comment.

Trump addressed the arrest on Tuesday, telling Fox News “only consequential presidents” are targeted, “and I am definitely consequential”, which he said brought him “a little solace”.

Taele already appeared in court on state weapons charges and a second-degree robbery charge for an unrelated incident.

“There is no room for error, particularly in light of previous attempts on President Trump’s life,” said Patrick Grandy, the assistant director in charge of the FBI’s Los Angeles office, in a statement.

In April, Cole Tomas Allen, a California man who authorities say harbored resentment for the Trump administration, rushed past a security checkpoint during the White House correspondents’s association dinner, where the president was in attendance, and shot a firearm before being apprehended by Secret Service agents. He has been charged with an attempt to assassinate a US president, to which he has pleaded not guilty.

In July 2024, a gunman opened fire at a rally where Trump spoke as the Republican presidential nominee. A crowd member was killed and a bullet grazed Trump’s ear. Federal agents fatally shot the suspected shooter, 20-year-old Thomas Matthew Crooks. An FBI investigation found no clear motive behind the deadly shooting.

Ryan Routh was recently sentenced to life in prison after being convicted of attempting to assassinate Trump on a Florida golf course in September 2024. Prosecutors said Routh spent weeks plotting to kill Trump before aiming a rifle through shrubbery as Trump played golf at his West Palm Beach country club.

Taele was a corporal in the US marines who was deployed to Iraq in 2008 and Afghanistan in 2010 and worked as a warehouse clerk, according to the US Marine Corps. He earned numerous commendations, including an award for good conduct, during his service from 2008 to 2016.

In October 2016, Taele was issued a California firearm permit for 0.40 caliber, 0.45 caliber and 9mm weapons, state records show. That permit expired in 2020. Taele was also a licensed security guard in the state between February 2019 and February 2025, records show.

title: FIFA pledges to defend Infantino after World Cup rights plan collapses
excerpt: FIFA’s leadership has reaffirmed its “full support” for President Gianni Infantino, days after he was forced to abandon a plan to sell off World Cup commercial rights that triggered a rare revolt with...
body_text:
FIFA’s leadership has reaffirmed its “full support” for President Gianni Infantino, days after he was forced to abandon a plan to sell off World Cup commercial rights that triggered a rare revolt within world football’s governing body.

The declaration followed a crisis meeting in Rabat, Morocco, on Wednesday, called after mounting pressure from UEFA and other confederations threatened to derail Infantino’s expected re-election to a fourth term at FIFA’s Congress in March.

In a statement, FIFA said Secretary-General Mattias Grafstrom and members of its management board reiterated their backing for Infantino as “the only official elected by the 211 FIFA Member Associations”.

Infantino reciprocated support for Grafstrom and FIFA’s administration.

Officials acknowledged that “mistakes were made” over the now-withdrawn FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal, which would have sold a 20 percent stake in a new commercial rights body to private investors to raise $4.2bn, and involved a company with family ties to US President Donald Trump.

FIFA said an apology had been issued in a separate letter to its managing council and member associations, with a review and report to follow. The organisation added it would “no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity” and would take “all necessary measures” to defend its reputation.

The meeting followed days of open dissent.

UEFA, the Union of European Football Associations, said it had lost confidence in Infantino’s leadership and issued FIFA with a “document preservation letter”. Infantino’s senior adviser, Carlos Cordeiro, resigned in protest, and former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger distanced himself from the plan.

The Times of London reported that UEFA, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation were prepared to paralyse FIFA or launch rival competitions if Infantino did not step aside, though some federations, including Qatar and several African associations, have publicly backed him.

"I have not had any plastic surgery at all. I don't think I need it," Stewart told People magazine.

"I use a little bit of fillers," she explained. "I go maybe once every four months for touch-ups.

"I'm more a maintenance kind of person. I'm not getting boobs done and hips and butts and stuff like that."

"Now, it's less important," she said when asked whether she still envies friends with happy marriages. "The older you get, the less you really need a mate, I think.

"I wouldn't want to be beleaguered with an older, ill person."

Stewart also marked her 85th birthday by sharing a photo of herself relaxing in a bubbling hot tub during a stay in Maine.

Fans quickly flooded the comments with compliments, with one writing, "Damn serving face too," while another added, "Martha you are everything truly."

The birthday milestone comes as Stewart continues embracing getting older on her own terms.

"I don't think about age," she told People. "Eighty-five is just a number; that's all I consider it. I don't want to have a party. It's not a big deal.

"My goal is to keep learning about everything."

Stewart credited much of her youthful appearance to the lifestyle she has maintained for decades.

"I have good genes. My mom looked great at 95," she said. "We eat well. We don't drink very much. We don't smoke. We eat healthy food. We exercise daily. I horseback-ride."

Stewart's disciplined routine extends well beyond her diet. She told People she still wakes at 3 a.m. every morning to complete her daily puzzles before starting her day.

The lifestyle entrepreneur recently recreated her 1995 People cover at her 156-acre Bedford, New York, farm, where she reflected on the career that made her the country's best-known homemaking authority.

ROSIE O'DONNELL WALKED AWAY AT THE HEIGHT OF HER SUCCESS AFTER REACHING ONE JAW-DROPPING FINANCIAL MILESTONE

Martha Stewart has called herself a "perfectionist." (Valerie Terranova/Getty Images)

"I still am a perfectionist. I still like to do many things at the same time. I like to do all the same things I've pretty much always done," Stewart said. "I'd like to have a little bit more free time. I don't have any free time at all, but I'm working on that."

Raised in Nutley, New Jersey, Stewart began modeling before launching a catering business and publishing her first cookbook, "Entertaining," helping build an empire that expanded into magazines, television, retail partnerships and home products. She became the first self-made female billionaire in the United States in 1999.

She has since authored more than 100 cookbooks, opened restaurants, become the oldest Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover model at age 81 and continues adding new ventures to her résumé, including her home intelligence app Hint, a skin care line and multiple brand partnerships.

Asked whether she already has everything she wants, Stewart pointed to her newest venture.

"No, I don't. I didn't have an app for my home, and so I'm making one," she said.

title: Labor MP Ed Husic taken to hospital with fractures and concussion after car accident

Husic to take ‘short’ period of leave after collision on Sydney motorway on Tuesday

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Labor MP Ed Husic was hospitalised this week after his car was involved in an accident with a truck travelling on Sydney’s M7 motorway.

The incident happened when the Chifley MP was travelling home from his electorate office, around 6.20pm on Tuesday, according to a spokesperson.

Husic was treated by paramedics at the scene and taken to hospital for assessment and treatment.

He was discharged on Wednesday with minor abrasions, fractures and a concussion.

A spokesperson for the MP said he was providing a statement to police about the incident.

“On medical advice, Mr Husic will take a short period of leave from parliamentary duties while he recovers.

“Mr Husic thanked the doctors, nurses and paramedics at Westmead hospital for providing him with outstanding care and thanked his friends and family for their support, especially during his hospital stay.”

Photos of the car show serious damage to the back driver’s side, with windows and windscreens smashed and airbags deployed.

Husic, the former industry minister, is expected to return to parliamentary duties soon. Parliament resumes in Canberra on Tuesday after the July winter break.

“Mr Husic was extremely grateful to walk away from the accident without more serious injury,” the spokesperson said.

NSW police have been contacted about the incident.

title: Erica Schwartz confirmed as new CDC chief amid US agency turmoil
excerpt: The United States Senate has confirmed Dr Erica Schwartz as the new head of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), as the federal health agency struggles with low morale and mass resign...
body_text:
The United States Senate has confirmed Dr Erica Schwartz as the new head of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), as the federal health agency struggles with low morale and mass resignations since President Donald Trump’s return to office.

The Senate confirmed Schwartz in a 51-44 vote on Wednesday, making the 54-year-old the agency’s first confirmed director since the Trump administration fired Susan Monarez last year over disputes regarding vaccine policy.

“With all the turmoil of the past two years, the CDC desperately needs stability, experienced leadership and a steadfast commitment to science,” Dr Georges Benjamin of the American Public Health Association said in a statement Wednesday.

Schwartz’s confirmation previously appeared in doubt as lawmakers questioned whether she would operate the agency based on scientific information or the demands of the president.

During a hearing before the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions last month, Republican Bill Cassidy questioned whether Schwartz would remain firm if pressured by the administration.

Cassidy later seemed to change his mind, stating that he had spoken with Schwartz and gained more confidence in her.

Layoffs and resignations at the CDC have resulted in the loss of about 3,000 workers, many of whom expressed frustration with vaccine policies promoted by Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr that fly in the face of longstanding scientific and public health consensus.

Schwartz was Trump’s third nominee for the position in just 18 months, and public health experts have expressed cautious optimism that she would bring a qualified background to the troubled agency.

She has medical and law degrees and previously served as deputy surgeon general, but will face considerable problems at the agency as the US experiences the worst Measles resurgence in three decades, falling childhood vaccination rates, and a cyclospora outbreak.

“Now, Dr Schwartz needs to prove that her leadership will serve science and not the whims of politicians. CDC needs a Director who will protect public health workers, defend evidence-based guidance, and refuse any directive that would undermine public safety,” the National Public Health Coalition, an organisation of former and current CDC workers, said in a statement on Wednesday.

Donald has been flirting with the idea of returning to his old team because they're stacked this season and about to embark on a chase for a Super Bowl championship, and he apparently likes the idea of being part of the journey.

title: Man and woman found dead in outback Queensland home after hours-long police siege

An hours-long siege has ended in tragedy after a man and woman were found dead ...
body_text:
A 45-year-old man and 23-year-old woman were found dead in the Charleville home after a near eight-hour siege by police

An hours-long siege has ended in tragedy after a man and woman were found dead in an outback home.

Several streets in Charleville, 600km west of Toowoomba in Queensland, were thrust into lockdown after police were called to investigate reports of a serious assault at the home around 6pm on Wednesday.

Residents in a three-street block were forced to retreat into their homes for nearly eight hours as specialist police surrounded the area.

The emergency public safety declaration was revoked just before 2am on Thursday.

A 45-year-old man and a 23-year-old woman were found dead in the home.

A crime scene was set up and a report is being prepared for the coroner.

No one else was injured during the incident.

The matter will be investigated by the ethical standards command.

title: American Airlines flight attendant's alleged killers tied to gang accused of preying on tourists: officials

Two men accused of d...
body_text:
FBI Special Agent in Charge Jason Hudson details the U.S. extradition of alleged Tren de Aragua leader Jose Enrique Martinez Flores during a news conference, Friday May 15, 2026.

Two men accused of drugging and killing an American Airlines flight attendant during a layover in Colombia have been arrested months after the slaying, authorities said, with the suspects allegedly tied to a gang known to prey on tourists.

Andrés Felipe Peña Corrales, 23, and William Olave Gamboa, 31, were captured in Peru in connection with the March killing of Eric Fernando Gutierrez Molina, 32, a Dallas-based flight attendant whose disappearance in Medellín sparked an international search.

Peña Corrales has since been transferred to Colombia to face charges, while Olave Gamboa remains in Peruvian custody awaiting extradition proceedings. Both men face charges including aggravated homicide and aggravated robbery in Colombia, according to authorities.

AMERICANS WARNED POPULAR TRAVEL ROUTES THIS SUMMER COULD CARRY CRIME AND KIDNAPPING RISKS

Two suspects arrested in Peru are seen in police custody after authorities accused them in the killing of American Airlines flight attendant Eric Fernando Gutierrez Molina. (U.S. Embassy Bogota)

A third suspect, María del Carmen González, 24, was arrested separately in Montería, Colombia. Investigators allege she was not directly involved in Gutierrez Molina’s killing but participated in withdrawing and moving money stolen from foreign victims as part of the group’s operation.

Colombian police identified all three suspects as alleged members of Los Goteros, a criminal organization accused of targeting foreign tourists by contacting them through dating apps, gaining their trust, drugging them and stealing money, jewelry and other valuables.

According to reporting by El Colombiano, investigators believe Gutierrez Molina was contacted through a dating app before meeting several people at a nightclub in Medellín’s El Poblado neighborhood.

The group later went to a hotel, where Gutierrez Molina and his coworker were allegedly drugged before their belongings were stolen and their financial accounts were accessed, the outlet reported.

The outlet also reported that scopolamine, sometimes called "Devil’s Breath" or "Dragon’s Breath," may have been used to incapacitate the victims, though authorities have not publicly confirmed toxicology findings in the case.

Gutierrez Molina was reportedly strangled, while his coworker survived.

DATING-APP CHARMER ACCUSED OF MURDER AFTER HISTORY OF DOMESTIC ARRESTS INVOLVING WOMEN HE MET ONLINE

Investigators allege the group accessed Gutierrez Molina’s bank accounts, stole other valuables and abandoned his body near Jericó, southwest of Medellín, where it was found five days later.

The arrests capped a months-long international investigation involving U.S. Homeland Security Investigations, Colombian prosecutors and Peruvian authorities.

"This successful outcome reflects the strong commitment of the United States, Colombia and Peru to work together to investigate and bring to justice a group of criminals in Colombia dedicated to the robbery and theft of U.S. citizens and ensure the safety of international travelers in the region," the U.S. Embassy in Colombia said in a joint statement.

The embassy also recognized the Mayor’s Office of Medellín, Colombia’s National Police and Peru’s National Police for their roles in the investigation.

EXCLUSIVE: ALLEGED $32M COVID-19 FRAUD FUGITIVE CAPTURED IN JAMAICA AND RETURNED TO US, FBI SAYS

Authorities say American Airlines flight attendant Eric Fernando Gutierrez Molina was drugged, robbed and killed after an overnight layover in Medellín, Colombia, in March 2026. (Edinson Arroyo/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Gutierrez Molina disappeared in March while on an overnight layover in Medellín before he was scheduled to continue to Miami.

Friends told local media at the time that he shared his location from an Airbnb near José María Córdova International Airport before communication suddenly stopped, prompting coworkers and family members to report him missing.

Days later, Medellín Mayor Federico Gutiérrez announced that authorities had recovered a body near Jericó. The remains were later identified as Gutierrez Molina.

Eric Fernando Gutierrez Molina, a 32-year-old flight attendant from Dallas, was reported missing in Colombia after he arrived on Saturday, March 21, according to reports. (CDColExt/X)

"We are heartbroken by the tragic passing of our colleague," American Airlines said in a statement previously provided to Fox News Digital.

"Our thoughts and support are with his family, loved ones and colleagues during this difficult time, and we are doing all we can to assist Colombian law enforcement in its investigation."

Authorities said investigators are working to determine whether additional foreign tourists were victimized by Los Goteros using the same alleged scheme.

Fox News Digital's Alex Koch and Alex Nitzberg contributed to this report.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

Clay Travis urges Elon Musk to up the reward for the potential game between the Las Vegas Aces & a high school boys team.

OutKick founder Clay Travis set the WNBA and sports world on fire recently when he made a compelling financial and social offer to the league and its best team, the Las Vegas Aces.

Play a state championship-winning high school boys basketball team of his choice, with $10 million up for grabs should they win.

This offer presented a compelling opportunity for the WNBA and the Aces to meaningfully increase their revenue, should they win the game, and more importantly, live up to their stated ideology and political beliefs. When Sophie Cunningham said in an interview that she wanted to protect girls, prevent males from competing in women's sports and keep locker rooms exclusively female, the outrage from many prominent personalities around the league was fierce and immediate.

CLAY TRAVIS UPS OFFER TO $10 MILLION FOR WNBA CHAMPION LAS VEGAS ACES TO PLAY HIGH SCHOOL BOYS BASKETBALL TEAM

Clay travis and sophie cunningham (Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images)

Players and coaches wore T-shirts expressing their support for males playing in women's sports. Her own coach said she wasn't educated on the science of males competing against women. A co-owner of the Seattle Storm was suspended for confronting young fans. And anti-biology WNBA fans have spent the past few Indiana Fever games booing Cunningham at every opportunity.

So far, though, both the league and the Aces have been dead silent when it comes to the golden opportunity Travis gave them. He joined "Don't @ Me with Dan Dakich" to talk about what led to the offer and how Elon Musk, of all people, could help.

CHERYL REEVE SENDS CLEAR MESSAGE TO SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM WITH ‘TRANS KIDS BELONG’ SHIRT DURING FEVER-LYNX GAME

"Sometimes the best way to respond to absurdity is to accept the absurd premise and advance it further to a larger degree of absurdity," Travis said. "Everyone with a functional brain knows that men are bigger, stronger and faster than women. And the whole reason women's sports exist is so women can compete because if we just had unisex sports, men would take all the spots and there would be no women's sports. So I said, as a way to point out this absurdity, I will give $10 million to a boys high school team, playing against WNBA champion Las Vegas Aces."

Las Vegas Aces center A'ja Wilson celebrates with teammates after Game 4 of the 2025 WNBA Finals at Mortgage Matchup Center. (Joe Camporeale/Imagn Images)

He also brought up that an even bigger dollar figure from someone with more resources, like Elon Musk, for example, could force the Aces hand.

"I would love it if somebody like Elon Musk would come in and say, 'hey, I'll make it 100 million,' you know. Because I think the dollar figure at 10 million, most people out there, if you thought you had a reasonable chance to win, would play, right? I mean, this is an unbelievable opportunity. I got boys, school team, coaches blowing up my DMs, blowing up my mentions by email, saying, our guys are saw your challenge. They can't wait to play."

It's one thing to stay radio silent on $10 million, but $100 million? That's 1/3 of the total estimated value of the Aces organization. It's three times their estimated annual revenue. How could they pass up that opportunity?

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!
