Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has shared a video of a street vendor being hunted by a drone before it exploded.

The man in the video verified by the BBC, 52-year-old street vegetable seller Yuriy, managed to survive the attack, but sustained shrapnel wounds and a concussion.

Known by some in Ukraine as "human safari", the deployment of remotely-operated drones against civilians has often been used by Russians to terrify residents of front line areas.

This particular drone attack happened in Kherson, which sits only a few miles from the front line.

Russia has repeatedly denied intentionally targeting civilians.

title: Vance to host Congress at White House to discuss legislative action on fraud
excerpt: Vice President JD Vance demands an end to widespread fraud, asserting it is critical for safeguarding taxpayer dollars and ensuring essential programs like Social Security serve their intended recipie...
body_text:
Vice President JD Vance demands an end to widespread fraud, asserting it is critical for safeguarding taxpayer dollars and ensuring essential programs like Social Security serve their intended recipients.

FIRST ON FOX: Vice President JD Vance will host members of Congress at the White House on Wednesday morning for a fraud task force meeting where members will discuss potential legislative action to address the administration’s crackdown on fraud.

A source familiar with the meeting told Fox News Digital that roughly 20 members from both the House and Senate are expected at the meeting. Vance will also detail how members can target fraud in the various states and districts they represent.

Vance has previously hosted meetings at the White House to address fraud with a number of attorneys general alongside other members from the administration involved in the task force led by Vance.

PENNSYLVANIA AG EXPLAINS WHY STATE LEADS NATION IN MEDICAID FRAUD CONVICTIONS WHILE OTHERS BATTLE MASS SCHEMES

Vice President JD Vance convened the first meeting of a new anti-fraud task force, blaming the Biden administration for weakening longstanding protections. (Photo by Heather Diehl/Getty Images)

"Our task force is using every tool at its disposal to end fraud once and for all. Congress has an important role to play in cracking down on fraudsters and protecting federal programs from abuse," a White House official told Fox News Digital. "President Trump, Vice President Vance, and all of the task force’s interagency partners will not relent until every fraudster is brought to justice."

On Tuesday, the Justice Department announced that it is expanding its Northeast Health Care Fraud Strike Force to Philadelphia as federal and state authorities target alleged Medicare and Medicaid fraud involving home healthcare services, adding Pennsylvania to a number of states across the country where the administration is honed in on fraud.

Federal and state law enforcement charged 19 defendants accused of participating in schemes involving more than $4 million in claims submitted to Medicare and Medicaid, according to a DOJ release obtained by Fox News.

On Sunday, Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday also announced a plea agreement involving the final defendant in a previously charged 21-defendant case tied to more than $1.7 million in claims.

Administrator for the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Dr. Mehmet Oz speaks ahead of U.S. Vice President JD Vance at the 128th Air Refueling Wing Hangar on July 08, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)

"The vice president’s task force continues to stop the flow of taxpayer funds before they fall into the hands of fraudsters and deliver savings to the American people," a spokesperson for Vice President JD Vance told Fox News Digital. "This is great momentum in the fight for the President’s War on Fraud."

WATCH: DR. OZ SAYS NEWSOM, OTHER BLUE STATES HAVE TURNED MEDICAID FRAUD INTO A 'FEATURE'

The task force has suspended payments to a number of healthcare providers who have been suspected of fraud across the country. As of May, Vance and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz withheld more than $1.4 billion in federal funding for home health and hospice providers nationwide.

In June, the Trump administration revealed new figures that show a drastic 7,100% spike in Medicare claims for skin substitutes in just six years, surging from $200 million to $14.4 billion from 2019 to 2025.

CMS identified 4,200 suspicious claims for skin substitutes, known as allografts, totaling $224 million in charges through May of this year.

"That's a lot of money," Oz said during a news conference in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, on Wednesday. "And that bankrupts not just hospital systems and physician groups, but it causes major problems across the entire landscape."

FEDERAL GOVERNMENT’S LANDLORD JOINS VANCE FRAUD CRACKDOWN AS WHITE HOUSE WIDENS HUNT: 'CRITICAL FORCE'

President Donald Trump established the task force through an executive order in May. He appointed Vance to the fraud crackdown team and various agencies and departments have been involved in rooting out widespread fraud.

"Vice President JD Vance and Republicans are doing a great job hunting down Fraud in the various States," Trump posted on Truth Social in June. "Billions of Dollars is being found, and we've just started!"

Preston Mizell is a writer with Fox News Digital covering breaking news.

title: Wisconsin brewery that promised free beer when Trump dies now plans 'half-price beer day' when McConnell dies
excerpt: ‘The Big Weekend Show’ co-hosts discuss a Wisconsin brewery facing renewed scrutiny after the White House Correspondents’ Dinner shooting and influencer Hasan Piker’s comments in a New York Times inte...
body_text:
‘The Big Weekend Show’ co-hosts discuss a Wisconsin brewery facing renewed scrutiny after the White House Correspondents’ Dinner shooting and influencer Hasan Piker’s comments in a New York Times interview.

The Wisconsin brewery that previously sparked outrage by promising free beer on "the day" President Donald Trump dies is once again drawing criticism after announcing plans for a "half-price beer day" when Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., dies.

In a post on Instagram on Monday, Minocqua Brewing Company said it plans to celebrate McConnell's death by offering beer at half price, arguing the longtime Kentucky Republican was responsible for "about half of all America's current problems."

"Well, folks, if our logic is right, we're supposed to get the news today that ‘Rigor Tortoise’ kicked the bucket about two months ago," the brewery said.

'THIS IS NOT NORMAL': AOC UNLOADS ON MCCONNELL'S PROLONGED ABSENCE

Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., is still recovering from a fall he suffered at home last month and is not "medically cleared" to return to the Senate, according to the Office of the Attending Physician.  (Courtesy of the Office of Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky.)

"Why today? Because so-called 'Establishment Democratic Hero' and modern day gutless member of the do-nothing opposition party — Governor Andy Beshear — failed to call a special election to replace the ‘ghost from Kentucky’ before August 3rd — which means by Kentucky law, the seat will go unfilled until January."

"When they announce that McConnell's Faustian dance has finally ended, we're gonna start serving our beer at ‘half price,’ because we promised #halfpricebeerday on the day they unplug the ventilator," the brewery continued.

McConnell, who is 84, has not been in the Senate for more than a month after being hospitalized for a fall in his home.

Last week, Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear demanded that McConnell prove he is fit to continue serving in Congress after a lengthy hospital stay or resign from office.

"I am calling on you to directly and verbally address the people of Kentucky and provide proof of your capacity to serve, or resign," Beshear wrote in a letter to McConnell, obtained by Fox News Digital.

WISCONSIN DEM'S BAR LAMENTS 'WE ALMOST GOT FREE BEER DAY' FOR TRUMP ASSASSINATION

The Minocqua Brewing Company is under fire again for its "free beer day" campaign, openly anticipating the death of Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky. (Google Earth)

In the post, the brewery said it chose the name "half-price beer day" because it blamed McConnell for "about half" of the country's current problems while noting that its previously announced "free beer day" promotion remained reserved for "someone more special."

The brewery also promoted "half-price beer day" T-shirts and encouraged supporters to wear them when the event eventually takes place.

Minocqua Brewing Company, which in a January social media post appeared to suggest it would give free beer to patrons if Trump was killed, while not explicitly using his name, is currently fighting getting their permit revoked.

The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reported on July 27 that Wisconsin's Department of Revenue sent a notice to liberal activist and brewery owner Kirk Bangstad announcing plans to revoke the brewery’s permit.

'FREE BEER' FOR TRUMP DEATH DEM ACTIVIST RUNNING FOR WISCONSIN GOV: 'I WILL WIN' IF THEY SILENCE ME

The Minocqua Brewing Company in Wisconsin has a history of pushing progressive politics. (Screenshot/Google Earth)

The Sentinel reported that state regulators pursued revoking Bangstad's alcohol license after authorities seized canned beer from his company in June, alleging it had been transported from Illinois without the required permits and taxes. The paper also reported that Bangstad criticized the proposed action as an excessive response, arguing the alleged tax violations did not warrant shutting down his business.

The revocation of the beer permit was set to go into effect on Tuesday, but a spokesperson for Wisconsin's Department of Revenue told Fox News Digital in a statement that "Minocqua Brewing Company has filed an administrative appeal, and, therefore, the permit will not be revoked, pending the outcome of the administrative appeal."

Bangstad, the owner of the brewery, is also the founder of the Minocqua Brewing Company SuperPAC, which "aims to remove Republican federal and state elected officials who perpetuated the election lies that caused the Insurrection of January 6, 2021, and whose downplaying of the seriousness of COVID-19 caused so many unnecessary deaths in our country," according to the brewery’s website.

Fox News Digital reached out to Minocqua Brewing Company, Gov. Beshear's office and Sen. McConnell's office for comment but did not immediately receive responses.

Rachel del Guidice is a culture reporter for Fox News covering the intersection of politics, faith, family, and American culture.

title: DOJ sends monitors to Michigan poll sites as lawmakers warn of partisan aim
excerpt: The US Department of Justice (DOJ) has announced it has sent federal monitors to polls in four Democratic-leaning cities in Michigan, amid warnings that the administration of United States President D...
body_text:
The US Department of Justice (DOJ) has announced it has sent federal monitors to polls in four Democratic-leaning cities in Michigan, amid warnings that the administration of United States President Donald Trump could use such monitors for partisan aims.

The DOJ announced the monitors would be present during Michigan’s primary vote on Tuesday as part of an effort to “ensure free and fair elections nationwide”, according to Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon.

“The Department of Justice is devoting extensive resources to ensure uniform and nondiscriminatory monitoring,” it said.

While the department has for decades overseen an election monitoring programme to ensure compliance with federal civil rights laws, lawmakers and advocates have raised concerns over how such a programme could be used under the current administration.

Trump has for years alleged, without evidence, that US elections have been marred by widespread fraud. He has never acknowledged his 2020 loss to US President Joe Biden.

Michigan has played a major role in those claims.

In a primetime speech delivered in mid-July, Trump re-upped a previously concluded probe into alleged voter fraud in the city of Muskegon as he called on the FBI to reinvestigate the case. Local officials had already determined that several voter registration forms had been fraudulently filled out in the city by employees of a consulting firm attempting to falsely reach their quotas.

No fraudulent ballots were cast in connection with the fake voter registration forms. State officials have highlighted the situation as proof of the efficacy of their election security practices.

The announcement on Tuesday came weeks after the Department of Justice said it planned to monitor 15 jurisdictions across six states: Arizona, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, New Hampshire and Virginia. The DOJ has said it will expand the use of monitors leading into November.

The department did not give a reason for why the four Michigan cities –  Detroit, Hamtramck, Lansing, and East Lansing – were selected.

Detroit, Lansing and East Lansing are all heavily Democratic leaning. Hamtramck, considered the first Muslim-majority city in the US, has historically leaned Democratic, but has shifted increasingly Republican in recent years.

Residents of the state on Tuesday were casting ballots to determine party nominees in local, state and US Congressional races for the midterm election in November.

Key races include a fierce Democratic Senate race, with progressive Abdul El-Sayed hoping to defeat US Representative Haley Stevens, widely viewed as a weathervane for the party’s future.

Voters will also decide the candidates for the gubernatorial race, with Trump-backed US Representative John James facing off with former presidential candidate Perry Johnson on the Republican side, as Democrat Jocelyn Benson, the current Michigan state secretary, is expected to sail to victory in her party’s primary.

In a letter to the Department of Justice dated Monday, 10 Democratic senators asked for assurances that FBI monitors deployed across the country will not “target jurisdictions in a partisan manner; discourage voter participation or interfere with the voting process; or pressure, harass, or interfere with state and local election officials as they do their jobs”.

They noted the wider context in which the monitors are being deployed, including efforts by the Trump administration to obtain state voter rolls. On Tuesday, a judge ruled the administration could not access Colorado’s voter data, the latest in a string of similar rulings.

Trump has also called for Republicans to “nationalise” elections. Under the US Constitution, state governments administer elections, in a system of decentralisation that advocates have long argued protects against wholesale interference.

The senators said that the DOJ has characterised the monitors as “routine” and “non-partisan”.

“However, it would be remiss not to acknowledge concerns that monitors are being deployed disproportionately to jurisdictions in states governed by Democratic leaders or with Democratic chief election officials,” they wrote.

“Moreover, election monitors are being deployed in the context of President Trump’s ongoing threats to nationalise, militarise, and otherwise interfere with the conduct of free and fair elections.”

title: Washington wildfire arson suspect previously charged with first-degree murder, records show
excerpt:
Fox News’ Sarah Alegre reports on wildfires across Spokane County, Washington, destroying hundreds of structures and forcing thousands of residents to evacuate on ‘Special Report.’

The man accused of...
body_text:
Fox News’ Sarah Alegre reports on wildfires across Spokane County, Washington, destroying hundreds of structures and forcing thousands of residents to evacuate on ‘Special Report.’

The man accused of setting the largest of the wildfires that have destroyed hundreds of buildings and forced tens of thousands of people from their homes in eastern Washington was previously charged with first-degree murder before pleading guilty to a reduced manslaughter charge, court records show.

Aaron F. Farinacci, 37, was arrested Monday on suspicion of first-degree arson in connection with the Old Trails Fire, the largest of three blazes burning in and around Spokane, Washington's second-largest city.

The fires have destroyed at least 700 buildings and forced about 67,000 people to evacuate. Authorities have not alleged any connection between Farinacci and the other two fires, which remain under investigation.

WASHINGTON MAN ARRESTED ON ARSON CHARGE TIED TO DEVASTATING SPOKANE WILDFIRE

The arrest came hours after Washington Gov. Jay Inslee, a Democrat, pointed to climate change as firefighters battled the region's destructive wildfires.

Aaron F. Farinacci was arrested on suspicion of first-degree arson in connection with the Old Trails Fire in eastern Washington. (Arizona Department of Corrections)

"Climate change isn't some existential global thing," Inslee said Monday. "It's our neighbors. It's our friends."

Court records reviewed by Fox News Digital show Farinacci was initially charged with first-degree murder and aggravated assault in a 2010 Arizona homicide before pleading guilty in 2012 to reduced charges of manslaughter and aggravated assault.

The Associated Press reported that Farinacci, then 21, fatally shot his father during an argument over washing dishes in Mesa, Arizona, in 2010. Farinacci also shot himself but survived.

A Maricopa County judge sentenced Farinacci to 12 years in prison after he pleaded guilty to manslaughter and aggravated assault. Arizona Department of Corrections records show he was released on Dec. 23, 2020.

Aaron Farinacci, 37, was charged with first-degree arson. (Spokane County Sheriff’s Office)

Less than six years after his release from prison, Farinacci again found himself accused of a major crime.

The Spokane County Sheriff's Office said Major Crimes detectives and Washington State Department of Natural Resources fire investigators identified Farinacci as the suspect after developing probable cause during the investigation.

Detectives obtained arrest and search warrants before taking Farinacci into custody without incident at his Spokane residence, where he was booked into the Spokane County Jail on suspicion of first-degree arson.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

Spokane County Sheriff John Nowels said witnesses reported seeing a man – later identified as Farinacci – acting suspiciously near where the fire started. After returning home and noticing smoke rising from the same area, they flagged down an Airway Heights police officer and provided investigators with a physical description of the man and the clothing he was wearing.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

Firefighters respond to a wildfire near Spokane, Washington, on Aug. 2, 2026. (South Pend Oreille Fire Rescue / FOX Weather)

Deputies initially detained and questioned Farinacci before releasing him as first responders focused on evacuating residents threatened by the rapidly growing fire, Nowels said.

As detectives reviewed witness statements, body camera footage and evidence gathered with fire investigators, they developed probable cause to arrest Farinacci.

Chimneys are the only structures remaining in a residential neighborhood after a wildfire hit the northern part of Spokane, Washington, Monday, Aug. 3, 2026. (AP Photo / Lindsey Wasson)

When deputies first contacted Farinacci, he was carrying waterproof matches and a butane lighter, investigators said. Fire investigators later determined the blaze was consistent with dry grass being ignited by a match or lighter.

Nowels said the first-degree arson charge reflected the evidence investigators currently have but cautioned that additional charges could be considered as the investigation continues and authorities assess the full scope of the fire's destruction.

Allen Sather stands in front of his 1968 Chevrolet C20 at the duplex he rented on W. Indian Trail Rd. that burned in a wildfire in Spokane, Washington, Sunday, Aug. 2, 2026. (AP Photo / Young Kwak)

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

The sheriff credited observant residents with helping investigators quickly identify the suspect.

"As it happens in so many critical cases, it was citizens who were paying attention to their surroundings, being aware and willing to step up and say something that led to the relatively quick apprehension of Mr. Farinacci," Nowels said.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

Greg Wehner is a reporter for Fox News Digital covering U.S. news and crime, with a focus on breaking developments, law enforcement, public safety and major stories shaping communities across the country.

Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A New York police official is being accused of serving as the getaway driver for her son in an apparent gang shooting in New York City, the New York Post reported Tuesday.

Police sources told the Post that Jennifer Lackard, a deputy police commissioner with the Mount Vernon Police Department, was arrested along with her son, Chase Lackard, 20, at their home Tuesday morning. Authorities said Chase was charged with shooting at rival gang members near the Bronx Criminal Court in late June.

Sources told the Post that Chase ran to his mother in her car after the shooting, and she sped off.

NANCY GUTHRIE RANSOM DEMANDS RELEASED BY PIMA COUNTY SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT IN BID TO IDENTIFY SENDER

Jennifer Lackard served as a deputy police commissioner with the Mount Vernon Police Department. ((Theodore Parisienne / New York Daily News via Getty Images) + Mt. Vernon Police Department)

Both the mother and son have been charged with attempted murder, attempted assault, criminal possession of a firearm, conspiracy and reckless endangerment.

The Mount Vernon Police Department said Tuesday that Lackard had been terminated effectively immediately.

"The allegations are unrelated to her duties with the Mount Vernon Police Department and do not stem from any conduct associated with the Department or the performance of her official responsibilities," the department wrote on social media.

ROMANIAN NATIONAL LEARNS FATE FOR SWATTING US OFFICIALS, INCLUDING MEMBERS OF CONGRESS, JUDGES

Police respond to a shooting in the Bronx in August 2025. (WNYW)

The incident was far from Chase's first run-in with law enforcement. He was shot by police in 2024 after allegedly wielding a gun during an argument.

He was also shot once before in 2023 by three other youths during a dispute on a bus. Chase is allegedly a member of the "Slutty Gang," according to the Post.

He reportedly demanded to know what gang the other youths belonged to and then attempted to drag one of them off the bus before being shot in the chest.

Anders Hagstrom is a reporter with Fox News Digital covering national politics and major breaking news events.

excerpt:
Supporters gathered outside the Indiana Fever game in Portland on Friday night were met with counterprotesters as Sophie Cunningham's comments on trans athletes continue to take over the WNBA.

Few th...
body_text:
Supporters gathered outside the Indiana Fever game in Portland on Friday night were met with counterprotesters as Sophie Cunningham's comments on trans athletes continue to take over the WNBA.

Few things in sports can get a fan's nerves up like being told you get to take a half-court shot at an NBA or WNBA game for cash or a car.

Sure, you could, by some miracle, make the shot, but you're more likely to embarrass yourself in front of an arena full of people... at least the ones who are still in their seats and aren't in line for a beer or the bathroom.

But, at least we can all be sure that if you take a shot, the odds of it being a worse display than one put on by a Portland Fire fan over the weekend are very, very low.

WNBA COMMISSIONER CATHY ENGELBERT CAUGHT HITTING LAUGHABLY BAD GOLF SHOT AFTER ALLEGEDLY DITCHING INTERVIEW

A recent attempt at the Portland Fire's half-court shot competition is going, and not for good reasons. (Photo by Ali Gradischer/Getty Images))

The Fire (whose logo I only just realized is a flaming rose. Seriously, I've had an easier time decoding death metal band logos) have a half-court shot competition according to their website. It's sponsored by Toyota, meaning that draining the shot earns you a brand new Toyota.

Hopefully a Land Cruiser. Those are cool.

One fan got this golden opportunity on Sunday when the Fire took on the Los Angeles Sparks and... well, let's just say that Portland area Toyota dealers were not sweating it on this one.

ATLANTA BRAVES FAN TAUNTS THE FREEZE WITH A BLOWN KISS AND GETS PASSED IN SPECTACULAR FASHION

Rule No. 1 of half-court shots should be that whatever you do, your biggest goal is to at least hit the backboard. I'd argue it's much better to airmail that ball into the club level seats than it is to barely get it past the free throw line.

That's a rough look as it is, but imagine putting every last drop of mustard you have on the ball to the point that you go scrawling across that flaming rose logo (seriously, did anyone else not pick up on that at first?). That tells the entire crowd in attendance you gave it your all... which is normally good, but that's not enough "all."

Not to pile on this guy, but regulation WNBA basketballs are also smaller and lighter than their NBA counterparts. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/NBAE via Getty Images)

The big winner in all of this is that guy's glasses. Talk about a snug fit. Those things were on there!

That was maybe the only thing that went right for him. If those specs had gone clattering across the hardwood, I think he would've had to change his name, move out of Portland, and start rooting for a new WNBA team.

Luckily for him, he wasn't the only loser as the Fire fell to the Sparks that night 106-101.

title: French trans phenom Julie Tétart looks WNBA-ready — so why hasn’t the ‘inclusive’ league called?
excerpt: WNBA star Sophie Cunningham shares her powerful message about standing up for girls' sports amidst criticism. She reiterates her commitment to truth and protecting young girls in locker rooms and spor...
body_text:
WNBA star Sophie Cunningham shares her powerful message about standing up for girls' sports amidst criticism. She reiterates her commitment to truth and protecting young girls in locker rooms and sports from competing against biological men, despite receiving negative feedback about her stance on transgender athletes. This comes after she retweeted a CBS Sports host years ago.

French trans basketball player Julie Tétart is waiting for a call from one of the inclusive WNBA teams who needs a 6'3 scoring and rebounding machine.

During the 2025-26 season for a club team in Monaco, Tétart dominated the second-tier French women's basketball Ligue 2 by dropping 21 points per game while grabbing 20 rebounds. The biological male, who came out as trans in October 2021, led the league in both categories. It was as season unlike any the Ligue 2 had ever seen.

Julie Tetart, a player for Monaco, is pictured during a French second-division basketball game in Reims, France, on Jan. 10, 2026. (ZUMA PRESS)

With those numbers, the WNBA should be knocking down Tétart's door, right?

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SPEAKS OUT TO PROTECT GIRLS AS WNBA ALL-STAR INITIATIVE BACKS ‘GENDER-EXPANSIVE’ GROUP

"If they contact me, I won't say no. But you have to be realistic: I'm old, and there are far better players than me!" the overly humble 34-year-old Tétart told OutKick in French over Instagram direct messages on Monday.

Tétart's season was so dominant that French media was stunned when the shredded center didn't win league MVP honors. The season was still good enough to win Player of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year and Domestic Player of the Year.

Woke WNBA fans swear there's no clear and present trans danger to biological women. They swear this is some sort of delusion cooked up by MAGA.

RILEY GAINES SAYS WNBA IS 'HELLBENT' ON BEING AN ACTIVIST ORGANIZATION OVER A BASKETBALL LEAGUE

Meanwhile, Tétart destroyed Ligue 2 so badly that there were collusion allegations being made against league captains and coaches who voted on the MVP award.

Those same voters are alleged to have excluded 43-year-old trans player Aurore Pautou (14.4 PPG, 7.7 RPG) from winning postseason awards. French trans groups are furious. "Despite top-tier athletic performance on the court during the 2025/2026 season by Julie and Aurore, voters for the Ligue 2 Féminine de Basket Awards deliberately decided not to grant them any awards," activist group TRANSpire cried on Instagram.

Julie Tetart, a transgender player for Monaco and the top player in the French second-division basketball league, is pictured in Reims, France, on Jan. 10, 2026. (ZUMA PRESS)

Former WNBA player Audrey Sauret, who's French, spoke out in April after the MVP drama and sounded a warning to leagues around the world as to what's coming if they don't protect biological females.

"Ligue 2 serves as a kind of testing ground, to introduce trendy ideas, but by allowing them to participate in professional competitions, we create unfair competition, especially for younger players," Sauret wrote. "This can close doors and discourage aspiring athletes. This situation risks becoming commonplace, even if it’s regulated. Men and women aren’t built the same way. Changing hormones doesn’t erase gender differences. I regret that this issue wasn’t addressed much sooner."

TRANS ATHLETE WINS NEW YORK STATE GIRLS' SHOT PUT TITLE, BEATING SECOND PLACE BY MORE THAN 2 FEET

During a March game that should've been a trans showdown, Tétart had 21 points and 30 rebounds, which was a new league record, breaking the previous record of 25 rebounds (Tétart held that record, as well), but Pautou didn't play.

Julie Tetart, a transgender player for Monaco, is pictured during a French second-division basketball game in Reims, France, on Jan. 10, 2026. Tetart is the best player in the French second division basketball league. (ZUMAPRESS.com)

The question we had for Tétart was simple: Would you ever consider trying out for the inclusive WNBA? The trans scoring and rebounding machine seemed confused at first before realizing we were 100% serious.

"Obviously, it's a childhood dream just like for any female basketball player, but unfortunately, it's not possible," the French native wrote back.

Wait a minute, why not? The WNBA is inclusive. What are we missing here?

WNBA COMMISSIONER VOWS TO CRACK DOWN ON 'RACISM, MISOGYNY,' DODGES BIG QUESTIONS AT ALL-STAR PRESS CONFERENCE

"The league, yes. The country, no, haha," Tétart fired back while hinting at some sort of problem with Donald Trump's presidency.

When pressed on what would need to change politically in the U.S., Tétart stopped playing games with me, finally admitting that if a WNBA call came, it would be time to talk business: "I won't say no."

As for Sophie Cunningham's stance that biological males need to stay out of women's sports, I gave Tétart a chance to respond. "Aucun," the French stat stuffer replied.

Imagine a Tétart vs. Cunningham matchup in 2027. It's time for the WNBA to once and for all prove just how inclusive it is. Tétart's DMs are wide open.

Joe Kinsey is the Senior Director of Content of OutKick.

title: Guatemala volcano eruption prompts evacuation of hundreds of people
excerpt:
Eruption of the Fuego volcano sends lava and ash nearly four miles into the sky as country declares alert warning

Hundreds of people living on the slopes of Guatemala’s Fuego volcano have evacuated t...
body_text:
Eruption of the Fuego volcano sends lava and ash nearly four miles into the sky as country declares alert warning

Hundreds of people living on the slopes of Guatemala’s Fuego volcano have evacuated their homes after a huge eruption spewed lava and plumes of ash.

Central America’s most active volcano erupted on Monday morning, with conditions intensifying by nightfall and prompting authorities to issue the country’s second-most severe alert warning.

By Tuesday, rivers of lava were streaming down the 3,763-metre (12,346-foot) volcano, which is located less than 100 kilometres (62 miles) from Guatemala City. Ash rose six kilometres (3.73 miles) into the red sky.

“Since early morning it was active. That night, the alarm was raised that we needed to evacuate,” a local resident, Alejandro Garcia, 68, told AFP.

Villagers left of their own accord out of fear, Garcia said, describing terrifying scenes of lava tumbling down the mountainside.

Firefighters said they transported at least 350 residents of the El Porvenir and Las Lajitas villages to the eastward San Juan Alotenango municipality.

Evacuees are staying in a community hall, where makeshift beds have been set up, while the number of people taken to other nearby towns remains unknown.

“If there were any chance of moving to a different house, it would be better, because you’re always afraid since the volcano doesn’t give any warning,” Lidia Ortiz, 40, said at the shelter.

Escuintla, to the south, was sheltering dozens more families, including children, local authorities reported.

“If an evacuation is ordered or conditions pose a risk to your life, follow the principle of self-evacuation,” Conred spokesperson Valeria Urizar said in a video posted on social media.

The country’s Institute of Volcanology warned of hot volcanic debris flows down Fuego’s slopes, with communities on the western and southern flanks at the greatest risk.

Fuego had been erupting for 23 hours straight by Tuesday morning, it said, although the intensity was easing.

“We’ve already gotten used to having the volcano constantly active, but this time it was really too much,” 50-year-old resident Sonia Vasquez said.

Guatemalan authorities urged “precautions with air traffic”, but there has so far been no impact on the capital’s international airport.

The education ministry ordered the suspension of face-to-face classes in communities within two municipalities near the volcano.

Traffic police also closed a road encircling the mountain range that connects the south coast with the colonial city of Antigua, the country’s main tourist destination and a Unesco World Heritage site.

Guatemala lies on the Pacific ‘ring of fire’ and experiences frequent seismic and volcanic activity.

There have been several such mass evacuations in recent years because Fuego erupted.

Authorities evacuated more than 500 people last year after Fuego spurted gas and ash, with residents moved to shelters from communities near the crater.

Another eruption in 2023 pushed around 1,200 people to evacuate.

In 2018, 215 people were killed and a similar number left missing when rivers of lava poured down Fuego’s slopes and destroyed a village.

title: Senate Democrat’s report says major banks ‘looked the other way’ on Epstein
excerpt:
A new report by a top Democrat in the United States Senate presents evidence that Wall Street banks “looked the other way” when it came to the behaviour of disgraced late financier Jeffrey Epstein.

T...
body_text:
A new report by a top Democrat in the United States Senate presents evidence that Wall Street banks “looked the other way” when it came to the behaviour of disgraced late financier Jeffrey Epstein.

The report, published on Tuesday, was released by Senator Ron Wyden, the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee.

He wrote that the banks’ actions “allowed Epstein to have ready access to the mountains of cash he used to lure, harbor and transport his victims” as part of his alleged sex-trafficking ring.

Wyden added that bank records and public court filings reviewed by his team “detail a shocking pattern of the biggest Wall Street banks in the country choosing to ignore clear evidence of sex trafficking and money laundering, just to keep a wealthy client on the books”.

Beyond shielding Epstein from federal scrutiny, the report says the banks may also have been in violation of federal anti-money laundering laws that would have required them to report the suspicious behaviour.

Wyden also took aim at the Department of Justice and the Department of the Treasury, insinuating they did not perform their due diligence in their investigation of Epstein.

The financier was found dead of an apparent suicide in a New York jail in 2019 as he awaited trial on federal sex trafficking charges.

The report comes as both Republican and Democratic critics question why the Epstein investigation has yielded so few US criminal charges, save for those against Epstein and his longtime confidante Ghislaine Maxwell.

Several foreign law enforcement agencies, by contrast, have opened investigations into individuals over their alleged ties to Epstein, including the United Kingdom’s Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, formerly known as Prince Andrew.

Wyden called Tuesday’s report “a ready-made roadmap for prosecutors, investigators and members of Congress to finally start holding the Epstein class accountable”.

The report cited the conduct of JPMorgan Chase, Deutsche Bank and Bank of America, naming several bankers at the institutions it said should be investigated. It also named several Epstein “accomplices” who allegedly “moved significant amounts of cash around the world on Epstein’s behalf”.

The investigators said Bank of America “likely violated” federal anti-money laundering laws by failing to report $170m in payments to Epstein from billionaire investor Leon Black.

Among its other allegations, the report charged that JPMorgan Chase executives “coached Epstein on how to withdraw cash through shell companies instead of his personal accounts, helping him conceal information from compliance personnel and government regulators”.

All three banks previously reached multimillion-dollar settlements with Epstein survivors, under which they admitted no wrongdoing.

“We take our legal and regulatory obligations seriously and, as we have previously said, the bank did not facilitate wrongdoing,” a Bank of America spokesman said in response to Wyden’s report.

A spokesperson for Deutsche Bank said it “regrets our historical connection with Jeffrey Epstein”.

“We have cooperated with regulatory and law enforcement agencies regarding their investigations and have been transparent in addressing deficiencies and investing in strengthening our control environment in parallel,” the spokesperson said in a statement.

JPMorgan Chase, which also reached a settlement with Epstein survivors in 2023, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Democrats have seized on the Trump administration’s handling of investigative files related to Epstein as a source of criticism. But the issue has also gained rare bipartisan support.

Last November, the Senate and House of Representatives passed a law requiring the Justice Department to release all the files within 30 days. The Justice Department said that all files had been released as of January, though they have been criticised for the level of redactions they contain.

Lawmakers have since introduced a new bill that would impose criminal penalties if full, unredacted access to the Epstein files is not granted to survivors or local and state law enforcement conducting relevant investigations.

Wyden’s report contains some of the most substantial allegations about the Epstein files since the January release, and comes just three months before the midterm elections in November.

For his part, Trump has repeatedly denied any knowledge of Epstein’s crimes, maintaining the pair’s well-documented friendship had ended in the early 2000s.

His vice president, JD Vance, recently said the administration was not trying to withhold any information, but that it had “screwed up” its public communications.

Several polls have shown Americans remain deeply unsatisfied with the level of transparency and accountability surrounding the Epstein files.

title: Video shows Russian drone chasing Ukrainian street vendor in 'human safari' attack
excerpt:
Drone appears to chase Ukrainian man and detonate near him

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has shared a video on social media of a drone hunting down a man in southern Ukraine, saying it showe...
body_text:
Drone appears to chase Ukrainian man and detonate near him

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has shared a video on social media of a drone hunting down a man in southern Ukraine, saying it showed an instance of a Russian "safari" attack against civilians.

The video shows the drone pursuing a street vendor on a city street in the Kherson region. The man moves away from the drone hovering above, before it chases him as he runs around a white van. Eventually, the drone swoops down on him and explodes on impact.

The man escaped with multiple shrapnel wounds, concussion and trauma, a doctor said.

Sometimes called "human safari", the deployment of remotely-operated drones against civilians has often been used by Russians to terrify residents of front line areas in Ukraine.

"The world must see this," Zelensky wrote on Telegram. "It must see every piece of evidence that Russia has gone mad, and every fact that Russian soldiers are enjoying killings and tormenting people."

The video showed a "barbaric war crime", said Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha.

The safaris were a "deliberate and systemic Russian strategy," Sybiha said. "The sadist operating this drone knows full well that he is targeting a civilian."

He added the attack was part of a deliberate Russian campaign to intimidate civilians and demanded international condemnation.

The Kherson regional governor later posted a video showing the man - identified as Yuriy, a 52-year-old street vegetable vendor - speaking from a hospital bed following the drone attack.

Yuriy said he and his wife had started to lay out crates of vegetables next to his van when he heard a distinctive buzzing sound overhead.

When his wife ran away, the drone turned to him instead. He held up some heads of garlic towards the drone's camera to show the operator that he was not trying to film it.

"It could see that I had tomatoes out, some cucumbers and eggplants laid out on the floor," Yuriy said. "It even ducked under the umbrella when I was running away round the other side."

BBC Verify geolocated the video to a market space beside a roundabout in the Tavriiskyi district in northern Kherson. It is not clear who filmed the attack, or how - but the earliest public copy BBC Verify found was shared by a pro-Ukrainian Instagram account on Tuesday morning.

"Safari" attacks have long been carried out by Russian troops in Kherson, which sits only a few miles from the front line.

A 2025 UN report said it had found Russian armed forces "recurrently killed and injured civilians" in the area by using drones to target them.

The videos filmed by the drones before they explode on to their targets are often posted online, allowing thousands to witness the last moments of the terrified victims.

"Posting videos of civilians being killed and injured amounts to the war crime of outrages upon personal dignity," the UN said.

Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 and denies targeting civilians.

Additional reporting by Richard Irvine-Brown, BBC Verify

title: Mass funeral held in Gaza for victims of 2023 Israeli strike
excerpt:
Remains of 112 victims, including 40 children, recovered from rubble more than two years after residential block was destroyed

Mourners gathered in central Gaza on Tuesday for a mass funeral for 112 ...
body_text:
Remains of 112 victims, including 40 children, recovered from rubble more than two years after residential block was destroyed

Mourners gathered in central Gaza on Tuesday for a mass funeral for 112 people, including 40 children, who were killed in 2023 in one of the deadliest Israeli strikes of the Gaza war.

Their bodies could not be recovered until now because of Israel’s continuing strikes, which have slowed, though not halted, since the ceasefire in October.

Hundreds of people gathered around more than 100 coffins wrapped in Palestinian flags and arranged in rows on the ground in Deir al-Balah. Mourners prayed for the victims before carrying the bodies through rubble-lined streets and past destroyed buildings for burial in a nearby cemetery.

The victims had been among more than 300 people killed on 22 November 2023, when Israeli warplanes demolished a residential block in Gaza City. The bodies of only about 40 people could be recovered by people at the scene, who dug through smouldering rubble with their bare hands and basic tools.

Last weekend, Gaza’s civil defence dug through the levelled apartment block and recovered the remains of a further 112 victims, including women and children. It said 157 people were still missing after the attack.

The ceasefire that was established in October – which has not stopped Israeli bombing of Gaza – has allowed first responders to dig through the rubble where thousands of remains are still buried across the territory.

At least 7,400 people have been reported by relatives as still buried under the rubble, Zaher al-Waheidi, head of the Gaza health ministry’s records department, told the Associated Press. He added that the true number was probably thousands higher because some strikes had killed entire families, leaving no loved ones to report them missing.

A UN commission, Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International have found that Israel committed genocide in Gaza. In June, a UN commission found that Israel was continuing to commit genocide in Gaza and that its security forces “deliberately targeted and killed” Palestinian children.

At least 26 Palestinians were killed by Israeli strikes over the weekend, despite the announcement of a deal intended to solidify the second phase of the October ceasefire. The killings happened just a few days after the US president, Donald Trump, hailed the latest deal – intended to lead to Hamas disarming and Israeli troops withdrawing from Gaza – as a “historic agreement”.

More than 73,000 people in Gaza have been killed by Israel since 7 October 2023, including more than 1,250 people since the October ceasefire.

Israel launched the war in Gaza after a Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 which saw around 1,200 people killed and 251 taken hostage. Five Israeli soldiers have been killed since the October ceasefire.

Ceasefire talks intended to move the agreement into a second phase have largely stalled. Senior Hamas officials said that the group’s disarmament is conditional on Israel withdrawing from the strip. Israel said that it had “serious security concerns” about last week’s agreement.

Most of the Gaza Strip remains in ruins, with the vast majority of its 2 million population displaced and living through a humanitarian crisis in unsanitary, overcrowded tent cities.

title: Trump administration reportedly drafting ban on Chinese datacenter components
excerpt:
Trump’s FCC is developing a measure to bar US imports of new models of Chinese datacenter devices, sources say

The Trump administration is reportedly drafting a ban on US imports of new models of Chi...
body_text:
Trump’s FCC is developing a measure to bar US imports of new models of Chinese datacenter devices, sources say

The Trump administration is reportedly drafting a ban on US imports of new models of Chinese datacenter components, in the latest sign US authorities are scrambling to respond to the rapid development of AI technology in China.

Four people familiar with the matter told Reuters that the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), which oversees the US ⁠telecommunications industry, is developing a measure to bar imports of new ​Chinese optical transceivers, which allow data to travel over fiber-optic cables at the speed of light within datacenters. Officials hope to publish the measure this year, according to Reuters.

The FCC could still modify or shelve the restriction, Reuters reported. But the deliberations are the latest example the Trump administration is increasingly focused on limiting Chinese technological incursions into cutting-edge US industries.

The US has long been at the forefront of the AI industry, with companies like OpenAI, Anthropic and Google driving the development of models, and chipmakers like Nvidia commanding the chip supply chain.

But advancements in China’s artificial intelligence, chip manufacturing and robotics technologies have rattled markets, caused divisions among US tech moguls and left the Trump administration scrambling to respond.

Chinese companies are some of the biggest manufacturers of components necessary for datacenters, with the country’s optical transceiver industry controlling a majority of the global market for the technology. US tech companies have committed trillions of dollars to build out American AI infrastructure. Plans for that buildout are broadly falling behind schedule, however, while China attempts to catch up with its own massive development of datacenters.

Chinese datacenter components are of concern because they could allow Chinese firms to steal ⁠data, install malware or disrupt service in the US if they were embedded in US infrastructure, experts say.

Last month, the FCC announced a ban on China’s advanced humanoid robots. The Trump administration is also reportedly mulling whether to restrict the use of Chinese open-source AI models.

US officials have cited threats to the US supply chain and fears over national security risks as rationale for those measures. Scott Bessent, the US treasury secretary, has also suggested that China could be sanctioned for theft of US data and intellectual property.

The White House and FCC did not respond to requests for comment.

The Chinese embassy in Washington told Reuters that Beijing ‌urges the US to “heed the objective and rational voices of the business communities in both countries” and “stop smearing Chinese companies and threatening them with sanctions”.

“China will take all necessary measures in response to any action that causes material harm to its interests,” it added.

Some Trump administration officials have been citing the example of Huawei, a Chinese telecom company, to argue for the new restrictions. Huawei’s equipment was so deeply embedded in US infrastructure that efforts to remove it were difficult.

A US ‌ban on new models of Chinese datacenter devices would probably hit China’s Zhongji Innolight, one of the biggest global sellers of transceivers, which was added to the Pentagon’s list of alleged Chinese military-backed companies in June.

title: US and Qatar report progress on Iran ceasefire and reopening Hormuz strait
excerpt:
Optimism echoes Trump’s claims on Monday that deal is close as mediators say they are exchanging proposals

US and Qatari officials have said progress is being made in restoring a ceasefire in the US-...
body_text:
Optimism echoes Trump’s claims on Monday that deal is close as mediators say they are exchanging proposals

US and Qatari officials have said progress is being made in restoring a ceasefire in the US-Iran war and reopening the strait of Hormuz.

The optimistic speculation on Tuesday brought oil prices down 2%, but the strait remained closed to shipping and a cargo vessel was reportedly struck by an unidentified projectile off Oman’s coast close to the strait.

Britain’s maritime security agency, UKMTO, reported the strike on Monday night but did not name the vessel.

The US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, said the US and Iran were negotiating and told CNBC television: “I think there is a chance we may have a deal today ​or tomorrow to open the strait and move towards a more normalised ​position in this conflict.”

His remarks echo similarly upbeat comments on Monday from Donald Trump, who claimed that a breakthrough was imminent, though Tehran quickly denied it was involved in any direct talks with the US.

Qatari and Pakistani mediators said they were talking to both sides in an effort to close gaps, restore the ceasefire deal from the memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed in mid-June and reopen the Hormuz strait, which was the portal for a fifth of the world’s oil and liquified natural gas.

Qatar’s ‌foreign ministry spokesperson, Majed al-Ansari, said Qatar, Pakistan and Oman were mediating in close coordination and exchanging draft proposals between Washington and Tehran. He said the diplomatic contacts had reached “very progressive stages”.

A senior Pakistani security official told Reuters news agency: “A lot is happening in the ‌background … We are talking to both sides. Our sole goal at this moment is to make both parties at least agree to start talking.”

However, neither Qatar nor Pakistan are directly involved in the focus of negotiations in recent days, which has been between Iran and Oman on a temporary transit scheme that would allow ships to enter and leave the Gulf. The MoU broke down in July when vessels tried to cross the strait along the Omani coast without seeking Iranian approval, and Iran attacked them.

Regional diplomats involved in the talks said Oman was under concerted US, European and Saudi pressure to accept a temporary scheme that would allow shipping to enter the Gulf via a route through the strait close to Iran, and then leave on a southern route along the Omani coast, which would be jointly controlled with Iran.

The contentious issue of Iran’s demand to charge transiting vessels tolls or other fees would be left to be decided during a 60-day negotiating period, during which time Iran’s nuclear programme would also be addressed.

The Omani government has been resisting the Hormuz proposal out of fear it could become permanent and give Tehran an enduring say over sea routes in Omani waters, the regional diplomats said.

The Iranian state-run broadcaster IRIB reported on Tuesday evening: “These negotiations, taking place between the two coastal countries of the strait of Hormuz, are focused on determining safe routes for ships to transit. The talks have so far been assessed as positive at both the technical and political levels, and Iran is working with Oman to develop the necessary mechanisms for future arrangements to manage shipping traffic in this strategic waterway.”

The talks are complicated by splits in Tehran, according to the diplomats, with the foreign ministry keen to do a deal and fearing Iranian control of the Hormuz strait could prove to be a wasting asset over time as sea traffic finds alternative routes. Regime hardliners, on the other hand, oppose the deal on the grounds that the US administration cannot be trusted to deliver the financial benefits promised in return for opening the strait.

“I think the regime understands the magnitude of the hold Iran has over the strait, and they smell the desperation coming from the US in terms of [trying to] strike a deal,” a diplomat from the region said.

Another diplomat said Riyadh was putting particularly heavy pressure on Oman because the Saudis thought “we may be on the brink of a regional war because there is a big faction in Iran that does not want a deal under any circumstances”.

title: Commanders cornerback Ahkello Witherspoon retires from football at 31
excerpt:
Akhello Witherspoon reportedly informed the Washington Commanders on Tuesday that he is retiring from football. (This video contains AI-assisted content)

Washington Commanders cornerback Ahkello With...
body_text:
Akhello Witherspoon reportedly informed the Washington Commanders on Tuesday that he is retiring from football. (This video contains AI-assisted content)

Washington Commanders cornerback Ahkello Witherspoon is retiring from the NFL at 31 years old.

The team announced Tuesday that they placed Witherspoon on the Reserve/Retired List and signed cornerback Fabian Moreau to take his place. Witherspoon practiced Monday and informed the team Tuesday morning that he was retiring, according to ESPN.

Witherspoon signed a one-year, $1.41 million contract with the Commanders in May but will not end up suiting up for them this fall.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Los Angeles Rams cornerback Ahkello Witherspoon (4) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Ariz., on Dec. 7, 2025. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

Witherspoon played college football at Colorado, where he starred as a defensive back. In 37 games, he recorded 71 tackles, three interceptions, 27 passes defended, one fumble recovery and one forced fumble.

In his senior year, Witherspoon led Division I college football with 22 passes defended. The San Francisco 49ers selected him in the third round of the 2017 NFL Draft, and he became a key piece in their secondary.

Washington Commanders cornerback Ahkello Witherspoon participates in a drill on the first day of training camp at BigBear.ai Performance Center at Commanders Park in Ashburn, Va., on July 29, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

He started 33 of the 47 games he played with the 49ers, recording 117 tackles and four interceptions, returning one for a touchdown, with 24 passes defended.

After four years with the 49ers, Witherspoon signed with the Seattle Seahawks, only to be traded to the Pittsburgh Steelers before ever suiting up for them. He spent the next two seasons in Pittsburgh.

Witherspoon played in 13 games with the Steelers, starting seven of them. He recorded 35 tackles and four interceptions over his two seasons.

Los Angeles Rams cornerback Ahkello Witherspoon breaks up a pass intended for New York Jets wide receiver Davante Adams during the third quarter at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J., on Dec. 22, 2024. (USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con)

After two years in Pittsburgh, he then signed what would become the first of three consecutive one-year contracts with the Los Angeles Rams. The best season of his career came in his first year with the Rams, when he started all 17 games and recorded 52 tackles and three interceptions.

For his career, Witherspoon started 64 of the 96 games he played in, recorded 243 tackles, 13 interceptions and 60 passes defended.

title: Labour members ‘have tougher view on welfare than you might think’, poll suggests
excerpt:
Survey finds party members see health, the economy, cost of living and climate crisis among biggest challenges

Andy Burnham has inherited a Labour membership that is sceptical about increased welfare...
body_text:
Survey finds party members see health, the economy, cost of living and climate crisis among biggest challenges

Andy Burnham has inherited a Labour membership that is sceptical about increased welfare spending, supportive of higher defence spending, and ranks the climate crisis as one of the country’s biggest challenges, according to new polling.

The survey of 788 members between the end of June and the end of July shows them ranking health (43%), the economy (42%), cost of living (39%) and climate change (29%) as Britain’s most important issues, ahead of welfare benefits (7%) and immigration (6%).

Despite the internal rows within the parliamentary Labour party (PLP) on welfare spending and general public pushback, 47% of members surveyed by ThinkLabour believe the government is spending too much on welfare, compared with 21% who believe it does not spend enough. When asked whether they would prefer the government to fund its current welfare bill differently, 52% said taxes should be raised. Additionally, 70% of Labour members said only high earners should be taxed while 24% supported higher taxes on everyone to fund the current bill.

The survey reveals members overwhelmingly backed more spending on social care, with 73% saying the government should spend more on this through higher taxes, either on higher earners alone or through general taxation. It found 68% of members wanted Britain to spend more on defence, and among the supporters for higher defence spending, 61% backed paying for this through higher taxes.

Three-quarters of Labour’s members said they had backed Keir Starmer in the 2020 party leadership contest. The survey did not ask members about Burnham’s leadership. However, a poll conducted just before Starmer’s disastrous local elections performance revealed Burnham had a net favourability of 72% at that time, suggesting he would be likely to win any leadership contest he could have fought in. Burnham won the leadership unopposed within the PLP so a vote from party members was not required.

The data is likely to be watched by those in government and it is understood these findings have been shared with senior strategists in Downing Street.

ThinkLabour, formerly known as Labour Together, has become increasingly linked to Burnham’s premiership. The former CEO Alison Phillips recently left the thinktank to become the prime minister’s deputy chief of staff, alongside the former director of devolution JP Spencer, who is now working in No 10 North. Ed Owen, a former Labour adviser during the Blair administration, is the interim CEO.

Christabel Cooper, ThinkLabour’s interim director of political strategy, said: “Labour members have a tougher view on welfare than you might think. They will be aware that welfare is something the Labour government has to get right if it is going to win a second term. And they also understand the importance of defence in a deeply uncertain world.

“That’s why it’s important to understand what members actually say rather than just rely on assumptions about what they might think.”

The survey, led by Cooper, comes after the organisation released a report titled Who is Labour For? arguing that Labour’s route back to electoral success laid in holding together voters under pressure on finances, progressive voters, and those concerned about the NHS and immigration. The report was shared with No 10 and publicly praised by the deputy Labour leader, Lucy Powell.

title: Second lady Usha Vance gets candid about new baby, juggling four children and motherhood
excerpt:
Second lady Usha Vance discusses life with four children, sharing how she and Vice President JD Vance make one-on-one time with each child while adjusting to life with their newborn son, Alec.

FIRST ...
body_text:
Second lady Usha Vance discusses life with four children, sharing how she and Vice President JD Vance make one-on-one time with each child while adjusting to life with their newborn son, Alec.

FIRST ON FOX: In her first interview since the birth of her fourth child with Vice President JD Vance just a few weeks ago, Usha Vance described the joy of being a new mother all over again during a candid interview with Fox News Digital on Tuesday, August 4.

The interview came on the same day the newest episode of her popular podcast, "Storytime with the Second Lady," was set to go live.

"It's been really lovely so far," she said of the experience of having four children, speaking from the Vice President's Residence. "One of the things that has just been beautiful to see is how excited my older kids are about their new brother. They're always fighting over holding him. When we do diaper changes or clothes changes, one of them is always there helping. They're willing to burp him, they want to grab things for him, they want to entertain him."

JD VANCE AND WIFE USHA WELCOME FOURTH CHILD, REVEAL BABY BOY'S NAME

She added, "So there's this really great way in which their needs are complementary with his."

Vice President Vance and his wife announced the birth of their fourth child in a July 20 Instagram post, as Fox News Digital previously reported. The couple said their baby boy, Alec Neel Vance, was born on Sunday morning, July 19.

Vice President JD Vance, second lady Usha Vance and their children Ewan, Vivek, Mirabel and new baby Alec pose for a family photo at the Vice President’s Residence on Wednesday, July 22, 2026.  (White House Photographer Emily Higgins)

"We are excited to announce that our baby boy, Alec Neel Vance, was born this morning," the couple wrote. "Usha and the baby are happy and healthy, and our kids are overjoyed to meet their little brother."

On Tuesday in her on-camera interview with Fox News Digital, Mrs. Vance called out the importance of doing things one on one with each of her children and the baby.

"I'm sure there are going to be hiccups here and there! But for right now, they seem to be really thriving."

"They feel like they're getting their own personal time with both of us," she said.

"For example, we go out [of the residence] and do something every day. And we've been doing that since the day we came home from the hospital. So yesterday was my middle child's day, and we went to a bookstore, we went to lunch — we did a quick return at a shop, and the whole time, it was just really special.

IVANKA TRUMP AND BETTINA ANDERSON'S CLOSE BOND ON DISPLAY AT MAR-A-LAGO BRIDAL SHOWER

"And we're trying to do that all the time. Now, I'm sure there are going to be hiccups here and there! But for right now, they seem to be really thriving."

She added, "My older kids see this as only good for themselves. Like, there's only one more kid to add to their pack. The parents are now outnumbered two to one!"

Second lady Usha Vance with newborn son Alec. She shared the joys and challenges of parenting four children with Fox News Digital. (White House Photographer Emily Higgins)

She referenced the jitters she had a bit ago — and how those were swiftly put to rest, and now part of the past.

"I would say I had all sorts of angst about this. My family [had] felt so complete. My kids were growing into a new phase," said Mrs. Vance.

Now, she said, "I'm really glad that we took this plunge. I'm really glad that we decided to move into the unknown and do something that felt like a little bit of a risk to a settled and happy family dynamic because it's only become happier."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"And we're looking forward to seeing what the next few years bring."

She is also continuing to expand and develop her podcast, "Storytime with the Second Lady."

The Vance family is shown together after welcoming their fourth child, Alec. Usha Vance said she initially worried about changing a family dynamic that already felt complete — but said adding another child has brought even more joy to their home. (White House Photographer Emily Higgins)

The latest episode features author Jackie Oshry reading her children's book about summer camp. Mrs. Vance said the podcast is designed to encourage children not only to read books but also to imagine creating stories of their own.

"One of the things we're trying to do with this podcast is highlight authors of books to show [the children] that it's not just reading that you can do," she said. "You can imagine your own stories. You can write them yourself."

So why this signature issue for her as second lady — and not others that she might have chosen? Mrs. Vance said that reading has long been one of her favorite hobbies and something she enjoys sharing with her own children.

She said she chose literacy as one of her key initiatives because she wanted to make "a concrete change" while serving as second lady. She noted how critical it is that children in America develop a love of, and facility with, reading from a young age.

Second lady Usha Vance is shown with author Jackie Oshry, whose children's book about summer camp is featured on the latest episode of Mrs. Vance's podcast, "Storytime with the Second Lady." (White House Photographer Emily Higgins)

She is also encouraging children in kindergarten through eighth grade to participate in the White House Summer Reading Challenge by reading 12 books before the end of August. Families who complete the challenge will be entered to win prizes — including a chance to visit the White House, she said.

In the waning weeks of summer, Mrs. Vance said her family is preparing for a new school year by gathering school supplies, organizing clothes and spending as much time outdoors as possible before classes begin for her older children.

"We're trying to make it a celebratory thing," she said of the family's back-to-school traditions.

"Over the month of August, we slowly get everything prepared so it doesn't come as too much of a shock when they have to wake up at 6:30 again every morning."

President Donald Trump declared in a Truth Social post right after the Vances' new baby was born, "Congratulations! A perfect baby boy for the wonderful Vance family."

JD and Usha Vance, pictured above with their three children, just before welcoming their fourth child, Alec, who was born July 19.  (White House Photographer Emily Higgins)

His post included a photo of the infant and two children.

Kelly McGreal is a production assistant with the lifestyle team at Fox News Digital.

title: Ex-MP urges Tories to drop candidate jailed for campaign of antisemitic abuse against her
excerpt:
Luciana Berger says Joshua Bonehill-Paine should have no role in public life because of ‘his racism and his view of women’

A former MP has urged the Tory leader to drop an election candidate who was ...
body_text:
Luciana Berger says Joshua Bonehill-Paine should have no role in public life because of ‘his racism and his view of women’

A former MP has urged the Tory leader to drop an election candidate who was previously jailed for a campaign of antisemitic abuse against her.

Kemi Badenoch on Tuesday defended the Conservative party’s selection of Joshua Bonehill-Paine, a former neo-Nazi, insisting she believes in “second chances”.

Writing on social media, Luciana Berger, who is now a peer, said: “For the avoidance of doubt, I don’t believe this man should have *any* role in public life – because of both his racism and his view of women.”

Directly addressing the Conservative leader in a thread of comments online, Berger said she was still “haunted” by the case and told Badenoch that she had “got this very, very wrong”.

“He was convicted for racial harassment for 5 specific blogs. But that wasn’t all – he’d published *reams* of deeply racist, misogynistic and pornographic material about me,” said Berger. She recalled being six months pregnant when she had to give evidence at the Old Bailey in what she described as “two days of hell”.

“I count myself lucky though. There were other victims whose lives he had totally destroyed,” she added. She said she felt sick reading commentators who were defending the selection.

Bonehill-Paine, the creator of the viral Crewkerne Gazette series of AI clips, is due to stand for election to Somerset council next year.

He told the Guardian on Monday that he was an executive member of the Tories’ Yeovil branch, working as an events organiser, and has carried out counter-extremism work since he was released from prison.

Badenoch said on Tuesday that she was not recruiting neo-Nazis to the Conservative party and that Bonehill-Paine was certified by the Home Office to train police officers on antisemitism and on countering extremism.

She added: “Yes, he is somebody who had been previously convicted for this, but he is someone who has shown contrition for his crimes, has been rehabilitated and is spending every day working to solve the very problem which he knew he had caused previously.

“He’s going up and down the country training people and the Conservative party believes in second chances.”

But there was criticism from the Board of Deputies of British Jews, Labour and others who contrasted Badenoch’s support for Bonehill-Paine with the freezing out of centrist Tories. Former Tory minister Gavin Barwell last month lost the whip after warnings from Badenoch that supporters of policies such as targets for net zero were no longer welcome in the party while former defence secretary Grant Shapps was recently blocked from standing again for the party.

Karen Newman, vice-president of the Board of Deputies of British Jews, told HuffPost: “It beggars belief that any party would select as a candidate a multiply convicted felon and the founder of a far-right group called National British Resistance.”

“We have contacted the Conservative party to set out our concerns and call on them to rescind his selection and review their vetting processes.”

Bonehill-Paine re-emerged in recent years as the creator of the Crewkerne Gazette, a satirical online account, and has a conviction for assaulting a police officer and burglary of a police station. He was convicted in 2014 of malicious communications over an anti-Islam hoax that led to death threats against the owners of a pub in Leicester.

He was jailed in 2015 for more than three years after posting antisemitic material online ahead of a planned neo-Nazi rally. In 2016, he was found guilty of racially aggravated harassment of Berger, who is Jewish.

The abuse directed at her was cited by the Jewish Labour Movement, which described Bonehill-Paine’s selection by the Tories as “appalling”.

Bonehill-Paine has meanwhile hit back at Reform UK after its leader, Nigel Farage, joined in the criticism of the Conservatives. An image of an email in which Reform thanked him for applying to be a party candidate and informed him that he had passed vetting checks was shared on X by Bonehill-Paine.

He also provided evidence indicating that the chair of Reform’s Yeovil branch had written to him as recently as June to ask if he would like to meet to discuss the prospect of standing for the party.

A Reform UK spokesperson said: “There’s a reason why Mr Bonehill-Paine wasn’t selected as a Reform UK candidate. Meanwhile, while Kemi Badenoch claims to have a new generation of Tory candidates and says she supports the fight against antisemitism, she is selecting a convicted antisemite to stand for the Conservatives. The hypocrisy is breathtaking.”
