title: Gaza holds mass funeral for 112 people killed in Israel’s 2023 Sabra attack
excerpt: More than 100 Palestinians whose bodies were trapped beneath rubble for nearly three years have been laid to rest in Gaza City, in one of the largest mass funerals held in the enclave since Israel’s g...
body_text:
More than 100 Palestinians whose bodies were trapped beneath rubble for nearly three years have been laid to rest in Gaza City, in one of the largest mass funerals held in the enclave since Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza began.

Thousands of people gathered on Tuesday to bury the remains of 112 members of the Abu Sharia and al-Hasayna families after rescue teams recovered their bodies from the site of a November 2023 Israeli attack in the Sabra neighbourhood.

According to Palestinian officials, the November 22, 2023 attack killed 308 members of the two families, including 40 children, 30 women and seven people with disabilities.

Rescue teams recently recovered more than 100 bodies from the site, allowing families to hold funeral prayers and burials. Palestinian authorities say about 157 people remain missing, either still beneath the rubble or otherwise unaccounted for.

Rows of coffins draped in Palestinian flags were carried through Gaza City as mourners gathered for the funeral. Large banners bearing photographs of the victims were displayed alongside calls for an end to Israel’s war on Gaza that began in October 2023.

The Palestinian Civil Defence in Gaza described the funeral as one of the largest held in the territory during the war, with spokesman Mahmoud Basal posting on X that Gaza was “set for an exceptional and painful scene”.

He said the funeral procession reflected the scale of the human losses suffered by Palestinian families who have waited years to bury their relatives.

The funeral also prompted an outpouring of grief from Palestinian researchers, activists and human rights advocates, many of whom said it symbolised the suffering of families still waiting to recover loved ones buried beneath the rubble.

Mustafa Barghouti, secretary-general of the Palestinian National Initiative, described the funeral as potentially being “the largest funeral in Palestinian history”.

Palestinian researcher Mahmoud Hamed al-Aila said Gaza was “extracting the bodies of its children from under the rubble after years of genocide”.

“What heart can bear this pain?” he asked.

Activist Mohammed Haniyah said dozens of other bodies have decomposed or are still missing under the rubble.

Another activist, Ali Abo Rezeq, said the procession turned “massacre statistics into coffins and shrouds”, highlighting that some families searched through the rubble with their bare hands because of the shortages of heavy equipment.

Online bloggers, including Malik Al-Shanbari and Khaled Safi, viewed the funeral not merely as a burial ceremony, but as a “renewed testament to the scale of the tragedy left behind by the war”.

Ramy Abdu, chairman of the Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor, said around 200 members of the Abu Sharia family are still believed to be beneath the rubble, and that their remains may have decomposed.

The funeral also highlighted the fate of thousands of other Palestinian families who are still waiting to recover the remains of their relatives believed to be missing beneath the rubble across Gaza.

The funeral was held amid ongoing Israeli violations of a “ceasefire” agreement in October. As of Monday, continued Israeli strikes have killed at least 1,250 Palestinians and injured 4,110 others.

The so-called ceasefire deal was signed after more than two years of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, which has killed at least 73,375 Palestinians and wounded at least 174,220, most of them women and children.

About 90 percent of Gaza’s infrastructure has also been damaged or destroyed during the genocide.

Meanwhile, the Assembly of Palestinian Clans and Families called on the Western-backed Board of Peace to accelerate efforts to recover bodies still trapped beneath the rubble, clear the debris and support the reconstruction of Gaza.

It said the burial of 112 Palestinians may have marked the end of the long wait for some families, but it did not end the search for thousands of others still missing.

title: The scam text test: Spot danger before you tap
excerpt: Halimah Delaine Prado, Google General Counsel, reveals the rise of AI-powered phishing scams originating from China's 'outsider enterprise.' She explains how these criminals use artificial intelligenc...
body_text:
Halimah Delaine Prado, Google General Counsel, reveals the rise of AI-powered phishing scams originating from China's 'outsider enterprise.' She explains how these criminals use artificial intelligence to create highly convincing fake websites, impersonating trusted brands like T-Mobile to defraud hundreds of thousands of Americans, causing millions in losses. Prado highlights Google's strategy to combat these evolving threats.

Your phone buzzes. The text reads, "Your package is delayed. Confirm your address here." A little later, it's a text message about an unpaid toll, suspicious bank activity or an account that will be locked unless you act now.

That's how scam texts work. They don't always look wild or obviously fake. They look routine, urgent and easy to deal with in a hurry. The good news: You don't need to memorize every scam. You just need a quick way to test suspicious messages before you tap. Here's the simple scam text test to run before you click, pay or share anything.

CyberGuy Live: Missed "Sick of Spam?" Get the replay and checklist

Our free CyberGuy Live class, "Sick of Spam?", has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our spam-stopping checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you step by step through simple ways to reduce robocalls, spam texts, junk email and unwanted messages. You’ll also learn how to curb political texts, clean up your inbox and spot messages that could put your personal information at risk.

Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

FAKE SHINYHUNTERS SEXTORTION EMAIL USES CARNIVAL BREACH DATA

Scam texts often imitate delivery companies, banks, toll agencies and online services to pressure people into clicking dangerous links. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)

If a text asks you to click, pay, verify, sign in or fix a problem, run through these checks first.

Are you actually waiting for that package? Do you use that bank? Did you recently drive on a toll road? If the answer is no, treat the message as suspicious. Even if the answer is yes, don't assume it's real. Scammers rely on coincidence. They send thousands of similar messages knowing that some recipients will be waiting for a package or use the company being impersonated.

Urgency is one of the biggest red flags. Watch for phrases like:

A real company may send an urgent alert, but scammers use pressure to stop you from checking whether the message is legitimate. Take a breath before responding. A few extra minutes spent verifying the message can prevent days or weeks of dealing with a stolen account.

Even if the address looks legitimate, avoid opening links in unexpected texts. Scammers can disguise links or create convincing copies of real websites. Verify the message through the company's official app or a website you type in yourself.

Many scam texts use vague greetings, odd wording, awkward punctuation or slightly incorrect brand names. You might see a message addressed to "Dear customer" instead of your name. It may refer to a package without showing an order number or claim to come from a bank without identifying the account involved. Good grammar doesn't guarantee a message is safe. Scammers now use artificial intelligence to write more convincing messages. Still, sloppy wording and missing details remain warning signs.

Legitimate companies may send you a one-time verification code. However, a bank, government agency or customer service representative should never ask you to give that code to someone else. Anyone who asks for your code may be trying to take control of your account.

This is the most important step. Instead of using the link or phone number in the message:

If the issue is real, you should still be able to find it through one of those trusted channels.

FAKE PASSWORD-MANAGER ALERTS COULD PUT YOUR VAULT AT RISK

A quick scam text checklist can help users spot fake alerts before sharing passwords, payment details or one-time security codes. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)

Scam texts often fall into a few familiar categories.

These messages claim a package was delayed, an address needs to be corrected or a small shipping fee must be paid. The link may lead to a fake postal or delivery website that collects your card information, password or home address.

These texts claim someone used your card, your account has been locked or you must verify a transaction immediately. The message may include a phone number connecting you to a scammer pretending to work for the bank.

Toll scams claim you owe a small amount and will face a larger penalty if you don't pay immediately. The amount is often low enough to make paying seem easier than investigating. The payment page then steals your financial information.

These messages claim your email, payment app, streaming service or social media account will be suspended. They direct you to a fake login page designed to capture your username and password. These scams work because each message sounds plausible. The goal is to make you react first and think later.

Simply opening a phishing page doesn't always mean your information was stolen. The risk increases if you entered information, downloaded a file or approved a permission request.

Use a different password for every important account. A password manager can create and store strong passwords so one stolen login doesn't give scammers access to everything else.

Change the affected account's password immediately and check whether a new device, email address or phone number was added. Contact the company through its official app, website or phone number. Tell the representative that someone may have gained access to your account.

Report any charges you don't recognize as soon as possible.

HOTEL WI-FI PHISHING ATTACK TARGETS MICROSOFT LOGINS

Anyone who taps a suspicious link should secure affected accounts, review recent activity and report the scam as quickly as possible.

Visit IdentityTheft.gov to create a recovery plan. You may also want to place a fraud alert or security freeze on your credit files. A credit freeze can prevent criminals from opening many types of new accounts in your name.

Avoid entering sensitive information on the device until you are confident it is secure.

Reporting scam texts helps phone carriers and government agencies identify active campaigns.

Good habits are your first line of defense, but strong antivirus software can add another layer of protection. Some security tools can warn you about suspicious links, phishing websites and malicious downloads before they put your information at risk.

Many text scams are only the first step. The message sends you to a fake website. That site may steal your password, payment details or other personal information. In some cases, it may also try to install malware on your device.

Security software cannot catch every scam or replace careful judgment. Still, it can help stop a suspicious link or malicious download before one quick tap leads to fraud or an account takeover. Features vary by provider and device, so check what is included before choosing a service.

Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android & iOS devices at Cyberguy.com

You never have to solve a surprise text from inside the text. Stop, verify independently and only act through official channels. That one habit can help you avoid a huge number of text scams.

Scam texts work because they make an everyday problem feel urgent. A package delay, unpaid toll or bank warning can seem believable enough to make you tap without thinking. Don't use the link or phone number in the message. Open the company's official app, type its website yourself or call a number you already trust. Strong antivirus software can help flag some suspicious texts and fake websites, but no security tool catches everything. Taking a few seconds to verify the message can save you from a stolen account or a costly mistake.

What is the most convincing scam text you have received, and what tipped you off before you tapped? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

title: Ohio Republican Max Miller faces growing calls to resign over domestic abuse allegations
excerpt:
Bernie Moreno, Miller’s ex-father-in-law, says congressman is unfit for office as Miller denies allegations

Max Miller, the Republican representative from Ohio, is facing a rising groundswell of resi...
body_text:
Bernie Moreno, Miller’s ex-father-in-law, says congressman is unfit for office as Miller denies allegations

Max Miller, the Republican representative from Ohio, is facing a rising groundswell of resignation calls from his own party over domestic abuse allegations after his ex-father-in-law, Bernie Moreno, a GOP senator, said he was unfit to serve in Congress.

With a deadline looming for party leaders to choose a potential replacement, Miller, a former White House aide, also came under pressure from Donald Trump on Monday after the president reportedly called and told him “things aren’t looking good” for his re-election campaign against Democrat opponent, Brian Poindexter.

Pleas for Miller to step down intensified after Moreno – father of Miller’s former wife, Emily Moreno – broke his silence on Sunday after months of refraining from comment on allegations concerning the alleged abuse of his daughter.

“If there are any basic standards of character required to hold elected office, Max Miller fails them,” Moreno, an ally of Trump, posted. “He should not serve in the House of Representatives.”

Moreno’s comments came after Miller posted a livestream video defending himself against the abuse accusations and saying his former wife had “significant mental-health challenges”.

A series of public statements from Moreno’s fellow Republican senators indicate that their sympathies are with him.

“[Miller] should resign. He should quit,” Roger Marshall, a senator from Kansas, told Politico. “I don’t know Mr. Miller’s story, but I trust Bernie [Moreno] so much as a good friend, and his family has such high values.”

West Virginia senator Shelley Moore Capito said: “I don’t know [Miller]. I haven’t read a whole lot about him, but if [Moreno] thinks he ought to resign, I’m supportive of that.”

Lisa Murkowski, a Republican senator from Alaska, said: “The accusations are very serious, and if there is truth to them, I am one who says that our elected officials need to be held to high standards.

“And certainly, when it comes to allegations of domestic abuse, child abuse, that’s not what we want in our lawmakers.”

Three other senators, Rick Scott of Florida, the West Virginian senator Jim Justice, and Cynthia Lummis of Wyoming, also gave public backing to Moreno against Miller.

“I don’t know enough about the allegations, but like Bernie said, it sounds like he thinks he needs psychological help,” said Scott, “I trust Bernie.”

Miller – who married Emily Moreno at Trump’s club in Bedminster, New Jersey in 2022 – has been accused of holding a gun to her head and scalding her with boiling water. Their toddler daughter, who was born in 2023 is also said to have suffered a broken collar bone due to his actions.

Miller denies allegations of abuse and has filed a defamation case against his wife over the claims. The couple divorced in 2025.

Axios reported that Trump called Miller on Monday amid concerns that the situation threatened Republican chances of holding the congressional seat in November’s midterms, when the party already faces an uphill challenge to keep its wafer-thin majority in the House of Representatives.

But the president avoided taking sides when asked about the issue by reporters in the White House. “I know Max, he’s a good person. I mean, I always thought he was a very good person. And I’m going to let the families figure that out,” he said.

Miller has resisted calls for him to withdraw from the race and told the Wall Street Journal that Trump “was supportive of me over the phone” on Monday’s call.

“He said he had a poll with no detail, and I pushed back with our poll that has us winning by 9 with our message out there,” Miller told the newspaper. “He kept on reiterating it’s going to be tough, and it’s going to be a really hard one for you.”

If Miller were to remove his name from the ballot before the close of business on Tuesday, a special Republican primary would be held to replace him.

If he were to withdraw after that, the party would still need to replace him by 10 August, but would need to give two days notice beforehand to hold a meeting to choose a substitute candidate.

title: Refuse collectors help Italian woman recover binned €1m lottery ticket

body_text:
Winner called waste management team after she realised stub showing she had hit the jackpot had been thrown away

A €1m lottery ticket has been recovered from the rubbish in Italy after the frantic winner called on refuse collectors to help her retrieve it, according to the waste management company.

The instant win ticket was “miraculously still in one piece” after garbage workers combed through mounds of rubbish on their truck, said Roberto Nicola Toscano, the administrator of the SANB company in Italy’s southern Puglia region.

Toscano explained how when the winner went on Sunday to check her ticket at her local shop after the draw, the machine indicated it was “non-payable”. That was because smaller retailers can only redeem small wins.

But the woman – who remains anonymous – didn’t realise she had won the big jackpot.

“The winner always played the same numbers, as they were associated with a loved one,” Toscano said.

When she returned home from the store, a family member told her that her regular numbers had won. They immediately ran back to the shop, only to discover the ticket had already been thrown away and the rubbish collected.

“We reconstructed the journey of the ticket, without much hope of finding it, as it had already been picked up by a garbage truck,” Toscano said

With a stroke of luck, however, they managed to identify the correct lorry and stopped it.

Given the risk posed by potentially dangerous material in the waste, they took the vehicle to a specialist company equipped to do the search, he said.

The workers searched for over a day, finding various tickets and ticket stubs.

“Among them was the stub we were looking for, which was miraculously still in one piece,” Toscano said.

When he told the winner they had found it, “she cried with emotion”, he said. “I would have hugged her, but we were on the phone.”

However, averting the disaster came at a price. SANB, located in Bitonto outside Bari, is a public agency, meaning that the cost of the search would have been borne by taxpayers.

Toscano said the woman had to sign a promise to “cover all of the additional costs” incurred – a gamble that paid off.

title: Chicago White Sox lead American League Central but face a red-hot Boston Red Sox team Tuesday
excerpt:
The World Series champion talks to Fox News Digital about the impact the additional postseason spots and upcoming CBA negotiations will have on the trade deadline.

With the trade deadline passing Mon...
body_text:
The World Series champion talks to Fox News Digital about the impact the additional postseason spots and upcoming CBA negotiations will have on the trade deadline.

With the trade deadline passing Monday, we are officially on playoff watch for teams. Every game from here on will take on a bit more intensity and importance. We know a few teams have dropped out of the race after the trades that took place. Others bolstered their roster, and we have two of them that are going all in, taking each other on today as the White Sox face the Red Sox.

It is the start of August, and the Chicago White Sox are leading the American League Central. Now, before you put a reservation down for some playoff tickets, keep in mind that the Tigers were leading the division to start August last year, and they were heavy favorites to win it. The problem is that the Guardians were lurking, had a spectacular September, and took down the AL Central. The Tigers still made the postseason, but it feels like we will get two Wild Card teams from the American League East, so the safest path for the White Sox is to win the division.

Chicago White Sox manager Will Venable meets on the mound with catcher Drew Romo, shortstop Colson Montgomery, first baseman Munetaka Murakami and second baseman Chase Meidroth during an MLB game at Rate Field in Chicago on May 13, 2026. (Patrick Gorski/Icon Sportswire)

They did add to the team at the trade deadline, and that should instill a bit more confidence in the roster. Their rotation will now have a couple of dependable guys. Davis Martin is one of those guys, but he is approaching the most innings he's pitched in a year. He is 9-5 with a 3.62 ERA and a 1.26 WHIP. He struggled in July after a mixed bag of results in June, so you do need to wonder if his success is fading. The White Sox went 1-4 in his starts in July, and he allowed 16 earned runs in 24 innings. One of those games was against the Red Sox where he allowed five earned runs in four innings.

RED SOX COME BACK FROM THE DEAD, MOVE INTO POSTSEASON CONTENTION WITH REMARKABLE 14-GAME WIN STREAK

The Boston Red Sox made arguably the most shocking move of the trade deadline, by acquiring Adley Rutschman from the Baltimore Orioles. The Red Sox were 32-46 on June 24. Since that point, they've gone 28-5. They have had three separate five-game or more winning streaks in that stretch, including one they are on right now. They just swept the Dodgers, arguably the best team in baseball. Can this level of winning be sustained for two more months? Unlikely, but it is impressive nonetheless.

Jarren Duran of the Boston Red Sox looks on after an at-bat against the Athletics at Sutter Health Park in Sacramento, Calif., on July 27, 2026. (Getty Images)

Tuesday they send Patrick Sandoval to the hill in hopes of making it six games in a row. For the year, Sandoval only has four starts under his belt and carries a 3.32 ERA and a 1.58 WHIP. None of his starts have been ugly or bad by any means. He did allow four earned runs against the Rays, but the other three saw him allow two or fewer. He faced the White Sox in the first start of his season and went 4.1 innings and allowed just one earned run on five hits.

The Boston Red Sox's win streak tied a franchise record at 15 games. (Photo by Danielle Parhizkaran/The Boston Globe via Getty Images)

It is hard to pick against the Red Sox with how hot as they've been. I have faded them in a couple of spots, but it didn't work out. The additions from the deadline should rejuvenate both of these teams as well. I think we should take the hotter team today, and I think we also need to start fading Martin. He will probably still have some good starts left, but he has struggled lately. He also didn't have a great June. His arm might just be getting tired. I'll take Sandoval and the Red Sox on the moneyline tonight.

title: EU commends Spain's 'swift response' to Ceuta migrant crisis
excerpt:
Hundreds of migrants were pictured lined up on a beach in Ceuta to collect aid on Tuesday

The European Union has praised Spain's "swift response" to the migrant crisis in Ceuta, following a meeting o...
body_text:
Hundreds of migrants were pictured lined up on a beach in Ceuta to collect aid on Tuesday

The European Union has praised Spain's "swift response" to the migrant crisis in Ceuta, following a meeting of the bloc's interior ministers on Tuesday.

Around 72,000 migrants crossed into the Spanish territory in North Africa between 30 and 31 July, Spain's Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said. He added that an estimated 70,000 have since been returned to Morocco.

At least 75 people died on the Spanish side of the border, while 11 deaths were reported in Morocco.

Irish Justice Minister Jim O'Callaghan, who chaired Tuesday's meeting, said the EU stood in solidarity with Spain and that migration required "a united European response".

The meeting had been expected to draw some tension, following earlier criticism of Spain from several EU nations.

On Thursday, Italy's right-wing Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni described the images from Ceuta as "shocking", writing on social media that such "uncontrolled immigration" was a security threat to Europe.

Italy suspended the Schengen zone agreement with Spain on free movement on Friday. Since the two countries do not share a land border, this would only apply, effectively, to flights - which appears simply to mean extra checks for passengers.

Watch: Migrants started to return to Morocco after thousands entered Spain's Ceuta on 30 July

The Schengen agreement eliminates border checks and now encompasses more than 450 million people and 29 countries in Europe.

Finland and Denmark backed Italy's move, while Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš urged a temporary suspension of Spain's Schengen membership.

Italy, along with Denmark and 20 other nations, later sent a letter expressing their concern over the Ceuta migrant crisis, and calling for a meeting of EU ministers.

In response, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said he had "serious concerns" about some European governments and pointed out that Ceuta was not part of the Schengen area.

While most had shown "support and solidarity", he said other European governments had chosen to attack Spain, "driven by prejudice, fake news, ignorance, or political interest".

Speaking after the meeting on Tuesday, Grande-Marlaska said the Schengen zone had not been compromised and that he hoped Italy would lift any added controls "as soon as possible".

Denmark's immigration minister Morten Bødskov said he was "very satisfied" with Spain's quick response, but added that the incident showed "it is absolutely crucial that we have control over the EU's borders".

Speaking afterwards, EU commissioner Magnus Brunner said the incident had been a "test" of European resilience and border security - which he said it had successfully "passed".

Brunner added that the EU had offered Spain emergency financial support to strengthen its borders and manage the crisis.

It is unknown exactly what led the tens of thousands of migrants to cross from Morocco into Ceuta in a span of just a few hours last week.

Brunner said it is thought that the influx was fuelled by criminal networks and social media disinformation.

The crossings came after Spain's Supreme Court ruled that migrants stopped at sea while trying to reach Ceuta or Melilla, another Spanish exclave, cannot be summarily returned to Morocco.

Moroccan authorities later said that it had warned Spain the ruling would cause "a problem", but Spain rejected this claim, with a government spokeswoman saying it had no evidence or intelligence "that alerted us to the magnitude of this unprecedented event".

title: Dave Rubin warns Trump has less than 3 months to push agenda before midterm elections

Despite having two and a half years left in office, Preside...
body_text:
'The Rubin Report' host Dave Rubin shares a warning for if the Republicans lose the House on a new episode of 'Hang Out with Sean Hannity.'

Despite having two and a half years left in office, President Donald Trump may have only three months to effectively implement his agenda, podcaster Dave Rubin said on Tuesday's episode of "Hang Out with Sean Hannity."

Rubin said Trump is likely to face hurdles beyond the typical challenges of policymaking if Democrats gain ground in Congress as a result of this year's midterm elections.

U.S. President Donald Trump pumps his fist as he leaves the stage after delivering remarks during the Faith & Freedom Coalition's 2026 Policy Conference at the Washington Hilton on June 26 in Washington, D.C. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

"If [Republicans] lose the House, [President Trump] is going to get hung up in impeachment," Rubin said.

100 DAY SPRINT TO THE MIDTERMS KICKS OFF AS REPUBLICANS AND DEMOCRATS CLASH FOR CONTROL ACROSS THE COUNTRY

"He'll be impeached, but he probably won't be removed from office. They're not going to get enough votes in the Senate one way or another."

Still, Rubin contended, the Make America Great Again movement faces an existential threat as its leader's time in the Oval Office draws to a close.

President Donald Trump walks to a waiting Air Force One at the Hagerstown Regional Airport on July 31 in Hagerstown, Maryland. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

"The point is that the process to end these last 10 years of MAGA and everything that has happened since 2015 will begin," he said.

The emboldening of the "crazies on the left" isn't the only threat, he added. Infighting among conservatives is going to "go completely bananas."

GOP CIVIL WAR ERUPTS OVER TRUMP'S LATEST AGENDA PUSH AS KEY REPUBLICANS THREATEN TO SINK MEGABILL

"It's going to be like rats jumping from a ship, and then you're going to have all these people leaving Trump and trying to pick up the pieces. It's going to be complete chaos."

Meanwhile, in Washington, D.C., Republicans are sounding the alarm that Trump’s demand to cancel the August recess could cost the GOP seats in the midterms, as vulnerable incumbents say they need to be home campaigning and connecting with constituents, not stuck on Capitol Hill.

"The Rubin Report" host acknowledged it was clichéd to claim the upcoming midterms would be "the most important election of all time," but said he does not see "how it could possibly be more important than it is right now."

"We are on the edge of handing the keys to the castle to people who are telling us they want to burn the castle down."

Fox News Digital's Alex Miller contributed to this report.

Max Bacall is an associate editor for Fox News Digital covering media, culture and comedy.

title: Oil prices fall on hopes Strait of Hormuz could reopen
excerpt:
Oil prices fell to a three-week low on Tuesday as senior US officials raised hopes of a deal with Iran to reopen the key Strait of Hormuz waterway.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secr...
body_text:
Oil prices fell to a three-week low on Tuesday as senior US officials raised hopes of a deal with Iran to reopen the key Strait of Hormuz waterway.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent both announced talks had progressed to allow shipments to potentially resume as soon as this week.

The cost of a barrel of brent crude, the global benchmark for oil prices, fell by almost 5% to under $80 on the news of supply disruptions potentially being eased.

But the failure of previous negotiations in recent months to de-escalate the conflict between the US and Iran has led to a volatile oil market, with drivers ultimately being hit by higher fuel prices at the pumps.

On Tuesday, along with the drop in Brent crude, US West Texas Intermediate prices were down more than 5%, to $76 a barrel. Both contracts dropped to their lowest levels since 13 July.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there had been progress made in discussions on getting more ships through the Strait with Iran and Oman.

"There's been progress made in those talks, but not finality yet. We're hoping that will happen very shortly," he told reporters at the State Department.

Bessent said a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could be agreed as soon as Tuesday or Wednesday.

There was a "chance we may have a deal today or tomorrow to open the strait and move towards a more normalized position in this conflict," he told CNBC.

"It would be freedom of movement," he added, when asked whether Iran would be allowed to charge for ships passing through.

While senior figures in the US government have announced talks have been progressing, no details of what a potential deal may look like have been released.

The Strait of Hormuz has been a central point in negotiations between the US and Iran. Before the conflict began in late February, the waterway handled about one-fifth of global daily oil and liquefied natural gas supplies.

The disruption has sent prices at the pumps up across the world. In the UK petrol prices are now at levels seen at the start of the conflict, with the average cost of a litre of petrol hitting £1.60, according to the RAC motoring group.

In the US, gasoline prices are on average above $4 a gallon, according to the AAA. Diesel is almost $5.40 a gallon.

Qatar, which is one of the key mediators between Washington and Tehran, said it was continuing efforts with other mediators to try to achieve a diplomatic resolution to the war, but admitted no direct talks were currently planned.

On Monday, President Donald Trump warned Iran faced its "last chance" to agree a deal to allow commercial shipping to resume in the Strait.

He said he had called off "massive" strikes on the country for talks to resume.

But Iran has said it was not negotiating with the US - and had no plans to do so - and is instead talking to Oman.

title: Elon Musk’s X latest to block Saudi dissident accounts inside kingdom
excerpt:
Exclusive: More than 60 accounts on X have been made unavailable in Saudi Arabia, after similar action on Snapchat and Facebook

Elon Musk’s X has become the latest major US social media company to bl...
body_text:
Exclusive: More than 60 accounts on X have been made unavailable in Saudi Arabia, after similar action on Snapchat and Facebook

Elon Musk’s X has become the latest major US social media company to block the accounts of Saudi Arabian dissidents so they are no longer visible inside the kingdom, following orders from Saudi authorities.

Earlier this year, the Guardian reported that platforms including Snapchat and Meta’s Facebook and Instagram had blocked dissidents’ accounts over allegations by Saudi authorities that they were violating local law.

At the time, X, formerly Twitter, said it had notified users that it had not taken any action following requests by Saudi authorities, and it “strongly believes in defending and respecting the voice of our users”.

However, since mid-July more than 60 accounts on the platform have been made unavailable in Saudi Arabia through geoblocking, which prevents users inside the kingdom from viewing the content, according to the London-based human rights organisation ALQST.

Those affected include Yahya Assiri, a Saudi human rights activist who runs ALQST, and Abdullah Alaoudh, a US-based activist and vocal critic of Saudi human rights violations. Others affected include exiled activists, Saudi academics and independent media.

Alaoudh, a senior policy adviser for Gulf issues at the American Committee for Middle East Rights, said: “I think it’s horrible because we were fighting tyrants back home and now we’re fighting tyrants and their cronies here where we are in exile.

“It’s censorship – and what’s even worse is that they did not say we violated X’s rules or Meta’s rules.”

Account holders received emails from X informing them that their content had been withheld in the kingdom “in order to comply with X’s obligations under Saudi Arabia’s local laws”.

A Saudi decree attached to the letters and seen by the Guardian said the accounts had transmitted material that “infringes on public order, religious values, public morals or the sanctity of private life”.

Abdullah Aljuraywi, a monitoring and campaigns officer at ALQST, whose X account was also blocked inside the kingdom, said: “The news was sadly not very surprising, given that the authorities have a long history of silencing criticism at home and treating Saudis who speak out from abroad, especially those still connected to people inside the country, as a threat.

“What is even more concerning is that technology companies have helped enable this suppression, instead of protecting the freedom of speech they often say they support.”

ALQST has called on X, Meta, Snapchat and YouTube to restore access to the accounts and provide transparency over how the decisions were reached.

Meta previously told the Guardian that when it received reports of content violating local law but not the company’s own community standards, the company may restrict the content’s availability in the country where it was alleged to be unlawful.

X and the Saudi embassy in London have been approached for comment.

Other accounts targeted include those of Ghanem al-Masarir, a prominent Saudi satirist. Earlier this year a British court ordered Saudi Arabia to pay him £3m in damages after his iPhones were hacked and he was physically attacked outside Harrods in central London.

In May, al-Masarir was notified by YouTube that two of his accounts, with more than 800,000 subscribers combined, would be blocked in the kingdom after legal complaints made from a “government entity”. YouTube did not respond to a request for comment.

The same month, X emailed al-Masarir informing him of the request from Saudi authorities alleging that his account violated Saudi law, with an attached decree. By July, the company had notified al-Masarir that his content had been withheld in the kingdom to comply with local laws.

“I’m not surprised that Saudi has asked to block, but I’m surprised Elon Musk has listened,” al-Masarir said. He predicted “other authoritarian countries around the world” would follow suit.

body_text:
Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos discusses the Nancy Guthrie investigation in a new video message to Savannah Guthrie and weighs in on the release of ransom notes.

An Arizona man who says a "swatting" call ended with deputies' bullets leaving him partially paralyzed is now demanding $176 million from the Pima County Sheriff's Department.

Axeel Melendez, 24, and his mother, Carmen Melendez, recently filed a notice of claim against the Pima County Sheriff's Office and Sheriff Chris Nanos, signaling their intent to sue, according to Arizona Public Media.

Dev Sethi, who is representing Melendez, told the outlet that the man and his mother were swatted, prompting a massive law enforcement response at their house. Swatting is a criminal prank where individuals place fake calls to 911 for a specific location with the goal of getting a law enforcement response to that location.

ROMANIAN NATIONAL LEARNS FATE FOR SWATTING US OFFICIALS, INCLUDING MEMBERS OF CONGRESS, JUDGES

Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos gives an update on the investigation after the disappearance of Nancy Guthrie on Feb. 5, 2026. (Rebecca Noble/Reuters)

"Our justice system recognizes the dignity of a human life and the importance of the completeness of your body. Axeel’s health, his independence, his ability to earn a living, his sense of security, that’s all been stolen away from him," Sethi said.

Someone impersonating Melendez initially called 311, a non-emergency number, on April 10 and said his father shot his sister, giving the address for Melendez.

NANCY GUTHRIE RANSOM DEMANDS RELEASED BY PIMA COUNTY SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT IN BID TO IDENTIFY SENDER

"This morning of the April 10 call has many red flags and hallmarks of it being a fake call, including…this call came into 311. Nobody reporting an emergency calls 311," Sethi said.

Sethi said the call was made from an out of state area code and added the caller didn't pronounce Melendez's first name correctly.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos speaks with a reporter in his office on Thursday, July 30, 2026. (Kat Ramirez for Fox News Digital, Matt Finn/Fox News)

Melendez received a threatening message from a hacker who stole his personal information during an online video game and demanded a ransom to return his accounts and passwords, his attorney said, even threatening to report him to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement because of his Hispanic name.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

After the threat, Melendez called 911 and shared his concerns about a possible swatting incident and was allegedly reassured there are safeguards.

"He tells a 911 operator all of this and she essentially downplays it and says, ‘Don’t worry, that’s not how it works. They can’t just call 911 and have the SWAT team show up at your house," Sethi said.

According to the attorney, Pima County deputies allegedly ignored a warning that Melendez's address was a known possible swatting target, stating that she approached the home with a mindset to "treat it like it’s real until it’s not real."

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Believing an intruder was breaking in, Melendez grabbed his family's legally owned handgun and took cover behind his bedroom door as deputies smashed through the window, according to the claim. The deputies then allegedly opened fire.

Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos gives an update on the investigation after the disappearance of Nancy Guthrie, the 84-year-old mother of U.S. journalist and television host Savannah Guthrie, who went missing from her in Tucson, Arizona, U.S. February 5, 2026. (Rebecca Noble/Reuters)

Melendez says he was hit in his right thigh and left shoulder, which left him with a spinal court injury in addition to broken ribs and a broken leg.

"He did everything we teach our kids to do. When you’re in danger, when somebody’s threatening you, what’s the first thing we tell all of our children? Call the police," Sethi said. "Axeel is a vulnerable young man, his life has been upended. He has real present needs and we’ve given them an opportunity to do the right thing and resolve the case, but the ball is wholly in their courts."

title: Battlefield robots open new front in innovation war with major US adversary
excerpt:
EdgeRunner AI Founder and CEO Tyler Saltsman told Fox News Digital how the Army is working with his company to build an AI "brain" designed to power the next generation of autonomous military robots.
...
body_text:
EdgeRunner AI Founder and CEO Tyler Saltsman told Fox News Digital how the Army is working with his company to build an AI "brain" designed to power the next generation of autonomous military robots.

FIRST ON FOX: The U.S. Army is teaming up with an artificial intelligence (AI) company to build an AI "brain" for military robots that can think, understand their surroundings and continue missions even after losing contact with human operators as the race for AI dominance intensifies.

Working with the Army Research Laboratory, defense AI company EdgeRunner AI has developed an onboard AI system that allows military robots to function in the battlefield without relying on cloud computing or an internet connection in environments where connectivity is lost.

"We like to think of robots as the next frontier of AI," EdgeRunner AI founder and CEO Tyler Saltsman told Fox News Digital.

"Think of them as a very far-out edge device, kind of like a cell phone, a tablet or a laptop. But now what we can do is we can put a brain, or a neural network, right on that robot so that robots can have context when they're on a mission helping the warfighter."

CHINA IS BUILDING AN AI WAR MACHINE. WASHINGTON MUST WAKE UP BEFORE IT’S TOO LATE

EdgeRunner AI founder and CEO Tyler Saltsman told Fox News Digital about the company's work with the U.S. Army to develop an AI "brain" for the next generation of military robots. (Fox News Digital/EdgeRunner AI)

The partnership comes as the U.S. and China race to integrate AI into their militaries, with both countries viewing AI as critical to maintaining a technological edge in future conflicts.

Saltsman said it's important for the U.S. to stay ahead in the global AI race, calling China's dominance in drone manufacturing "problematic."

"Whether or not China's ahead of us is debatable, but if China is, it's not by much," he said.

Saltsman said today's AI is "too generalized," which is why his company is developing technology built for specific military missions.

"Warfighters don't need 19th-century poetry," he said. "They need specific intelligence to his or her occupation in order to make better decisions in the heat of battle and that can increase the probability of winning the fight."

Working alongside aerial drones, the AI is designed to help robots "problem solve through different routes" while detecting explosives, carrying ammunition, scouting routes and reporting enemy activity.

UKRAINE’S BATTLEFIELD IS TRANSFORMING THE FUTURE OF NATO

Saltsman said the technology remains in the "development phase" and gives military robots the ability to understand what they see, not just detect it. (EdgeRunner AI)

"As you combine them together, you get a much better clarity of the battlefield and increased situational awareness," he said.

When communications are cut off, Saltsman said the military will need autonomous systems that can continue making decisions on their own.

"You can have a human pilot that controls the ground robot or the drone in the air," he said. "But then if they were to be jammed by a radar jammer and lose connectivity, then the neural network on that robot can still continue the mission and still aid the warfighter."

Saltsman argued the military "can't rely on internet access in war," warning that depending on systems like SpaceX's Starlink could add a "risk" to missions.

"The problem with Starlink is if you use it, you're effectively showing the enemy where you are, so you might as well be wearing a beacon on you saying, 'Hey, here's where I'm located,'" he said.

INSIDE CHINA’S AI ‘WOLF PACK’ DRONES BUILT WITH TAIWAN CONFLICT IN MIND

U.S. Army soldiers stand near an armored military vehicle on the outskirts of Rumaylan in Syria's northeastern Hasakeh province, bordering Turkey, on March 27, 2023. (Delil Souleiman/AFP via Getty Images)

Pointing to the Russia-Ukraine war, Saltsman said the success of drones has sparked a new push for autonomous ground robots.

"As drones have become ubiquitous, now ground robots are like the next thing and then eventually humanoid robots so robots that move and look like humans," he said.

Despite the push to advance military AI, Saltsman said safety can't take a back seat and that the technology is built using "transparent" datasets to "understand the biases" of the AI.

"That's another thing that differentiates us," he said. "One of the problems is how to use AI safely, how to put guardrails around it and how to understand it."

While the technology remains in the "development phase," Saltsman said the breakthrough gives robots the ability to understand what they see, not just detect it.

"You can put computer vision models on robots so they can see, but if they don't understand the context of what they're seeing, they're not useful and that's what we're solving for."

Kiera McDonald is a Production Assistant for Fox News Digital.

title: Todd Blanche’s attorney general nomination will advance to full US Senate vote
excerpt:
Blanche, one of Trump’s most trusted legal aides, had confirmed in writing that $1.8bn slush fund for president’s allies was dead

The US Senate judiciary committee voted along party lines to advance ...
body_text:
Blanche, one of Trump’s most trusted legal aides, had confirmed in writing that $1.8bn slush fund for president’s allies was dead

The US Senate judiciary committee voted along party lines to advance Todd Blanche’s nomination for attorney general after he confirmed in writing that a planned $1.8bn slush fund for Donald Trump’s allies was dead. Experts say, however, that Trump could easily reverse the deal.

His nomination will now proceed to the full Senate, where it will likely face intense skepticism from Democrats.

Ahead of the vote on Tuesday, every Democrat on the committee railed against Blanche’s nomination, saying he was unfit for the role and would do the president’s bidding. They emphasized his work defending the controversial fund, his mishandling of the files related to Jeffrey Epstein, the murder of Alex Pretti and Renee Good, and prosecutions of protesters and Trump’s political rivals.

“We are going to advance out of this committee probably the most discreditable person ever to seek the office of Attorney General of the United States,” said Sheldon Whitehouse, a Democratic senator from Rhode Island.

Blanche, one of Trump’s most trusted legal aides and formerly his personal defense lawyer, has faced questions over his suitability to lead the Department of Justice, which is supposed to operate independently of the White House.

He signed an order scrapping the so-called “anti-weaponization” fund – a roughly $1.8bn pool of money created in May as part of a settlement ending Trump’s lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service – in a bid to defuse a Republican rebellion over his nomination.

The lawsuit came after the leak of the US president’s confidential tax records by a former IRS contractor, who has been serving a prison sentence since 2024.

Trump had cast the fund as compensation for people he claimed were unfairly targeted by politically driven investigations, and defended it as recently as this weekend. Critics said it risked becoming a taxpayer-funded payout to Trump loyalists, including some defendants from the January 6 Capitol riot.

The most consequential criticism stemmed from two Republican members of the judiciary committee, John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina. Blanche’s nomination required their support.

But both outgoing senators have turned on Trump, recently telling party leaders they would not let Blanche’s confirmation move without firm guarantees that the fund would be shelved for good.

Speaking ahead of the vote on Tuesday, both Cornyn and Tillis said their concerns had been satisfied.

Tillis described the anti-weaponization fund as a “payout pot for punks”, but said he was satisfied it wouldn’t be moving forward.

“I’ve never liked this 1776 fund. It made no sense to me, and I thought it was an insult to the police officers and the people that defended us on January the sixth. It’s done. It’s been rescinded, and I am satisfied,” he said.

Despite saying he would vote for Blanche, Tillis lamented the politicization of the justice department under Blanche’s leadership. He criticized the department’s ongoing prosecution of the former FBI director James Comey in eastern North Carolina over a picture Comey posted with seashells arranged saying “86 47” – shorthand for getting rid of Trump.

“Some bonehead in North Carolina thinks that that’s a crime. Well, they better damn sure have information to back it up because if all it is is a picture, that person should lose his job, his or her job,” Tillis said.

Cornyn and Tillis faced public criticism from Trump over the weekend for pushing Blanche to put in writing that the anti-weaponization fund was dead and the scope of the tax immunity was limited. Cornyn defended the push on Tuesday.

“While this may sound like nitpicking to some, it’s critically important not only to me but to other members of the Senate,” Cornyn said. “Given this agreement with Mr Blanche, I expect the department to live up to to this in future litigation.”

Echoing the concerns of many other Democrats, Cory Booker, a Democratic senator from New Jersey, said the agreement with Blanche offered little assurance the justice department could not reverse itself and go ahead with the fund anyway.

“I’ve been here 14 years. I have not seen something as farcical as what I’ve witnessed over the last few weeks,” Booker said. “I’m going to say it very clear: this is all hat and no cattle.”

In his order, released on Sunday, Blanche stressed that the fund had never actually been operational: no board had been appointed, no money moved, and no claims filed or paid.

While there was concern that the settlement also provided broad immunity for Trump and members of his family from tax audits, the US Department of Justice separately clarified the IRS-related order was limited to the plaintiffs in the original settlement, and did not amount to blanket protection from future audits.

Both Cornyn and Tillis later confirmed they would vote to advance Blanche’s nomination.

Because the underlying settlement still references the fund, a future attorney general – or Trump himself, with Congress’s help – could try to revive it. Trump added to that uncertainty over the weekend, saying that if Blanche’s confirmation stalled, he would simply keep him on in an acting capacity and push lawmakers to create the fund through legislation instead.

title: Mass funeral in Gaza for 112 Palestinians killed in 2023 Israeli strike
excerpt:
Watch: Funeral for 112 people takes place in Gaza City

Large crowds turned out in Gaza City for a mass funeral for 112 people, mostly women and children, who were killed in an Israeli strike on a res...
body_text:
Watch: Funeral for 112 people takes place in Gaza City

Large crowds turned out in Gaza City for a mass funeral for 112 people, mostly women and children, who were killed in an Israeli strike on a residential block in late 2023, early in the Gaza war.

The bodies - belonging to members of two extended families - have only recently been recovered from under the rubble in a two-week-long operation.

Dramatic footage showed the remains lined up in rows, each victim covered with a Palestinian flag and some with a photo of the dead, before relatives carried them away.

The funeral is said to be the biggest of its kind to have taken place in Gaza.

"I think this is a feeling that was supposed [to be felt], a feeling of pain, grief and loss," said one mourner, Ali Abu Sharia. "After we managed to retrieve them and bury them, perhaps we can be partially relieved despite the pain of loss and all we're still living through."

Forty children, 38 women and seven people with disabilities were listed among the dead from the Abu Sharia and Hassayna families, who are one clan.

They were killed when a residential block in the Sabra neighbourhood of Gaza City was attacked by Israel on 22 November 2023.

It was a day of heavy bombardment, six weeks after the 7 October Hamas-led assault on southern Israel, which led to 1,200 people being killed and 251 being taken hostage.

The BBC has asked the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) for information on what was targeted but has not yet received a response.

Since the start of the war, at least 73,377 people have been killed in Gaza, according to the Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

Forty children were listed among the dead

In Gaza, the recovery work was carried out by the Civil Defence, which operates under the Hamas-run interior ministry. Its efforts have been supported by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC).

"We provide material support - literally the gloves, shovels, protective equipment and body bags they use," said Patrick Griffiths, spokesperson for the ICRC.

"We provide training, supporting them to do their work safely, in line with professional practice ensuring the deceased are treated with dignity. And we've supported them by renting - for hundreds of hours - two of the only excavators available for this work in Gaza."

"It's not an answer any family wants to receive - confirmation that your loved one has been killed," Griffiths added. "But it's essential towards them receiving closure and being able to mourn their loss in their own way."

Last month, the BBC filmed the start of the operation to uncover bodies in Sabra.  A single bulldozer picked through the rubble and then more delicate work was done by hand.

"This multi-storey building has been levelled. There were maybe more than 180 civilians inside. Most of them, around 90%, were killed," Civil Defence spokesman Mohammed Basel said at the time.

"On that day [of the strikes], the Civil Defence crews couldn't get to the site because it needed co-ordination [with Israel via a third party such as the ICRC] and there was great danger in reaching the area."

Relatives of the dead were at the scene to guide the recovery crews during the recovery work. They said they had retrieved as many bodies as they could immediately after the attack and were relieved to be able to give others a proper burial.

"It's a devastating and sad feeling that resonates with everyone who was here," said Nahed al-Hassayna, as he showed the BBC the rubble of his family's living room.

"The kids – what did they do?" he asked, holding up the possessions of two of his young relatives. "This was a school backpack for Omar, and this was Ibrahim's shoe. Why? Why were they killed?"

"I'm the sole survivor of my family," said Yousef Abu Sharia, standing nearby. "Today, I'm talking to you [as] the one who lost my mother, my father, my uncle and my cousins and all my family. I lost them under this rubble."

It is believed that dozens more bodies are yet to be recovered at the site.

Across the Gaza Strip, thousands more people are unaccounted for.  The remains of many are thought to be under the rubble left by intense Israeli air strikes during the war.

I had a few emailers Monday claim that my headlines were clickbait. Blah, blah, blah. The headline said Macy Kate and then I had Macy Kate in the post. I can't help it if you're using some old flip phone that won't load Instagram embeds. Tough luck.

Paulina Gretzky, wife of Team Captain Dustin Johnson of 4 Aces GC, is seen during Day Three of the LIV Golf Invitational - Chicago at Rich Harvest Farms on September 18, 2022 in Sugar Grove, Illinois. (Getty Images)

KEY TRUMP AGENCY PUTS TOP UNIVERSITIES IN CROSSHAIRS OVER ALLEGED RACE-BASED DORM PROGRAMS

Kevin emailed in saying his wife had dropped $800 on their daughter's dorm room on things like a padded headboard, sheets, a comforter, etc. That price sounded outrageous to me. Over the last 24 hours, I've learned that many of you are paying for wall decorations, and all sorts of non-essentials.

And as someone who once literally packed everything for a vacation except for underwear I am smart enough to have my wife handle everything.

She’s having a great time because she selects things and offers him choices and 99% of the time the answer is "I don’t care, anything is fine".

Our list is coming out a little less than $700 for the necessities which includes things like an iron.

I think we all know that’s going to go unused.

If you include the additional $250 for cold weather gear that we don’t need in Hawaii it gets to be a little more than $900

I don’t know if Kevin’s aware of it but he might be getting off easy because my wife says there are actually outfits out there that specialize in dorm décor which includes design themes and professional set up. He can also take comfort in the fact that his daughter’s food bill isn’t going to be nearly what it is for a 175 lb. kid that likes to lift weights.

– Brandon in NW Houston is living through this stage of life right now: Slightly different take on dorms in 2026. I don't know how it was for you, but when I went to Southwest Texas back in 1991, I had some clothes, a TV, and a gleam in my eye. Our youngest is off to OK State in a week, and mom has been going crazy on his dorm. We have enough Amazon boxes to build a 1:1 scale fort out of them. I'm talking hanging organizer for the closet, medical kit, shoe rack, mattress pad, fan on a clip, light on a clip, etc etc. Hell, she had me calling carpet stores to look for carpet to put on top of the carpet in the dorm! Granted, the stuff in the room is probably pretty gross, but what's wrong with a rug??

He's about at his wits' end, but he understands that it isn't about him; this is all about her making sure he has everything he could possibly need and is comfortable.

RILEY GAINES SAYS WNBA IS 'HELLBENT' ON BEING AN ACTIVIST ORGANIZATION OVER A BASKETBALL LEAGUE

This is very out of character for her, but it's her baby boy. She got him into running (XC, 24-hour relays, marathons, etc) and they've really had some good/bonding times with it the last few years.

– Travel Ball Hardo Chris B. in Houston said on Facebook: 800 is not a surprising number. mattress pad, sheets, pillows, comforter, lamp(s), decorations, mini frig?, misc supplies, etc. it adds up faaaaast.

Kinsey: Decorations? Sheets are like $20 on Amazon and they're going to puke on the sheets anyway.

– Hardo: I’m not suggesting you bid on the Mona Lisa, but they are gonna wanna hang stuff on the walls. Moving away can be hard. They need to make it their home.

– Diesel added: Dorm rooms should be decorated with finished cases of Busch light lol

Kinsey: Thank you for saying it, Diesel. Look, I get it for those of you with daughters. But, spending a bunch of money on decorations for your son's dorm room, if that's happening, is nuts. What happened to buying weed posters at Spencer's at the mall and calling the room decorated?

The more I think about it, the more into focus it's becoming why our college students are coming out of school feeling entitled to jobs with high salaries, great time off and the theory they should be able to afford a 10-year-old 2,500 sq. ft. house with four bedrooms on a half-acre lot with great trees.

They aren't being told to go get a job to buy their own decorations. Yes, I will buy you sheets that you'll puke on, but you'll have to come up with your own At Home budget for 40 fuzzy pillows so your bed looks cool on Instagram.

– Jake C. asks: Do you think the WNBA ends up collapsing sooner rather than later? The vast majority do not want politics in sports at all, let alone 24/7, yet this league keeps doubling down.

Kinsey: Later. As someone in my position, I don't want the Dubya to collapse. It's a content machine. Did you see the latest from Angel Reese where she claims there weren't dolls to play with when she was a kid because they were all white dolls? That's the continous nonsense these idiots provide to a website like OutKick. Honestly, our job has never been easier. 5-10 years ago, summers were horrible for content.

Our July numbers were through the roof. On Facebook, we just had 45.5 million views during the month and much of that was thanks to these woke idiots. Let them double, triple and quadruple down. We'll keep battling them. There's literally nobody else on this battlefield. It's OutKick vs. the WNBA.

– Mark T. in Florida says: Not a follower of the WNBA but you can't help put notice how they are not a serious league but a political activist association trying to disguise as sport. The Commissioner needs firing and a host of league personnel and officials should be out of a job as well. From media credentials being denied to in arena posters trying to be banned, coaches wearing activist clothing on the sidelines and officials showing complete bias; ghosting interviews that possibly could ask uncomfortable questions its hard to believe people are wasting money on a garbage product.

The games aren't even the show now, its the nonsense in around and off the court that's taken the spotlight. They are what they are; a non-serious activist association.

Kinsey: Mark gets it. Name another outlet that's willing to take on these activists. ESPN? The Athletic? LOLOLOLOLOL.

– Mark in SC emails: Opinion---I just looked up Lawrence Taylor stats & accordingly it appears Luke had 4 more solo tackles than Taylor.

Not a huge Panther fan yet I respect all the players as they keep trying to overcome their QB issues as Young is to small & the number of times he's been sacked shows it. I think Tepper needs an outsider to teach him how to build a good team.

Kinsey: At just 35 years old, Kuechly goes into the Pro Football Hall of Fame this week.

– Pat H. in Stonington, CT couldn't believe his eyes when he read Monday Screencaps: Oh my God, I remember the GA! Plenty of my friends worked there loading clays; nothing like working in a box in the middle of August, with the sun beating down on a barren landscape, just make gas money and some Friday night jingle.

I went to the GA a few times, just marveling at the exquisite Krieghoff and Perazzi shotguns that actually cost a purported $100,000, and being tossed around in the back of a Range Rover, because the gun was actually free to the owner! I couldn’t wrap my teenage head around that, any more than I could comprehend using the airport as the backstop to thousands of pellets hurtled in the general direction!

I grew up in Englewood, OH. Joined the Navy in ‘86, and never looked back. Thanks for the memory jolt!

Guys, I promise it's OK to tell your sons you've cut their dorm decorating budget. And it's time for you to send this column to your wives so they stop blowing through money that can eventually be spent on a house down payment for your kids.

You should be good to go this morning. Let's go get after it. There's work to do, America.

Joe Kinsey is the Senior Director of Content of OutKick.

title: Jordan convenes emergency meeting over Israel’s potential to ‘trigger religious conflict’
excerpt:
Country convenes emergency meeting of ministers from Arab and Islamic world, fearing such a move could ‘trigger a religious conflict’

Jordan is convening an emergency meeting of foreign ministers fro...
body_text:
Country convenes emergency meeting of ministers from Arab and Islamic world, fearing such a move could ‘trigger a religious conflict’

Jordan is convening an emergency meeting of foreign ministers from the Arab and Islamic world over what it says is an “imminent” threat of an Israeli takeover of the most important religious site in Jerusalem, with the potential to “trigger a religious conflict”.

The meeting on Wednesday – and the Jordanian warning – follow an escalating pattern of government-backed incursions by Jewish religious extremists on the compound around the al-Aqsa mosque and Dome of the Rock, in violation of a status quo treaty overseen by Jordan’s Hashemite monarchy, by which only Muslims can pray at the site.

On 23 July, more than 2,000 Israelis from the religious right – mostly settlers led by the national security minister, Itamar Ben Gvir – stormed the area, known to Jews as the Temple Mount. They prayed and performed rituals all around the compound in what Jordanian officials said was the worst violation in modern history.

Amman has also been alarmed at a recent recruitment drive for religious Jews for a special Temple Mount police unit, and is braced for more direct challenges to traditional Jordanian custodianship by extremist Israeli leaders in the major Jewish holidays in September. This year, those holidays will come amid an intense election campaign, in which the far-right coalition of the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, will be fighting for survival.

“This is a constant threat, a dangerous threat that we’re trying to counter in every tool that we have possible,” Jordan’s foreign minister, Ayman Safadi, told the Guardian. “We warn that tampering with the status quo … could trigger a religious conflict that will reverberate beyond Palestine and Jordan into the whole Muslim world.”

Safadi, who will host Wednesday’s emergency meeting, bringing together his counterparts from Arab League countries, as well as Turkey, Indonesia, Malaysia and Pakistan, said it was “something that the whole international community should be aware of. Jerusalem is a tinderbox.

“We’re trying to explain the danger. We’re protesting legally. We are trying to create awareness of the imminent danger in the continuation of those Israeli measures.”

Jordan’s custodianship of the al-Aqsa compound dates back to Ottoman times, and the status quo encompassing the city’s religious sites was enshrined in the 1878 Treaty of Berlin. The Hashemite kingdom’s oversight in Jerusalem was expanded to cover Christian holy sites in the 20th century, and its custodianship was reaffirmed after the 1967 war, and in the 1994 Israeli-Jordanian peace treaty.

Infringement by Jewish extremists triggered riots in the British Mandate period between the world wars, and a 2000 visit to the compound by the right-wing leader Ariel Sharon, soon to become the Israeli prime minister, ignited more than four years of violence in the second intifada.

Jordan is uniquely vulnerable to the impact of Israel’s broader ethnic cleansing campaign in the West Bank, which Amman fears may also escalate dramatically as the October elections loom. There is anxiety over what the Israeli government might do in the three months before the vote, as radical elements seek to change the geography of the region in ways which could be difficult to reverse.

For Jordan, the worst-case scenario is an attempt at the mass deportation of Palestinians from the West Bank, which would destabilise the country in several ways, including economic costs, the political impact of an influx of an angry, dispossessed population, and threats to the country’s delicate demographic balance.

“Our position that this is a red line that we will not allow to be crossed. We have made that known to everybody that we will do whatever it takes to prevent any attempt at Israeli displacement of Palestinians into Jordan,” Safadi said. “Not only will that be a violation of international law and of the right of the Palestinians to stay on their land, but that will also be a tremendous escalation.”

Jordanians descended from previous waves of Palestinian refugees already represent more than half of Jordan’s 11.5-million population, and the country’s original residents, the “East Bankers”, are wary of what they see as a further dilution of national identity.

Israel has already refused to renew a 2021 water agreement under which it shared 100m cubic metres a year to its parched neighbour, one of the most water-scarce countries in the world. It reverted to the 50m cubic metres originally agreed in the 1994 treaty, which falls far short of the needs of a much bigger population than the Jordan of 32 years ago.

The Israeli government reportedly halved the water supply in retaliation for criticism from the Jordanian government of the mass killing of Palestinian civilians by Israel in the Gaza war, and officials have hinted that the taps could be turned back on if the criticism ended.

The Israeli government’s provocative actions in Jerusalem and the West Bank and over water raise the political cost to the monarchy of maintaining normal relations with its western neighbour.

“Anti-normalisation sentiment here has grown even larger than before due to the Zionist state’s plans of annexation of the West Bank, the denial of Jordan’s share in the water agreement and also the daily challenges to the custodianship at the al-Aqsa mosque,” said Dima Tahboub, a member of parliament and spokesperson for Jordan’s Islamist Umma party. “Every day there is penetration by settlers into the al-Aqsa mosque and at the same time, [Palestinian] Jerusalemites are prevented from entering the mosque.”

Tahboub’s party is Jordan’s biggest political bloc, known as the Islamic Action Front (IAF) until earlier this year when it was ordered to adopt a less ideological name. Its rise has largely been driven by events on the other side of the River Jordan, and the Gaza war helped it win over 22% of the available seats.

The surge in political Islam came as a shock to the monarchy, which slowed down its plans for political reform and the transfer of more power to parliament as a result. The Muslim Brotherhood movement was outlawed last year and IAF, which operates as its political arm, had its offices raided. It has, however, been allowed to continue as a party, under the name of Umma, which means “community” or “nation”.

Tahboub said there was more the government could be doing to rally international support to resist Israel’s encroachments.

“I think more pressure can be exerted. The issue is not being put to the table with the force that it needs,” she said, while stressing that the Umma party stood together with the Jordanian government in the face of its adversaries, and that it understood the limitations imposed by geography and economics which have left it significantly dependent on the US for its economic and security needs.

Unlike other Gulf monarchies, Jordan has not allowed the US its own military bases on its territory, but there is a US presence on Jordanian bases, which has grown significantly since the start of the US war with Iran. Amman has sought to play down the presence of US forces, planes and other equipment, but that has been made harder by repeated successful Iranian airstrikes, which have killed three Americans and injured scores at the Muwaffaq Salti base in the eastern desert.

For decades the US military presence has been seen as a security guarantee for Jordan, but it has also proved to be a political liability, especially as the Jordanian air force has found itself serving as Israel’s first line of defence shooting down Iranian drones and missiles heading towards Tel Aviv.

Last month, several hundred prominent figures from politics, the law and Jordanian cultural life signed an open letter calling for the withdrawal of US forces, in a rare direct challenge to the government.

The letter said: “We maintain that their presence exposes Jordan to security, political, and economic risks that serve no national interest and increases the likelihood of our country being dragged into a regional conflict to which it is not a party.”
