title: Hero sheepdog becomes unlikely rescue partner after unexpected move aids first responders
excerpt:
A sheepdog jumped into action herding a field full of goats out of the way so first responders could safely touch down in Laguna Beach, California.

A Southern California sheepdog is being hailed as a...
body_text:
A sheepdog jumped into action herding a field full of goats out of the way so first responders could safely touch down in Laguna Beach, California.

A Southern California sheepdog is being hailed as an honorary first responder after police drone video captured the hardworking pup helping clear the way for an emergency helicopter.

The Laguna Beach Police Department shared drone video Friday showing officers and firefighters responding to an emergency in the city's foothills as crews prepared a landing zone for a helicopter.

As crews worked on the ground, a hardworking white sheepdog sprang into action, herding a nearby group of goats away from the landing area and helping keep the helicopter's path clear.

Drone video released by the department shows the dog weaving behind the herd as dozens of goats move up the hillside and away from the helicopter's approach.

FBI, ATLANTA POLICE TARGET UNAUTHORIZED DRONES FLYING NEAR WORLD CUP VENUES

A herd of goats moves across a hillside as an emergency helicopter approaches during a Laguna Beach rescue response. (Laguna Beach Police Department)

At one point, the camera zooms in on the pup happily trotting across the hillside with its tail wagging after completing its impromptu mission.

"The sheepdog stepped up and helped guide a group of goats out of the way so the units could work," the Laguna Beach Police Department wrote in a social media post. "That's a good boy."

Officials have not publicly released details about the emergency response or what prompted the helicopter deployment.

CRUISE PASSENGER HAILED AS HERO AFTER JUMPING INTO WATER TO SAVE 84-YEAR-OLD MAN

Southern California sheepdog earned praise as an honorary first responder after drone video showed it herding goats away from a helicopter landing zone during an emergency response in Laguna Beach. (iStock)

The feel-good video quickly won over social media, where viewers crowned the four-legged helper "Sgt. Sheepdog" and praised the pup for calmly guiding the herd of goats out of the way.

DOG SAVED FROM ISIS BY ARMY VETERAN 'KIDNAPPED' FROM FAMILY YARD BY LOCAL AUTHORITIES

A Laguna Beach Police Department patrol SUV parked along a street in Laguna Beach, California. (Laguna Beach Police Department)

The Laguna Beach Police Department appeared to agree, writing simply, "That's a good boy."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Laguna Beach Police Department and the Laguna Beach Fire Department for additional information about the emergency response, including what prompted the helicopter deployment and for comment.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Ms Rachel claims 'no one needs a billion dollars,' endorses Democratic progressives Abdul El-Sayed, Cori Bush
excerpt: Hosts on 'Fox & Friends' discuss far-left activists' anti-ICE protests at facilities like Delaney Hall in Newark, N.J., where nearly 100 people were arrested. YouTuber Ms. Rachel, popular for children...
body_text:
Hosts on 'Fox & Friends' discuss far-left activists' anti-ICE protests at facilities like Delaney Hall in Newark, N.J., where nearly 100 people were arrested. YouTuber Ms. Rachel, popular for children's content, is shown leading sing-alongs with kids at the facility, raising questions about politicalization.

Popular children's YouTube educator Ms. Rachel backed a dozen progressive Democratic candidates on Friday, including former Rep. Cori Bush, D-Mo., and Michigan U.S. Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed, using her audience of more than five million followers to promote candidates she believed cared about children.

"I think all kids and people should have medical care. I don’t think anyone needs a billion dollars ever, I think all kids should be safe from violence," Accurso said in a post on Instagram.

Accurso's slate covered House and Senate contests in eight states. It also included Vermont Rep. Becca Balint, Minnesota Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, former Maine Senate President Troy Jackson, Florida state Rep. Angie Nixon and former Tennessee state Rep. Justin Pearson.

YOUTUBE STAR MS RACHEL GIVES FUNDS TO DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST MICHIGAN SENATE HOPEFUL ABDUL EL-SAYED

Ms. Rachel endorsed Cori Bush, Abdul El-Sayed and 10 other progressive candidates, telling her five million Instagram followers she backs those who protect kids. (Nathan Congleton/NBC via Getty Images)

"These are the folks I believe care about all kids," Accurso said.

Bush, who is seeking to reclaim her former St. Louis-area seat from Rep. Wesley Bell in Tuesday’s Democratic primary, is a Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) member. In early July, Bush said in a post on X that she was proud to be re-endorsed by the DSA.

"Together, we’ll work to abolish ICE, deliver Medicare for all, end wars overseas, and achieve true economic justice," Bush said.

EX-'SQUAD' MEMBER FIGHTS FOR COMEBACK AS SOCIALIST WING RAMPS UP WAR ON DEM ESTABLISHMENT

Children’s educator Rachel Griffin Accurso, has more than 20 million YouTube subscribers. (Maxine Wallace/The Washington Post via Getty Images)

El-Sayed rejected the socialist label during a Tuesday interview with MS NOW host Jen Psaki despite him receiving endorsements from Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio Cortez, D-N.Y., El-Sayed spoke at six DSA events between 2017 and 2020.

"I’m simply not a socialist ... I've studied a lot of the solutions that I fight for," El-Sayed said to Psaki. "Things like Medicare-for-all, things like rethinking the way that our financial system implies that corporate CEOs are more interested in a quarterly bottom line than they are in the long-term sustainability of their business."

El-Sayed’s campaign platform calls for Medicare-for-all, taxing billionaire wealth and banning corporate money in politics.

A federal filing also listed a $3,000 payment from Accurso to his campaign ahead of Tuesday’s Michigan primary against Rep. Haley Stevens. The filing did not specify whether the payment was a contribution or a loan.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

In her post, Ms. Rachel said that politicians "shouldn’t attack each other." (Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images)

Accurso also connected her endorsements to the influx of what she described as outside money in Democratic primaries.

"I think politicians shouldn’t attack each other and I don’t think big groups should be able to use millions to attack candidates," Accurso said.

The National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC) previously criticized Accurso's financial support for El-Sayed, whose platform calls for an arms embargo against Israel.

NRSC spokeswoman Samantha Cantrell addressed the two in a statement to the New York Post in July.

"Abdul El-Sayed and Ms. Rachel are one and the same, forcing their socialist, they/them, anti-America agenda on our children," Cantrell said.

Ms Rachel also recently weighed in on the investigation into Nolan Wells’ mysterious death, with a now-viral social media post pointing to unsupported allegations that race played a role in law enforcement’s handling of the case. (Nathan Congleton/NBC via Getty Images; Christine Wonsley/Facebook)

Accurso has increasingly used her platform, which includes a YouTube channel with more than 20 million subscribers, for political advocacy.

In June, Accurso visited Delaney Hall, an immigration detention facility in Newark, New Jersey, and traveled to Washington to urge Congress to end family detention and separation.

Accurso said on Wednesday that she is involved with politics because she cares "so much about kids and families everywhere," and said she could not watch them suffer and "not stand with them" in an Instagram post where she simultaneously endorsed El-Sayed.

Fox News Digital reached out to Accurso, Bush, the DSA and El-Sayed for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

CJ Womack is an associate editor at Fox News.

CJ joined Fox News Digital's team in 2026, which highlights the vital role journalism plays in shaping politics and culture. He has years of experience analyzing and reporting on the news media.

CJ graduated from Long Beach State University in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science and a minor in Journalism.

You can send news tips to cj.womack@fox.com and follow CJ on Twitter.

title: Entire Squad endorses Abdul El-Sayed days before Michigan Democratic Senate primary
excerpt: Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed said during an interview that he was "simply not a socialist" when pressed on his association with prominent left-wing leaders such as Bernie Sanders and Rep. ...
body_text:
Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed said during an interview that he was "simply not a socialist" when pressed on his association with prominent left-wing leaders such as Bernie Sanders and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.

Every member of the "Squad," an informal left-wing congressional caucus, has endorsed Abdul El-Sayed ahead of Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary, according to his campaign website.

The Squad is made up of Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., Ayanna Pressley, D-Mass., Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich., Summer Lee, D-Pa., Delia Ramirez, D-Ill., and Greg Casar, D-Texas.

Many of the squad’s current and former members have past or ongoing affiliations with the Democratic Socialists of America, an organization El-Sayed is attempting to distance himself from as he attempts to moderate ahead of a swing-state general election.

The unified endorsements sharpen the ideological stakes of the Tuesday primary, linking El-Sayed to the party’s most prominent progressive bloc even as he rejects the socialist label and seeks to present himself as a viable candidate in a battleground state. The support also gives Republicans an early line of attack should El-Sayed defeat the more centrist Stevens and advance to the general election.

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., is among the members of the Congressional Progressive Caucus. (Alex Wong/Getty Images)

DEM PRIMARY ERUPTS AS ESTABLISHMENT FAVORITE DISMISSES RIVAL AS ‘CELEBRITY CANDIDATE’

"The entire Squad has now endorsed Abdul El-Sayed to carry on its radical, socialist, anti-American agenda in the U.S. Senate, and they will be rejected by Michiganders at the ballot box," National Republican Senatorial Committee regional press secretary Samantha Cantrell told Fox News Digital.

Casar was the most recent Squad member to endorse El-Sayed, throwing his support behind him Thursday.

"Abdul El-Sayed is showing what it means to run a bold, pro-working class campaign," Casar said. "House progressives need strong partners in the Senate in order to put money in your pocket, get money out of politics, and win Medicare for All. I’m proud to endorse Abdul."

SOCIALIST-BACKED DEM WHO RIPPED THE WEALTHY CRACKS STATE’S TOP 1%, TAX RETURNS SHOW

Every member of the "Squad," an informal left-wing congressional caucus, has endorsed Abdul El-Sayed ahead of Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary. (Sarah Rice/Getty Images)

Casar, Ocasio-Cortez, Tlaib and Lee all have current or former Democratic Socialists of America affiliations. El-Sayed at one point even appeared at a Democratic Socialists of America event alongside Tlaib.

El-Sayed headlined that event, a fundraiser that brought in roughly $10,000 for the Detroit Democratic Socialists of America, and was photographed next to Tlaib behind a table with a poster on it depicting a hand labeled "DSA" choking a snake labeled "capitalism."

The Michigan Senate hopeful attended and spoke at six Democratic Socialists of America events between 2017 and 2020, Fox News Digital previously reported. Organizers affiliated with the socialist organization have described El-Sayed as "a longtime friend of Detroit DSA."

ABDUL EL-SAYED SAYS RALLYING WITH HASAN PIKER DOESN'T MEAN HE ENDORSES 'AMERICA DESERVED 9/11' REMARK

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and Sen. Bernie Sanders join hands following a campaign rally on July 18, 2026, in Detroit. (AP Photo/Jose Juarez)

Despite pulling in endorsements from socialists and his longtime association with the Democratic Socialists of America, El-Sayed rejects the socialist label and has distanced himself from the group.

"I'm not technically or practically DSA," El-Sayed told The Wall Street Journal in early July.

In an interview with CNN, he said, "I am not somebody who is a socialist. I believe in capitalism, I just believe that capitalism has to be regulated."

El-Sayed faces off against Rep. Haley Stevens in Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary Tuesday. Stevens is widely viewed as the more centrist of the two. Polls generally show El-Sayed leading Stevens by a comfortable margin, according to the New York Times.

The El-Sayed campaign did not respond to a request for comment.

title: Ukrainian drone attacks kill eight in response to Russian missiles
excerpt:
Swarms of drones launched overnight by Ukraine towards targets in multiple Russian regions have killed at least eight people, despite Russia saying it successfully shot down 635.

The deaths announced...
body_text:
Swarms of drones launched overnight by Ukraine towards targets in multiple Russian regions have killed at least eight people, despite Russia saying it successfully shot down 635.

The deaths announced by regional governors on Sunday included three killed by a drone strike on a car in the Udmurtia region, more than 1,300 kilometres (800 miles) beyond the Ukrainian front line.

“This act is monstrous in its senselessness. These people were definitely not a military target,” acting Governor Olga Abramova said on Telegram.

In the Saratov region, civilian infrastructure was hit in the cities of Saratov and Engels, and two people were killed when a residential building in Engels was struck, Governor Roman Busargin said.

Both Saratov city, which hosts a major oil refinery, and Engels, home of a strategic bomber airbase, have come under repeated Ukrainian attack in recent years.

Ukraine’s military said it had attacked ⁠the Saratov refinery and the Engels airbase, sparking fires at both facilities. It said its forces had also struck an oil ⁠depot in the western Kaluga region.

In the Belgorod region bordering Ukraine, three people were killed and five wounded in Ukrainian strikes, the local task ‌force reported.

Ukrainian drones also attacked a Wildberries warehouse in the Samara region, around 800 km (500 miles) from Ukraine’s most advanced military ⁠positions, Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev said. He said there were no casualties and that a fire that had broken out as a result of the attack was being put out.

Ukrainian forces have been striking deeper inside Russia as they expand strikes on economic and energy targets, ‌hoping to undermine Moscow’s ability to wage its more than four-year-old war in Ukraine.

They have attacked about a dozen Wildberries sites since July 18 in a bid to disrupt the operations of the company, a linchpin of the consumer economy often described as Russia’s answer to Amazon.

In Ukraine, one person died on Sunday as a Russian guided bomb struck a residential building in the southern city of Zaporizhzhia, according to local administration head Ivan Fedorov. Another attack on Sunday killed one person and set fire to a postal terminal on the outskirts of Kharkiv, in the northwest, regional administration head Oleh Syniehubov said.

Both sides are increasingly using long-range missiles and drones to attack each other far beyond the front lines.

Data compiled by AFP from Ukrainian Air Force reports revealed that Russia fired a record 376 missiles at Ukraine in July, more than double the total launched in June, with most targeted at Kyiv.

The intensified ballistic campaign killed more than 170 civilians between July 1 and July 27 according to UN figures, culminating in an overnight barrage on Friday that killed at least nine people and wounded 33 in the Ukrainian capital.

During that attack, Russia launched 220 aerial weapons, including 35 missiles, 27 of them ballistic, and 185 drones.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said air defence units intercepted 154 drones but only one ballistic missile, because of a critical shortage of US-supplied Patriot interceptor missiles.

title: Man arrested after Scottish woman found dead inside suitcase in Athens
excerpt:
Greek police say 26-year-old Afghan national is believed to have left Elisabeth-Jane Ross’s body in derelict building

Greek authorities have arrested an Afghan national in connection with the death o...
body_text:
Greek police say 26-year-old Afghan national is believed to have left Elisabeth-Jane Ross’s body in derelict building

Greek authorities have arrested an Afghan national in connection with the death of a Scottish woman whose body was found in a suitcase in an abandoned building in central Athens.

Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, a charity worker described as an “angel full of innocence and goodness” by friends, had been in Greece for almost three weeks when she is believed to have died.

Police sources said the suspect was a 26-year-old Afghan citizen who had allegedly confessed to the crime. He had been brought in for questioning by Greece’s homicide division last Thursday, two days after Ross’s body was publicly identified.

A statement released by police on Sunday said: “A criminal file has been opened against a 26-year-old foreign national for intentional homicide, robbery and violation of the law [regarding] weapons.”

Explaining the accusation of ownership of illegal weapons, security officials said “various arms – some real, some fake” had been discovered in the suspect’s home, also thought to be in the downtown area of Kypseli where the body was discovered.
 He is expected to be charged on Monday.

Throughout the investigation, Greek authorities had worked closely with the UK’s National Crime Agency (NCA) and Police Scotland, according to the statement.

Ross, who had strong links with the charity sector in Greece, is the daughter of a prominent lawyer in Edinburgh, where she also lived.

She was reported to have friends in Kypseli, where her body was discovered on 18 July by a homeless man in what had once been a car park. Wrapped in cloth, it had been placed in a suitcase left in a decrepit, rubbish-strewn building at the site.

Sources told the Guardian that the suspect’s alleged use of credit cards that belonged to Ross had contributed to police identifying him.

“He was caught on camera withdrawing money with the cards from various ATMs,” one said. “The credit cards belonged to Ms Ross. That played a big role in leading us to him.”

For days, investigators were unable to make headway, citing the lack of fingerprints or DNA on the suitcase. Adding to the mystery was the discovery that her mobile phone had been used until the time when the body was publicly identified last week.

Police had described text messages sent to her father and other members of her family as deliberately misleading. The messages had spoken of her “need to be alone”.

The Briton’s “dispersed movements” in the days leading up to her death had made the quest to track her killer even harder.

After leaving the home of close friends in Keratsini, a suburb close to the port of Piraeus, where she had stayed for two weeks after flying to Greece, she had gone her own way, renting an apartment in the district of Exarchia in downtown Athens.

Greek media outlets reported the suspect had been found in possession of the keys to the rental apartment and that he was “the partner” of one of the Briton’s friends.

“As confirmed, the victim arrived in the country on June 26 and stayed at the home of friends until July 10, from where she departed to an unknown [address],” the police statement said.

The homicide division said it had made the announcement after amassing evidence that proved the Afghan had “placed the body in the case and carried it to the abandoned car park” in Kypseli.

Analysis of CCTV footage had played a role.

“The subsequent preliminary investigation … using investigative material and digital analysis of video footage, proved the involvement of the 26-year-old foreign national in the incident. [He] was brought in [for questioning] on 30 July and confessed to his actions,” the statement said.

It remains unknown how Ross died. Media reports quoted the suspect as telling police that when he visited the flat in Exarchia he had discovered her lifeless body in the bathroom.

An initial on-site postmortem showed there were no evident signs of injury or struggle on the Briton’s body but proved inconclusive because of advanced decomposition. Authorities have fast-tracked toxicological tests and analysis of vital organ tissues to determine the cause of death.

Grigoris Leon, who heads the Hellenic Society of Forensic Medicine, told the Guardian that examination of the lungs and eyes would help provide answers and determine “whether she had died a natural death”.

As tributes have poured in, flowers have been left beside the abandoned lot in Kypseli. One note read: “Here lies an angel.”

One friend in Edinburgh agreed with that, saying: “We have lost an angel, an angel full of innocence and goodness who only wanted to help people wherever she went.”The UK Foreign Office previously said: “Our thoughts are with Elisabeth’s family during this difficult time. We are providing consular support and are in contact with the local authorities.”

A Police Scotland spokesperson said: “We are aware of the death of a Scottish woman in Athens and are liaising with authorities in Greece. Officers are providing support to her family in Scotland.”

title: RFK Jr tells US families to vaccinate children against measles amid outbreak
excerpt:
Health secretary, longtime vaccination skeptic, spent years boosting misinformation about vaccines including MMR

Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US health secretary, on Sunday told American parents that the...
body_text:
Health secretary, longtime vaccination skeptic, spent years boosting misinformation about vaccines including MMR

Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US health secretary, on Sunday told American parents that they should get their children vaccinated against measles, as the surge in infections has reached numbers not seen in the past 35 years.

Kennedy, a leading vaccination skeptic who has spent years amplifying misinformation about vaccines, including the shot that protects against measles, mumps and rubella (MMR), made his call in the course of a contentious interview with CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday morning.

His remark came as the incidence of measles crossed a milestone – the US has now officially recorded 2,371 confirmed infections so far this year, surpassing the total tally in 2025 of 2,289.

Taken together, the past two years have seen more measles infections in the US than the rest of the 21st century combined. The last time a greater number of measles cases were recorded in a single year was in 1991.

Kennedy’s statement was extracted from him by Dana Bash, CNN’s host, who invited him to use his “bully pulpit” to talk directly to parents as the new school year approached. She urged him to tell families that they should vaccinate for measles “because it is safe and it will help them save their children’s lives”.

The health secretary replied: “Parents should get their children vaccinated for measles. A measles vaccine is effective, it stops measles in about 97% of the cases. People should get vaccinated.”

Later in the interview he added that people should also get the combined measles, mumps and rubella vaccine, the main protection against the disease that has been a particular target of the anti-vaccination movement.

The health secretary’s call for parents to vaccinate their children for measles contrasts starkly with the many years in which Kennedy has been a leading proponent of misinformation questioning the efficacy and safety of vaccinations. Even since he became the country’s top health official, he has depicted a measles vaccination as a personal choice and claimed inaccurately that the power of the inoculation is waning.

The call also comes late in the day, given the rate at which measles is spreading in the US. The 37 new measles outbreaks that have already been recorded this year are putting the US in danger of losing the measles elimination status that it has held since 2000.

Kennedy continues to shrug off criticism that his work as a prominent vaccine skeptic, both before and after he entered the Trump administration, has exacerbated the problem. Asked whether he took any responsibility for the measles surge, he said: “Absolutely not.”

He went on to blame the outbreaks on religious communities who eschew vaccines and on global health conditions.

Any hope that Kennedy’s measles statement might indicate a change of heart were dashed in the rest of the CNN interview in which he turned combative. Batting off questions from Bash, the health secretary responded with personal attacks.

He accused the CNN host of “saying nonsense”, “repeating like a parrot” and “making assertions you can’t support”. In one especially demeaning remark he said Bash had become “flustered”.

“I’m not flustered at all,” she asserted in a calm voice. “I am frustrated because you are the HHS secretary and you are talking about things that lead to vaccine hesitancy in this country.”

In a further comment dripping with condescension, Kennedy told Bash “you probably don’t understand this because you’re not a scientist”.

The journalist riposted: “But you’re not, either.”

Kennedy used the CNN exchange to spread further misinformation about other aspects of public health. He claimed that both respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) that is a major cause of infant mortality and Lyme disease were caused by manipulation of germs in laboratories.

The suggestion has been contradicted by decades of scientific evidence that suggest they both have natural roots. RSV was initially identified in the 1950s, two decades before such experimentation, known as “gain-of-function” research, started.

During the interview, Kennedy repeated unfounded claims that there was a link between Tylenol use during pregnancy and autism, and poured doubt on the efficacy of vaccines to protect children against Covid-19.

Speaking to CNN’s State of the Union later in the show, Ashish Jha, who advised Joe Biden’s White House on its Covid response, said he was heartened to hear Kennedy say that “every kid in America should be getting the MMR vaccine”. But he added that much else of what the health secretary had said “just isn’t true”.

Jha said that the dramatic rise in measles cases on Kennedy’s watch was not coincidental. “The administration has not done enough to promote vaccines. It has not done enough to highlight the harms that come from measles.”

title: ‘Iron fist’ doesn’t work with Iran: Former US hostage in Tehran
excerpt:
