Republican candidate Christy Peterson, a local accountant, is also running in the Nov. 3 general election, which Kiros is widely expected to win given the district's strongly blue lean. In 2024, Kamala Harris won 77 percent of the vote in the district en route to winning Colorado.

Despite the tension, some community leaders like Rattiner say they aren't giving up on dialogue if Kiros is elected in November.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"The Jewish community doesn't want to be in a state of permanent warfare with any representative," Rattiner said. "I sincerely hope that Melat Kiros will listen to our community and educate herself about the policies and positions that she has and the implications in the Jewish community. But I think what she may have even more of an opportunity to do is use her credibility on the left to help elevate concerns of the Jewish people so that when the Jewish people do call out in pain, when they express their fear and concern, it's not written off."

Kiros' campaign was backed by several progressive groups, including the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), Justice Democrats, and the Working Families Party. She became the 28th candidate endorsed by a far-left group to win a Democratic primary election this cycle as the socialist movement continues to increase its influence across the nation.

Kiros' campaign, Shimon Blau, and the DSA did not return Fox News Digital’s requests for comment.

Kristine Parks is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Read more.

title: Ramaswamy outlines key contrasts with Dem opponent less than 100 days out from key gubernatorial election
excerpt:
Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy told Fox News Digital about his plans to cut taxes and create jobs while criticizing Democratic rival Amy Acton's COVID-era leadership.

HAMILTON, OH...
body_text:
Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy told Fox News Digital about his plans to cut taxes and create jobs while criticizing Democratic rival Amy Acton's COVID-era leadership.

HAMILTON, OHIO - Ohio Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy gave Fox News Digital an update on his campaign roughly 100 days from the midterms and said the contrast between him and his opponent was on display at Dr. Anthony Fauci’s controversial Senate hearing this week.

"I think if every person in Ohio votes for the candidate who's going to bring high-paying jobs most quickly to our state, we're going to win in a decisive victory," Ramaswamy said at the Butler County Fair on Wednesday after speaking to an enthusiastic crowd of roughly 100 people.

"And my pledge is really simple, lower costs, that's lower electric bills, lower property taxes and lower healthcare expenses, bigger paychecks, more high paying jobs in the state and better schools by bringing standards back to public education. And one of the things I've seen is that that's a message that isn't just limited to Republicans, it's resonating with voters across the state."

One of the most talked about issues at the fair, including two attendees who spoke to Fox News Digital, was property taxes and which candidate would best address that growing and often disruptive expense.

MORENO UNLOADS ON FAUCI AFTER SENATE HEARING, CALLS HIM DEMOCRATS' 'HERO' OVER PANDEMIC POLICIES

Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy told Fox News Digital about his plans to cut taxes and create jobs while criticizing Democratic rival Amy Acton's COVID-era leadership. (Fox News Digital/Andrew Mark Miller)

"The top issues that people are struggling with is number one, the property tax burden, it's gotten way too high," Ramaswamy said when asked what he’s hearing most from voters in terms of what they are most concerned about.

"We've laid out a practical plan to give the biggest property tax relief package Ohio's ever seen. Number two is the electric bills, which have gone up way too quickly. It more than doubled in many parts of the state. Producing more energy and ending load forecasting inflation, those are things that a governor actually can do. And that's something that I'm gonna lead with."

Ramaswamy added that the third issue he hears most from voters is healthcare costs and the overall cost of living.

"The number one way I'm going to be able to address that is by raising take-home pay, both by bringing more high-paying jobs to the state, but also by allowing Ohioans to keep more of what they earn by becoming a zero-income tax state, just like Texas and Florida and Tennessee, Ohio can be that state and I'm confident I'll be able to put the state on a path to get there starting next year."

RAMASWAMY: MEDICAID FRAUD RAISES HEALTHCARE COSTS FOR HARDWORKING OHIOANS

Amy Acton, former director of the Ohio Department of Health and Democratic gubernatorial candidate, meets with local residents while campaigning at Bottoms Up Coffee in Columbus, Ohio, on Monday, April 6, 2026. (Stephen Zenner/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Fauci made headlines this week after invoking the Fifth Amendment over 100 times during a Senate hearing on his handling of the coronavirus, a moment Ramaswamy told the crowd as well as Fox News Digital relates to his opponent Dr. Amy Acton’s time as director of the Ohio Department of Health from 2019 to 2020.

Ramaswamy pointed to a comment from Acton, which Fox News Digital reported on earlier this month, claiming the COVID mortality rate was at 50% when in reality it was significantly lower. Acton’s campaign responded saying she had been referring to death rates in hospitals and that she "worked to keep Ohioans safe."

"I think people look at that and say, is that somebody who has the kind of character that has the capacity to deal with data and make objective decisions and lead?" Ramaswamy explained. "And while those questions are playing out for Anthony Fauci at the national level, I think they're really resonating right here in Ohio. You could walk around and you could even see some of the signs at this fair that are protesting the decisions she made because she actually wanted Ohio to shut down county fairs while still allowing BLM protests to rage wild on the streets at the same time in the name of science. That's not objective decision-making."

CVivek Ramaswamy steps on stage at CTL Aerospace on Feb. 24, 2025, in Cincinnati, Ohio. Ramaswamy launched his Ohio gubernatorial campaign during the event. (Jon Cherry/Getty Images)

Ramaswamy is making the case that Ohioans are "rejecting that mentality" in favor of "common sense."

Polling suggests that the race between Ramaswamy and Acton will be a tight race with the Real Clear Politics average of polling showing a dead heat despite President Trump winning Ohio by commanding margins in the past three presidential election cycles, including by 12 points over former Vice President Kamala Harris in 2024.

Andrew Mark Miller is a reporter at Fox News. Find him on Twitter @andymarkmiller and email tips to AndrewMark.Miller@Fox.com.

One of Brooke Hanlon's closest friends is shedding new light on the slain New Jersey mother's young adult life in Boston as the investigation into her unsolved murder stretches into its second month.

Hanlon, a 35-year-old therapist, was found fatally stabbed inside her Chester, New Jersey home on June 6. Nearly eight weeks later, authorities have yet to name a suspect or person of interest in the homicide case.

"Honestly, it’s been confusing, heartbreaking, and incredibly frustrating," said Jennifer Payne, Hanlon's graduate school friend and former roommate, who shared photos of the pair during their time in Boston and the years following.

"I’m already someone who struggles with 'not knowing' and wanting all the information as much as possible," Payne added. "So the near total silence leaves your mind racing to fill in the blanks."

Meanwhile, Brooke's husband, James "Conor" Hanlon—who goes by Conor—has made no public statements regarding the killing of his wife and mother to their 12-month-old baby girl.

title: MIKE DAVIS: After SCOTUS fumbles birthright citizenship, we need sensible census solutions
excerpt:
Vice President JD Vance assesses the Supreme Court’s ruling on birthright citizenship, the rise of socialist candidates within the Democratic Party and more on ‘The Ingraham Angle.’

The Supreme Court...
body_text:
Vice President JD Vance assesses the Supreme Court’s ruling on birthright citizenship, the rise of socialist candidates within the Democratic Party and more on ‘The Ingraham Angle.’

The Supreme Court just punched America in the gut. In Trump v. Barbara, five justices stole We The People’s most crucial sovereign power of deciding who becomes fellow citizens by illegally constitutionalizing birthright citizenship for the children of Chinese birth tourists, Islamic terrorists, and other illegal immigrants who hate America. That's bad enough. But the rot goes deeper: illegal aliens and temporary visa holders are counted in the census – the process that determines how many U.S. House seats each state gets. That drives the Electoral College, which decides the presidency. This is a rigged game, and it has to end in time for the 2030 census.

Here's how the Fourteenth Amendment actually works: Section 1 grants birthright citizenship to anyone born in the United States and "subject to the jurisdiction thereof" -- a provision enacted after the Civil War for the children of the freed slaves, not so Chinese babies born in America can return to Beijing for the rest of their lives, mail in their votes, and even later run for U.S. president. Section 2 apportions House seats based on "the whole number of persons" in each state. The government has made a mess of both.

Pro and anti-Trump demonstrators rally outside the U.S. Supreme Court, before justices hear oral arguments on whether President Donald Trump can deny citizenship to children born to parents who are in the United States illegally or temporarily, on Capitol Hill, in Washington, Wednesday, April 1, 2026. (J. Scott Applewhite/AP Photo)

Foreign diplomats and invading soldiers are excluded from both citizenship and the census; that much makes sense. But illegal aliens have been counted in the census since Jimmy Carter's administration, and the Barbara decision now pretends these Chinese and other foreign children simply born here are full American citizens. Temporary visa holders – students and workers – are counted too, and their kids get citizenship under Barbara as well. Meanwhile, birth tourists aren't counted in the census, but their children are now citizens. So a woman who flies in for a week to watch a World Cup game, gives birth, and flies home has produced an American citizen, but she herself isn't a "person" for census purposes.

'IT'S INSANE': GOP SENATOR SAYS SUPREME COURT BIRTHRIGHT RULING HANDS CHINA A CITIZENSHIP LOOPHOLE

The current system is a constitutional embarrassment, thanks to five Supreme Court justices – Chief Justice John Roberts, Professor Amy Coney Barrett, and the three liberal women – who put their vanity over our sovereignty. Why does a Chinese birth tourist's child qualify under the more restrictive citizenship standard, while the mother doesn't qualify under the less restrictive census standard? Why do visa holders count as census "persons" while tourists don't, even though both came here legally—unlike illegal aliens, who count for everything?

This incoherent reasoning will lead to devastating outcomes.

BIRTH TOURISM CRACKDOWN EXPANDS AS HOUSE CHAIRMAN RAISES CRIMINAL CONSPIRACY CASE

Congress has the fix. The Equal Representation Act limits census counts to American citizens and lawful permanent residents. That definition tracks the correct reading of "subject to the jurisdiction thereof" from United States v. Wong Kim Ark (1898) and aligns Sections 1 and 2 of the Fourteenth Amendment. "Persons" in Section 2 means inhabitants, or individuals lawfully and permanently domiciled here. Illegal aliens and visa holders don't qualify. The Supreme Court signaled as much in Franklin v. Massachusetts (1992), noting that the Framers understood "persons" to mean permanent inhabitants even when the text didn't use that word explicitly.

President Trump could act by executive order, but Congress must act by statute to lock in this understanding. Trump's term ends in January 2029. That means the next president will oversee the 2030 census. If that president is a leftist, then Trump’s executive orders will get reversed overnight. Legislation doesn't. Pass the Equal Representation Act, get Trump's signature, and dare the Supreme Court to overturn it. In doing so, we will at least partially correct the Court’s catastrophic error in Barbara – where the Supreme Court woefully handed out American citizenship to Chinese birth tourists like cotton candy at a foreign carnival.

The briefcase of a census taker is seen as she knocks on the door of a residence, Aug. 11, 2020, in Winter Park, Fla. Eleven small cities in Illinois and Iowa are the only municipalities so far to have signed agreements with the U.S. Census Bureau for a second count of their residents in 2024, the first year the special censuses can be conducted, in a repeat of what happened during the 2020 census. (AP Photo/John Raoux, File)

The Census Bureau is also long overdue for a cleanup. In 2020, Democrats netted roughly half a dozen House seats and Electoral College votes through what was, at minimum, staggering incompetence. Trump v. Slaughter confirmed the president can remove executive branch officials wielding executive authority. That power extends to the Census Bureau's chief operating officer, who runs more of the operation than the director.

HOUSE PANEL DEMANDS CLASSIFIED BRIEFINGS ON NONCITIZEN VOTING, ALLEGED CHINESE ELECTION INTERFERENCE

The stakes go beyond politics. The census drives federal Medicaid funding to states. That means illegal aliens and visa holders don't just influence who controls Congress. They determine how much money flows to needy Americans. That’s ludicrous, and sanctuary states exploit it deliberately. The Framers and ratifiers of the Fourteenth Amendment never imagined illegal immigration, birth tourism, or temporary visa schemes at this scale. We The People, the sovereign citizens of America, certainly never consented to any of this.

And consider the national-security dimension. China, our primary geopolitical enemy, has sent 1.5 million Chinese birth tourists to the United States. Their Chinese children are now citizens under Barbara. China could flood this country with workers and students on visas, pad the census count, and manufacture political representation in Congress — all without firing a shot. Not to mention, again, these Chinese kids can mail in their votes in American elections from Beijing and even run for president of the United States. China has already run a years-long election interference campaign against this country, as detailed in materials President Trump recently declassified. We are handing our enemies a lever to pull inside our own republic.

Benjamin Franklin said that we have a republic if we can keep it. Even with five narcissists in robes on the Supreme Court who put themselves over our sovereignty, national security, and country, Congress can and must pass the Equal Representation Act. The Supreme Court must uphold it. The alternative is a census permanently distorted by hostile foreigners who have no lawful claim to shape the course of American democracy.

Keeping the republic means fixing our census. Now.

Michael R. Davis is the founder and president of the Article III Project.

title: Caitlin Clark kept from reporters despite triple-double night as coach goes viral for women's sports comments
excerpt: Indiana Fever head coach Stephanie White addresses questions about trans athletes in women’s sports. Later, Aliyah Boston and Makayla Timpson are asked about Sophie Cunningham’s stance before the sess...
body_text:
Indiana Fever head coach Stephanie White addresses questions about trans athletes in women’s sports. Later, Aliyah Boston and Makayla Timpson are asked about Sophie Cunningham’s stance before the session is cut off as the players leave.

The WNBA's crossover of controversy with the "Save Women's Sports" movement deepened on Friday night.

Caitlin Clark was not made available to speak to reporters despite recording the fourth triple-double of her career. Her teammates that were made available fled the scene when a reporter sent by OutKick attempted to ask about Sophie Cunningham's recent stance on protecting women's sports.

And while Clark and her teammates were on the floor dominating the Portland Fire for the Fever's fifth straight win, their coach was going viral on social media for answers to questions asked by the same reporter about the women's sports debate that has gripped the W in recent weeks.

Caitlin Clark #22 and Sophie Cunningham #8 of the Indiana Fever high five during a game against the Portland Fire on July 31, 2026, at Moda Center in Portland, Ore. (NBAE via Getty Images)

During a pre-game press conference, Fever head coach Stephanie White was asked her opinion on biological males competing in women's sports.

"I don't know that I would say I'm educated enough from a scientific standpoint. I don't ever believe that exclusion is the answer. I just don't. I do think that when we think about various levels of sport, various governing bodies of sport, and things that go into that, like I said, I'm not educated enough at the different levels. I know growing up I played with the boys all the time," White answered.

The coach was then immediately asked if she would welcome a biological male in the WNBA. She did not rule it out.

FEVER COACH STEPHANIE WHITE DODGES QUESTION ON GOP LETTER ABOUT CAITLIN CLARK’S TREATMENT IN WNBA

"I don't know, when we talk about biological male and scientifically where we are, I think it's a totally different scenario. Like I said, I'm not educated enough on transgender and transitioning, to give you a smart answer. I would say though that I just don't think that exclusion is the answer, we need to have deeper and more layered conversations," she said.

She was then immediately asked if she would "be okay with them in the locker room."

Head coach Stephanie White and Caitlin Clark of the Indiana Fever meet during the second quarter against the Connecticut Sun at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, Indiana, on June 17, 2025. (Dylan Buell/Getty Images)

White did not answer that question, and took a different question asking if the topic had become a point of "frustration," for her team, but acknowledged the debate as "part of our growth edge as a league."

"There is frustration, of course, because we want to talk about basketball, and we want to continue to work on our game, and we want to continue to grow as a team. But I also understand this is part of our growth edge as a league, and we have to be able to manage, we have to be able to insulate as much as we can, and then we have to be able to lead with conversation."

It was the second game in a row in which a rally took place outside prior to tip-off in support of Cunningham. The Fever guard addressed the rallies prior to the game.

"I have honestly had nothing to do with them," Cunningham said, per The Associated Press. "I think it’s people just practicing their rights of freedom of speech and doing what other fans have been doing since the WNBA has started. And so props to them, props to everyone who is able to be competent and be bold and courageous enough to to speak their truths.

"I think at the end of the day, I come in and I do my job. I think everyone who knows me personally, they know that I’m full of love. I’m bubbly. I love the people around me. I love basketball. I love inspiring the next generation and doing that in a positive light. And so that doesn’t even cross my mind. Doesn’t cross my teammates’ minds.

"And again, I’m here to play basketball, but I’m also here to be me, and I’m not gonna like shadow that or hide or, you know, dim my light just because maybe people don’t agree with that."

Meanwhile, Clark was not made available to reporters for the second straight game. Fox News Digital has asked the Fever why Clark was not available, but has not received a response.

The reporter sent by OutKick also attempted to ask the two players who were available in the post-game press conference, Aliyah Boston and Makayla Timpson, about Cunningham's recent stance on the issue, but the question and the remainder of the press conference was abruptly cut off when he began to ask.

The Fever cut the final exchange out of the video of the conference that was uploaded to YouTube.

Boston did address a general question about the Fever facing heightened attention.

"We know that there's always going to be attention with the fever and for us it's about coming in winning games. It's for uh it's about showing up and doing what we can to continue to take steps forward in this league," Boston said. "And I think there's always going to be outside noise. Um but I think we've been professionals long enough to know that if you let that affect you, then you're not really here for the right things. And so for us, we just keep the main thing, the main thing."

White's responses drew criticism on social media from some users who support protecting women's sports, while others criticized the questioning itself.

Some critics compared White's answer to a previous controversial statement by U.S. Supreme Court Justice Kentaji Brown Jackson. During her 2022 confirmation hearings, Jackson was asked by Senator Marsha Blackburn to provide a definition for the word "woman." Jackson famously declined, responding, "No, I can't... I'm not a biologist.

Many media members, like Sarah Spain, hold Sophie Cunningham and Caitlin Clark to a different standard than other WNBA players. (Kamil Krzaczynski)

Portland Fire head coach Alex Sarama was also asked a question by that same reporter about males in women's sports during pre-game media availability, and did not give a straight answer.

"My focus is as a basketball coach. To be completely honest, I don't think I've ever had to think about that. I'm completely supportive of people from all communities, people from all walks of life, so that's my stance, completely, I'm support of everyone in the Portland community," Sarama said.

Outside the Moda Center, dozens of Cunningham supporters gathered for the second consecutive Fever road game, while counterprotesters assembled nearby, some wearing costumes.

The Portland demonstration followed Tuesday’s rally in Seattle, where supporters gathered outside Climate Pledge Arena to back Cunningham’s stance and proposed Washington ballot initiatives to protect girls’ sports.

Inside the arena, two 16-year-old girls wearing XX-XY Athletics shirts held a courtside sign reading, "Thank you Sophie for speaking up for girls." The teenagers alleged that Storm co-owner Celeste Keaton approached them, invoked their Christian faith, called them "f---ing insane" and left one of them in tears.

The Storm publicly apologized, while the WNBA fined Keaton an undisclosed amount and barred her from Seattle’s next five home games. Cunningham later praised the girls for standing up for their beliefs, promised to send them gifts and called Keaton’s alleged conduct "truly embarrassing."

A third Cunningham rally is planned for Sunday outside Target Center before the Fever face the Minnesota Lynx, in one of the higher-stakes games of the entire WNBA season.

The game will pit the league's two hottest teams as the Fever are 19-10 after their five-game winning streak, while the Lynx are riding a nine-game winning streak to the best record in the W at 24-6.

And Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve, unlike White and Sarama, has taken a more definitive stance on the debate over males in women's sports.

Reeve revealed her stance on the issue on July 17, days before Cunningham revealed hers. Reeve was asked that day about the recent Supreme Court ruling that protects state laws that ban males from women's sports.

"The attacks on trans people, the attacks that they’ve gone through… it seems like it’s got way more aggressive, it’s sort of sickening when the issues they are trying to tackle are really not issues, the number of transgender athletes they are now making laws for and creating a problem, to get elected," Reeve said.

"What I’m hopeful for is that people have gotten themselves more educated and they understand that, that’s not actually a problem… exclusion is never the answer, separate isn’t equal, and trans lives matter, so to take away something that’s so valuable that sports brings to young people in particular and what it does, as I have a youngster, encourages you to be part of a team and what it gives you in terms of teamwork, leadership, competitiveness, all the things, they have every right to that as well"

Now, Reeve will lead a marquee-matchup showdown against Cunningham, Clark and the Fever with what is expected to be the biggest Cunningham rally to date raging outside on Sunday.

Jackson Thompson is a sports reporter for Fox News Digital covering critical political and cultural issues in sports, with an investigative lens. Jackson's reporting has been cited in federal government actions related to the enforcement of Title IX, and in legacy media outlets including The New York Times, The Los Angeles Times, The Philadelphia Inquirer, The Associated Press and ESPN.com.

In 2011, the Philippines’ government promised to deliver one of the world’s most ambitious r...
body_text:
101 East investigates how the Philippines’ ambitious regreening programme is failing the nation’s forests.

In 2011, the Philippines’ government promised to deliver one of the world’s most ambitious regreening projects.

The idea was simple: pay locals to restore forests and cultivate barren land by planting and tending millions of trees.

But 15 years on, a joint investigation by 101 East and Lighthouse Reports reveals how the National Greening Program has failed to meet most of its targets.

Satellite imagery shows that instead of being protected, some forests are being destroyed, while some Indigenous communities fear losing the land their livelihoods depend on.

101 East investigates how the Philippines is failing its forests.

Margot Gibbs, lead supply chain investigator

title: Spain attacks 'selfish' response of some EU countries to Ceuta migrant crossings
excerpt:
Spanish police officers and soldiers escort a large group of migrants in Ceuta to the border to take them out of Spain

Spain has condemned the "selfish, polarising and unlawful" reaction of some EU c...
body_text:
Spanish police officers and soldiers escort a large group of migrants in Ceuta to the border to take them out of Spain

Spain has condemned the "selfish, polarising and unlawful" reaction of some EU countries to the influx of about 60,000 migrants from Morocco to Ceuta.

Officials say almost all those who reached the enclave on 30 July have returned, while Spain's Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said on Saturday that the death toll had risen to at least 67.

It comes after Italy temporarily suspended the EU's border-free Schengen arrangement with Spain, as Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called the scenes "shocking".

Finland and Denmark backed Italy's move, while Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš urged a temporary suspension of Spain's Schengen membership.

In a letter to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said he had "serious concerns" about some European governments.

He said the Spanish government had fully restored control over the border and prevented any "unauthorised onward movement towards continental Europe" in less than 48 hours.

While most had shown "support and solidarity", Sanchez said other European governments had chosen to attack Spain, "driven by prejudice, fake news, ignorance, or political interest", and pointed out that Ceuta was not part of the Schengen area.

"The European Union cannot afford this kind of selfish, polarising and unlawful reaction," he said.

The Spanish leader called for an urgent meeting with EU interior ministers to "reaffirm that the security of our external borders is a shared responsibility of all Member States".

Meanwhile, 22 of the EU's 27 countries also called for emergency talks in an open letter, citing "serious concerns" regarding the developments in Ceuta.

The nations "welcome that Spain and Morocco are cooperating closely to ensure the swift return of migrants", but said a video conference of EU interior ministers would help reach agreement on mobilising EU instruments and support for Spain to restore "effective control" of the border and prevent further uncontrolled crossings.

Watch: Tens of thousands of migrants enter Ceuta

There were chaotic scenes on Thursday in Ceuta as border controls in the North African enclave apparently broke down.

In a news conference on Saturday, Grande-Marlaska told reporters the situation in Ceuta had almost returned to normal.

"Almost all of [the migrants] have already left Ceuta," the minister said, adding that businesses had now reopened. "The situation has been almost entirely reversed."

He also said Spain had started to establish an inflatable maritime barrier to prevent further illegal migrant entry.

Spanish soldiers watch migrants sitting on the pavement before escorting them back to Morocco

But while the situation on the ground is easing, political and diplomatic fallout is rippling through Madrid and other capitals.

On Thursday, Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wrote on social media that such "uncontrolled immigration" was a threat to national security, before suspending the Schengen zone agreement with Spain for a month.

The Schengen Area is a system of open borders spanning 29 European countries that have abolished controls at their common borders.

Spain responded by summoning the Italian ambassador to Madrid, while its foreign minister said he expected "European solidarity and not partisan demagoguery".

Finland's Interior Minister Mari Rantanen said she had started preparations for restoring internal border checks "if the need arises". She also urged "all European countries" to support Meloni's move.

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen also urged the EU to "consider all options, including a suspension of Schengen co-operation".

France has tightened checks on its border with Spain and said it would increase its police presence by Saturday.

Portuguese PM Luis Montenegro said he was considering reinforcing border checks.

Von der Leyen said the images from Ceuta were "unacceptable". "We cannot allow anyone to come to our Union without abiding by our rules," she said on social media.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said he "supports Spain's intention not to allow illegal migrants onto the European continent", and demanded that Morocco "take back illegal migrants immediately".

In the US, the State Department said the incident was a direct result of Spain's migration policies. President Donald Trump called the situation a "catastrophe" and said "it looks like an invasion of a country by hundreds of thousands of people".

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez blamed trafficking gangs for the migrant surge in Ceuta

Spain has defended its handling of the migrant surge. Madrid has sent troops, more police, drones, divers and boats to Ceuta. The country has also deployed its armed forces to bolster security in another Spanish enclave, Melilla, where hundreds of crossings were also reported.

Sánchez, who has visited Ceuta after the migrant influx, said he would consider reinforcing the border with Morocco, and that Moroccan authorities were co-operating.

He blamed trafficking gangs for the migrant surge, calling the incident a "violation of Spain's territorial integrity".

"Trafficking mafias took a self-serving interpretation of a Supreme Court ruling" which "spread like wildfire", he said.

EU Commissioner Magnus Brunner said, after a phone call with Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares, that "not a single person has crossed to mainland EU".

In June, Spain's Supreme Court ruled that migrants stopped at sea while trying to reach Ceuta or Melilla could not be summarily returned to Morocco without due process.

While the surge of migrants this year is extraordinary, Ceuta has long been a focal point for migrants attempting to reach Europe. During the summer months, there is often a big push to reach Ceuta, typically organised over social media.

In 2021, about 8,000 people entered Ceuta over a matter of days, exacerbating Spain's diplomatic tensions with Morocco.

Morocco, which has been suffering from a high unemployment rate, witnessed several Gen Z anti-government protests last year, with young people demanding better opportunities and improvements to public services.

Together with Melilla, Ceuta forms the European Union's only land borders with Africa. Migrants can enter the enclave by swimming several kilometres.

Spain has a relatively friendly approach to immigration. In April, the government approved plans to give legal status to 500,000 undocumented migrants, allowing them to be formally integrated into the workforce.

At that time, the right-wing Italian prime minister had already criticised Sánchez, saying the policy would "affect its neighbours".

In June the European Parliament approved tougher migration rules that grant authorities broader powers to return irregular arrivals.

body_text:
Rescuers continue the search for six climbers still missing after an avalanche hit Pakistan’s Broad Peak, as officials identified one of the four recovered bodies as Nadhira Al Harthy, the first Omani woman to summit Mount Everest.

Pakistani authorities recovered three of the bodies on Friday in harsh weather that hampered flights by search and rescue helicopters, officials said, and identified them as Nepalese climber Pur Bahadur Gurung and American climber Sarah Mallory Geis, as well as Harthy.

The officials did not immediately identify the fourth body that was found.

The expedition comprised five Nepali climbers, the Omani and American climbers, Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, a Chinese climber identified only as Wang, and one other foreign climber, according to the Alpine Club of Pakistan.

The expedition leader was the renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja, a Nepal-born former soldier in the British army widely known as Nims Dai. He climbed the world’s 14 highest peaks in a record 189 days in 2019, an achievement featured in the Netflix documentary, 14 Peaks: Nothing is Impossible. His record was surpassed in 2023.

The climbers were swept away in an avalanche on the 8,051-metre (26,414ft) peak, the world’s 12th-highest mountain, about midday on Thursday. The area in which the search is taking place is “remote and difficult”, said Sajid Hussain, deputy director of the tourism department in Gilgit-Baltistan.

Of the world’s 14 highest peaks, eight are in Nepal, five in Pakistan and one in Tibet. Climbing experts say barely more than three dozen mountaineers have climbed all 14 peaks to date. Broad Peak is considered one of Pakistan’s most challenging climbs.

Nepal’s Gurung, known to his friends as Yukta, climbed Everest more times than anyone else from the Gurung community, with 10 successful ascents to his name, Nepal’s Online Khabar noted. He also successfully climbed 12 of the world’s 8,000-metre (26,246ft) peaks.

Yukta had also set a record by summiting Pakistan’s K2, the world’s second-highest peak, within 24 hours. He was regularly involved in rescue operations for tourists stranded in the mountains.

Oman’s Al Harthy held a master’s degree in geography and previously served as director of the Citizenship Department at Oman’s Ministry of Education, Gulf News reported. In 2019, she became the first Omani woman to reach the summit of Mount Everest, and then the first Omani to climb K2, the world’s second-highest mountain.

For the US’s Geis, it was her first try at an 8,000-metre peak in Pakistan.

Geis, 39, lived in San Antonio. She announced on social media earlier this year that she was closing her Pilates studio to take “a giant leap of faith into the unknown to see where life goes. I have a sneaking suspicion there will be lots of helmets, harnesses, and crampons involved.”

Sakhi was a guide for the company, as well as a geographer and high-altitude photographer who had climbed several of the world’s major peaks.

title: Spanish PM calls for urgent EU meeting after ‘selfish’ responses to Ceuta crisis
excerpt:
Pedro Sánchez hits out at ‘polarising and unlawful reaction’ over mass crossing into Spanish enclave in north Africa

Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has called for an urgent meeting of EU inte...
body_text:
Pedro Sánchez hits out at ‘polarising and unlawful reaction’ over mass crossing into Spanish enclave in north Africa

Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has called for an urgent meeting of EU interior ministers after what he called some member states’ “selfish, polarising and unlawful reaction” to this week’s mass border crossing into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, in north Africa.

More than 50,000 people crossed into the territory from Morocco on Thursday and Friday, with at least 67 people dying in the attempt. Some drowned, while others were crushed as they tried to cross a breakwater barrier.

Although more than 48,000 people had voluntarily returned to Morocco by 6pm on Friday, the influx triggered a political crisis for the Madrid government and led some fellow EU countries to call for Spain to be suspended from the Schengen free-movement zone.

Italy announced on Friday evening that it would suspend its Schengen arrangements with Spain, even though Ceuta – and Spain’s other north African enclave, Melilla – are subject to special Schengen rules that prevent onward movement within the zone.

Italy’s foreign minister, Antonio Tajani, blamed the situation in Ceuta on the Sánchez government’s decision to offer a now-closed scheme to regularise the status of more than 1 million undocumented migrants and asylum seekers. He said the programme had incentivised human trafficking and was “profoundly wrong”.

Tajani’s remarks prompted a sharp response from Spain’s foreign minister, José Manuel Albares, who said the comments were “unbecoming” and accused Italy of “partisan demagoguery”.

Sánchez was equally forthright in a letter sent to the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, the European Council president, António Costa, and Micheál Martin, the prime minister of Ireland, which holds the EU presidency.

In the letter, the Spanish prime minister said he had been deeply concerned by the reaction some EU governments had shown to events in Ceuta.

Sánchez said that while most had expressed support and solidarity, others had chosen to attack Spain and call for its temporary exclusion from the Schengen area.

“Such an attitude – driven by prejudice, fake news, ignorance or political interest – is … contrary to European law, humanitarian law, and the principles of solidarity that bind us together,” he said.

In a pointed rebuke to Italy, he noted that Spain was “according to Frontex, one of the least porous external borders of the European Union, with a number of irregular entries that is half that recorded, for example, in Italy in recent years (2021–2026)”.

He concluded by saying the EU could not afford “this kind of selfish, polarising and unlawful reaction” and asked for an urgent video conference of EU interior ministers to address the issue.

Senior EU officials are due to meet on Saturday in a “political crisis response team” convened by Ireland’s presidency. The meeting is designed to help member states make clear responses using expert opinion.

Ireland’s justice minister, Jim O’Callaghan, who is leading the meeting on behalf of the EU, said he had been in touch with Spain’s interior minister, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, to express his solidarity and support.

“I will remain in close contact with the Spanish government, member states and the EU institutions as the situation evolves,” he said on Friday night.

Many of the remaining people who crossed into Ceuta returned to Morocco on Saturday morning amid a reinforced Spanish police and military presence.

“We hope to go to Europe to work and earn a living – that’s it,” Souleil Boyan, a 19-year-old from Senegal, told Agence France-Presse outside a migrant centre in Ceuta where dozens of other people from sub-Saharan Africa were waiting for officials.

“We all know that in Africa there isn’t much opportunity,” he added.

The Spanish government said in a statement that the situation in Ceuta remained calm and quiet.

“Friday night passed without incident,” it said. “Entries were completely halted, while departures to Morocco continued without any notable events.”

It said containment barriers were being installed at the Tarajal beach breakwater, including a 500-metre-long inflatable barrier and a line of anchored buoys.

title: Paidwork breach exposes 23M user records
excerpt:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Making a few extra dollars online should not put your bank details or identity at risk. Yet that is the concern for pe...
body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Making a few extra dollars online should not put your bank details or identity at risk. Yet that is the concern for people who used Paidwork, an online earnings application.

A leaked database tied to the platform reportedly contains information from more than 23 million accounts. If you ever signed up, now is a good time to take the warning seriously.

CyberGuy Live: Missed "Sick of Spam?" Get the replay and checklist

Our free CyberGuy Live class "Sick of Spam?" has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our spam-stopping checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you step by step through simple ways to reduce robocalls, spam texts, junk email and unwanted messages. You’ll also learn how to curb political texts, clean up your inbox and spot messages that could put your personal information at risk.

Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

Paidwork lets people earn small amounts through online microtasks, but the reported breach shows how much personal information can sit behind those tiny payouts. (Photo by Nikolas Kokovlis/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Paidwork is a microtask platform that offers small payments for completing online activities. Those jobs can include answering surveys, testing apps and watching advertisements. You complete tasks, build a balance and eventually request a payout. For many people, the account may feel low risk because the earnings are small. However, the information behind those payments can be far more valuable.

Hackers claimed in March 2026 that they had obtained data from Paidwork. They later offered the information for sale. Nearly 11 GB of data allegedly taken from the platform appeared publicly in July. The data breach notification service Have I Been Pwned analyzed the released files and found more than 23 million unique email addresses. The service added the incident to its database on July 19, 2026.

Paidwork told CyberGuy it is actively investigating the reported breach, working with external security specialists and taking steps to protect affected accounts and notify users as appropriate.

The exposed information appears to reach far beyond email addresses. Have I Been Pwned says the files contain names, phone numbers, physical addresses and dates of birth. They also reportedly include education levels, gender information, profile photos and personal interests.

The financial records raise additional concern. The files reportedly contain bank account numbers, transaction information and payout histories. Attackers may also have device information and IP addresses. Those details can reveal how you connected to the service and which equipment you used.

Finally, the leak reportedly contains passwords stored as bcrypt hashes. Bcrypt makes passwords harder to crack than weaker storage methods. However, short or predictable passwords can still face attacks. That is a huge amount of personal information to exchange for tasks that may pay only a few cents.

WHAT A SCAMMER SEES THE MOMENT THEY GOOGLE YOUR NAME

The leaked database reportedly includes names, home addresses, bank details, transaction records and password hashes tied to more than 23 million accounts. (Photo by Ute Grabowsky/Photothek via Getty Images)

You may have earned very little through Paidwork. A criminal could still find plenty of value in your account. For example, a phishing email could mention a real payout before claiming that your bank transfer failed. Another message could include your address to make a fake security warning look convincing.

Criminals can combine several leaked details to build a believable story around you. Password reuse creates another danger. If attackers crack your Paidwork password, they can test it on other websites. This type of attack is called credential stuffing. It succeeds when people reuse one password across several accounts. Your email account should cause the greatest concern. Someone who gets inside may use it to reset passwords for other services.

Bank account numbers and transaction histories can also support convincing fraud attempts. A caller who knows your payment history may sound like a legitimate representative. Attackers do not care how much you earned. They care how much they can make from the information connected to you.

This leak should make all of us think carefully about the information we give side-income platforms. A task may pay only a few cents. Meanwhile, the service may request your legal name and bank account information before releasing your earnings.

It may also collect your birth date, home address or information about your device. That creates an uneven trade. Before joining an earning app, review what information it collects. Look for an explanation of why the company needs each detail.

Also, check whether you can delete your account after you stop using the platform. Find out whether you can remove old payout methods and profile information. Avoid completing optional profile fields that reveal extra details about your life. The company cannot lose information that you never provided. You should also think carefully before connecting your primary bank account to a service you plan to use only occasionally.

Anyone who used Paidwork should change reused passwords, watch financial accounts and stay alert for phishing messages built with stolen personal details. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)

Have I Been Pwned lists the Paidwork incident as affecting 23.3 million accounts. You can search the email address you used for the platform through its breach-checking tool.

A match means your email address appears in the released files. However, the public search will not display every exposed detail connected to you. You should still secure your accounts when a search produces no match. Public breach databases may contain incomplete records.

Also, make sure you visit the real Have I Been Pwned website. Criminals often create fake breach-checking pages to collect more personal information. Never enter a password, Social Security number or banking information into a breach-search tool.

Start with your login credentials and financial accounts. Then reduce the amount of personal information criminals can find elsewhere.

To see if your email was affected, visit Have I Been Pwned at haveibeenpwned.com . It is the first and official source for this newly added dataset. Enter your email address to find out if your information appears in the Synthient leak. When done, come back here for Step 2.

Change the password connected to your Paidwork account, even if you no longer use the platform. Create a completely new password. Avoid adding a symbol or number to your old password because criminals often test common variations. Next, change that password on every other account where you reused it. Also, immediately replace an exposed password anywhere you used it.

A password manager can create and store a different password for each account. That limits the damage from one exposed login. You also avoid relying on short passwords that are easier to remember and crack. Protect the password manager with a strong master password. Then enable multifactor authentication for the password manager itself.

Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) anywhere the option appears. Start with your email account. Then protect your bank, payment services and other important accounts. An authenticator app or security key usually provides stronger protection than a text message. However, any second verification step can improve your security.

Contact any bank or payment service you connected to Paidwork. Explain that your account information may appear in a leaked database. Ask whether the institution recommends extra monitoring or a replacement account number. Next, turn on alerts for withdrawals and transfers. You should also receive a warning when someone changes your account information. Report any transaction that you do not recognize. Do not ignore a small charge because criminals sometimes use minor transactions to test an account.

A credit freeze can help stop someone from opening a new credit account in your name. You need to place the freeze separately with Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. A freeze costs nothing to place or remove. You do not need to wait for evidence of identity theft. The FTC says a credit freeze can help after your personal information appears in a data breach. Remember that a credit freeze cannot prevent fraud involving an account you already have. Continue watching your existing bank and credit card statements.

Be suspicious of emails, texts or calls that mention Paidwork, a payout or a bank transfer. A criminal may know your full name or address. That knowledge does not prove the message came from a legitimate company. Avoid clicking links in unexpected messages. Open the official app or type the company's address into your browser instead. Never share a verification code with someone who contacts you. Criminals often request those codes while trying to enter your account. Phishing links can steal information or install malware on your device.

Strong antivirus software can warn you about malicious links, infected attachments and fake websites. This protection becomes especially useful after a breach. Criminals often send fake security alerts that pressure you to download a file or visit a login page. Keep your security software updated so it can recognize newer threats. However, antivirus protection cannot catch every convincing scam. Continue checking the sender and web address before clicking anything. The FTC recommends using security software to protect your devices from malware and other online threats. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com.

The Paidwork files reportedly contain information that may also appear on people-search websites. A data removal service can send opt-out requests to data brokers that collect and sell personal information. Reducing those records may make it harder for criminals to expand a leaked profile. You can also submit the removal requests yourself for free. However, you may need to contact many sites and repeat the process when your information returns. A data removal service cannot erase the Paidwork files from criminal forums. It also cannot remove government records or every old listing from the internet. The FTC says people-search sites usually provide an opt-out process. It also notes that paid services can complete requests on your behalf. Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com.

A platform may pay you a few cents while storing information that can affect your life for years. The Paidwork files reportedly combine personal profiles with banking information and password hashes. That gives criminals several ways to target you, even when your Paidwork balance was nearly empty. Paidwork says it has no confirmed evidence its systems or accounts were compromised. However, Have I Been Pwned found more than 23 million unique email addresses in the publicly released files. Treat the warning seriously if you ever used the platform. Change reused passwords first. Then secure your financial accounts and watch for messages that know a little too much about you.

How much personal information should a side-hustle platform be allowed to collect for a few dollars in return? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com
